ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r11.speaker: أبو السمال وأبو السميفع
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r11.claim: The passage attributes variants to Abū al-Sammāl al-ʿAdawī and al-Ghanawī, and to Abū al-Sumayfa, who reads “هو خير وأعظم” with both words nominative.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال باللام العدوي وأبو السمال بالكاف الغنوي وأبو السميفع هو خير وأعظم برفعهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r12.speaker: أبو زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r12.claim: Abū Zayd says Banū Tamīm raise the words after a separator, construing the phrase as a new nominal sentence whose subject and predicate form the second object.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r12.anchor: قال أبو زيد هي لغة بني تميم يرفعون ما بعد الفاصلة يقولون كان زيد هو الفاعل بالرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r13.claim: The cited verse by Qays ibn Dhurayḥ illustrates the Banū Tamīm use of a nominative phrase after a separator.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114/r13.anchor: وعليه قول قيس بن ذريح تحن إلي لبنى وأنت تركتها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r1.claim: Seek forgiveness in every state, since people rarely avoid shortcomings relative to their own standing.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r1.anchor: واستغفروا الله في كافة أحوالكم فإن الإنسان قلما يخلو مما يعد تفريطا بالنسبة إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r2.speaker: الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r2.claim: The Sufis count a worshipper’s awareness of or regard for their own worship as a shortcoming.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r2.anchor: وعد من ذلك الصوفية رؤية العابد عبادته

ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r3.claim: It is suggested that this is why the command to seek forgiveness follows the commands to pray, give zakat, and lend God a good loan.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r3.anchor: قيل ولهذه الإشارة أمر بالاستغفار بعد الأوامر السابقة بإقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة والإقراض الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r4.claim: Omitting the object of “forgiving” and “merciful” indicates that the forgiveness and mercy extend generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p114#2/r4.anchor: وفي حذف المعمول دلالة على العموم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r7.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r7.claim: ʿĀʾishah says the Prophet's character was the Qurʾān and night vigil was obligatory for him and companions for a year until their feet swelled; revelation then made it voluntary.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r7.anchor: عن زرارة بن أبي أوفى عن سعيد بن هشام قال: انطلقت إلى عائشة رضي الله عنها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r10.claim: Adnā means less than two-thirds of the night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r10.anchor: إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى} أقل من {ثلثي الليل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r11.speaker: أهل مكة والكوفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r11.claim: Mecca and Kufa readers use accusative naṣfahu wa-thuluthahu, coordinating with an implied verb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r11.anchor: قرأ أهل مكة والكوفة: "نصفه وثلثه" بنصب الفاء والثاء وإشباع الهاءين ضما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r12.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r12.claim: Other readers use the genitive, coordinate with thuluthayi, and pronounce final hāʾs with kasrah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بجر الفاء والثاء وإشباع الهاءين كسرا عطفا على ثلثي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r13.claim: The group with the Prophet means believers who kept vigil with him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r13.anchor: وطائفة من الذين معك} يعني المؤمنين وكانوا يقومون معه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r14.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r14.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says God does not miss what they do and knows night, day, and their vigil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r14.anchor: قال عطاء: يريد لا يفوته علم ما تفعلون، أي أنه يعلم مقادير الليل والنهار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r15.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they stood until their feet swelled and could not endure or measure the vigil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r15.anchor: قال الحسن: قاموا حتى انتفخت أقدامهم، فنزل: "علم أن لن تحصوه"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r16.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r16.claim: Muqātil says some prayed all night for fear of missing the required amount; they could not know its measure.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r16.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كان الرجل يصلي الليل كله، مخافة أن لا يصيب ما أمر به من القيام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r17.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r17.claim: God returned to them with pardon and relief.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r18.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r18.claim: Recite what is manageable in prayer; al-Ḥasan specifies Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r18.anchor: {فاقرءوا ما تيسر من القرآن} يعني في الصلاة، قال الحسن: يعني في صلاة المغرب والعشاء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r19.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r19.speaker: قيس بن أبي حازم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r19.claim: Qays says Ibn ʿAbbās recited al-Fātiḥah and one verse of al-Baqarah in each rakʿah, then cited this command.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p256#2/r19.anchor: قال قيس بن أبي حازم: صليت خلف ابن عباس بالبصرة فقرأ في أول ركعة بالحمد وأول آية من البقرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r1.claim: The sick are among those unable to keep night vigil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى وآخرون يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r2.claim: These are people traveling for trade and seeking God's provision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r2.anchor: يعني المسافرين للتجارة يطلبون من رزق الله {وآخرون يقاتلون في سبيل الله}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r3.claim: Those fighting in God's path also cannot keep night vigil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r3.anchor: وآخرون يقاتلون في سبيل الله} لا يطيقون قيام الليل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r4.claim: Ibrāhīm reports Ibn Masʿūd saying a patient trader supplying a Muslim city and selling at the day's price has the rank of martyrs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r4.anchor: روى إبراهيم عن ابن مسعود قال: أيما رجل جلب شيئا إلى مدينة من مدائن المسلمين صابرا محتسبا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r5.claim: This means whatever amount of Qurʾān is manageable for you.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r5.anchor: {فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه} أي [ما تيسر عليكم]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r6.claim: Commentators say this allowance belonged to early Islam and was abrogated by the five prayers, as indicated by establishing prayer, giving zakat, and offering a goodly loan.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r6.anchor: كان هذا في صدر الإسلام ثم نسخ بالصلوات الخمس، وذلك قوله:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the loan means charity beyond obligatory zakat, including kinship ties and hosting guests.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ما سوى الزكاة من صلة الرحم، وقرى الضيف.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r8.claim: Good sent ahead earns better afterlife reward than what is given and greater than what is postponed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r8.anchor: تجدوا ثوابه في الآخرة أفضل مما أعطيتم {وأعظم أجرا} من الذي أخرتم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r9.claim: Khayran and aʿẓama are second objects since wujūd meaning seeing takes two; Basrans call huwa a separator, Kufans a support without iʿrāb position.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r9.anchor: ونصب "خيرا وأعظم" على المفعول الثاني، فإن الوجود إذا كان بمعنى الرؤية يتعدى إلى مفعولين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r10.speaker: عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r10.claim: The Prophet says one's wealth is what one sends ahead, while an heir's is what one leaves behind.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p258/r10.anchor: عن الحارث بن سويد قال: قال عبد الله: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "أيكم ماله أحب إليه من مال وارثه"؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p259/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p259/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p259/r1.claim: Ask God to forgive sins; He is forgiving and merciful.

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r1.claim: Adnā is used metaphorically for less, since what is nearer to a thing is less distant from it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r1.anchor: استعار الأدنى للأقل لأن الأقرب إلى الشيء أقل بعدا منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r2.speaker: ابن كثير والكوفيون
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr and the Kūfans read naṣfahu and thuluthahu in the accusative, coordinated with adnā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير والكوفيون { ونصفه وثلثه } بالنصب عطفا على { أدنى }

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r3.claim: A group of the Prophet's companions also performed the night vigil.

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r4.claim: Only God knows the exact measures of night and day; placing God's name first signals exclusivity, supported by the statement that people cannot enumerate it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r4.anchor: لا يعلم مقادير ساعاتهما كما هي إلا الله تعالى، فإن تقديم اسمه مبتدأ مبنيا عليه { يقدر } يشعر بالاختصاص

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r5.claim: People cannot calculate the time intervals or keep precise count of the hours.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r5.anchor: أي لن تحصوا تقدير الأوقات ولن تستطيعوا ضبط الساعات

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r6.claim: God grants concession to leave the prescribed amount of night vigil and lifts the liability for doing so.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r6.anchor: بالترخص في ترك القيام المقدر ورفع التبعة فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r7.claim: It may mean perform whatever night prayer is easy, with Qurʾān naming prayer by one of its pillars; another view says the phrase means recite the Qurʾān itself as easily as possible.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r7.anchor: فصلوا ما تيسر عليكم من صلاة الليل، عبر عن الصلاة بالقرآن كما عبر عنها بسائر أركانها

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r8.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r8.claim: One reported account says the earlier option made night vigil obligatory, this verse abrogated that obligation when it became difficult, and the five daily prayers later abrogated this ruling.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r8.anchor: قيل كان التهجد واجبا على التخيير المذكور فعسر عليهم القيام به

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r9.claim: This is a new explanation of the ruling, giving a further reason for its concession; the ruling is repeated in light of it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r9.anchor: استئناف يبين حكمه أخرى مقتضية الترخيص والتخفيف ولذلك كرر الحكم مرتبا عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r10.claim: Those traveling to seek God's bounty are traveling for trade and for acquiring knowledge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r10.anchor: والضرب في الأرض ابتغاء للفضل المسافرة للتجارة وتحصيل العلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r11.claim: The phrase refers to people fighting in God's path.

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r12.claim: The command is to perform the obligatory prayer.

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r13.claim: The command is to pay the obligatory alms.

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r14.claim: The good loan means other charitable spending, or paying zakāt in the best manner; the promise of return encourages it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r14.anchor: يريد به الأمر في سائر الانفاقات في سبل الخيرات، أو بأداء الزكاة على أحسن وجه

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r15.claim: What is advanced is better and more rewarding than what is deferred to a bequest at death, or than worldly goods.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r15.anchor: من الذي تؤخرونه إلى الوصية عند الموت أو من متاع الدنيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r16.claim: Khayran is a second object of tajidūhu and either an intensifier or separator, since afʿal min is definite-like and resists the article; a reading has huwa khayrun as a nominal clause.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r16.anchor: و { خيرا } ثاني مفعولي { تجدوه } وهو تأكيد أو فصل

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r17.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r17.claim: Seek God's forgiveness in all circumstances because no person is free of shortcomings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:20/r17.anchor: في مجامع أحوالكم فإن الإنسان لا يخلو من تفريط

BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r3.claim: The sūra closes with seeking forgiveness for the disbelievers' earlier resistance and for what obedient believers fail to fulfill, as 73:20 indicates.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r3.anchor: ثم ختم السورة بالاستغفار من كل ما تقدم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r1.claim: The verse teaches moderation in worship to spare people hardship, since life is the opportunity to gather good before death.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r1.anchor: أشار سبحانه وتعالى إلى الاقتصاد تخفيفا لما يلحق الإنسان من النصب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r2.claim: The soul belongs to the subtle, instantly created world of command, while the dense body belongs to the gradual world of creation; the soul is therefore alien to bodily attachments.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r2.anchor: فإن الروح في غاية اللطافة ، والجسد في غاية الكثافة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r3.claim: Remembrance, prayer, and good works help the soul reconnect with its elevated spiritual realm; wisdom means justice and moderation in words and deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r3.anchor: وذلك بصرف القلب كله عن هذه الدنايا والتلبس بالأذكار والصلوات وجميع الأعمال الصالحات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r4.claim: Adnā means less in duration here; nearness and lower rank both imply a shorter distance, explaining the word's shared senses.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r4.anchor: لأن كلا منهما يلزم منه قلة المسافة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r5.claim: On the general reading, the Prophet stood for less than two-thirds on some nights and less than the half and third on others.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r5.anchor: أدنى من كل منهما في بعض الليالي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r6.speaker: ابن كثير والكوفيون
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir and the Kufan readers put half and third in the accusative, specifying the amounts included under less than two-thirds.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r6.anchor: المعنى على قراءة ابن كثير والكوفيين بالنصب تعيين النصف والثلث الداخل تحت الأدنى من الثلثين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r7.claim: Both readings match the earlier choice to pray a full half, less than a half (a third), more than a half (two-thirds), or an even smaller portion (a quarter).
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r7.anchor: وهو على القراءتين مطابق لما وقع التخيير فيه في أول السورة بين قيام النصف بتمامه أو الناقص منه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r8.claim: A ṭāʾifah is a group whose members are suited to gathering around the Prophet and turning toward one another.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r8.anchor: أي يقوم كذلك جماعة يفيها أهليبة التحلق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r9.claim: Those with the Prophet are his companions in words and deeds, meaning Muslims; the broader phrase avoids implying that those who did not pray were not Muslims.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p215/r9.anchor: وكأنه اختار هذا دون أن يقول من المسلمين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r1.claim: God alone measures night and day with exact precision and knows every minute because He created them; the verse recalls 67:14.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r2.claim: God knew people could neither calculate the night's measure precisely nor sustain the prescribed practice.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r3.claim: The Prophet said, “Be upright, and you will not encompass it,” cited to illustrate human inability to calculate fully.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r3.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ' استقيموا ولن تحصوا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r4.claim: God lifted the earlier obligation of precisely measured night vigil and licensed people to leave it without blame.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r5.claim: Calling the relief repentance does not imply a prior sin; the heavy obligation could have led people into sin.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r5.anchor: وكأنه سماه توبة وإن لم يكن ثم معصية إشارة إلى أنه من شأنه لثقله أن يجر إلى المعصية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r6.claim: Recitation stands for prayer because it is prayer's greatest pillar, indicating that night vigil is recommended rather than obligatory.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r6.anchor: معبرًا عن الصلاة بالقراءة لأنها أعظم أركانها إشارة إلى أن التهجد مستحب لا واجب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r7.claim: Recite whatever is easy from the Qur'an, in or outside prayer and by night or day.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r7.anchor: أي يفي الصلاة أمو غيرها في الليل والنهار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r8.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r8.claim: Al-Qushayri says the easy recitation may be five verses or more.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r8.anchor: قال القشيري : من خمس آيات إلى ما زاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r9.speaker: قيل
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r9.claim: An unnamed view sets the easy minimum at ten verses or more.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r9.anchor: ويقال : من عشر آيات إلى ما يزيد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r10.speaker: قيس بن أبي حازم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r10.claim: Qays ibn Abi Hazim reports praying behind Ibn Abbas, who recited al-Fatihah and one verse of al-Baqarah in each of the first two units.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r10.anchor: قال قيس بن أبي حازم : صليت خلف ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالبصرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r11.speaker: قيل
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r11.claim: Another view takes the command as bare recitation in place of the former night-prayer obligation, as an added easing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r11.anchor: وقيل : إنه أمر بالقراءة مجردة إقامة لها مقام ما كان يجب عليهم من الصلاة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r12.claim: The Prophet said that praying with ten verses removes heedlessness, one hundred marks devotion, and one thousand brings the rank of the richly rewarded; Abu Dawud, Ibn Khuzaymah, and Ibn Hibban transmit it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r12.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r13.speaker: المنذري
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r13.claim: Al-Mundhiri says the thousand verses begin at Surat al-Mulk and continue to the end of the Qur'an.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p216/r13.anchor: قال المنذري : من سورة الملك إلى آخر القرآن ألف آية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r1.claim: God spells out why the former night-prayer measure was eased: illness, travel, and fighting make exact observance difficult.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r1.anchor: فسر ذلك العلم المجمل بعلم مفصل بيانا لحكمة أخرى للنسخ

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r2.claim: Since the surah is among the earliest revelations, it foretells that the Muslim community will grow greatly.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r2.anchor: وهذه السورة من أول ما أنزل عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r3.claim: Illness is mentioned first as the broadest excuse and one over which the sick person has no control.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r3.anchor: ذكر عذر المريض وبه أنه لكونه أعم ولا قدرة للمريض على دفعه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r4.claim: Travelers are described as striking the earth because a diligent walker strikes it with his foot.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r4.anchor: لأن الماشي بجد واجتهاد يضرب الأرض برجله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r5.claim: Travel for trade follows illness as another common reason that prevents exact night observance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r5.anchor: أتبعه السفر للتجارة لأنه يليه في العموم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r6.claim: Seeking God's bounty includes pursuing profit in trade or acquiring knowledge; God's provision exceeds people's hopes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r6.anchor: من الربح في التجارة أو تعلم العلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r7.claim: Fighting in God's way means attacking God's enemies; the repeated phrase exalts jihad and avoids confusion with a return to commerce.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r7.anchor: وأظهر ولم يضمر تعظيما للجهاد ولئلا يلبس بالعود إلى المتجر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r8.claim: The phrase places the fighting within God's path and removes moral and physical obstacles that block that path.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r8.anchor: ذلك القتل مظروف لطريق الملك الأعظم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r9.claim: Al-Baghawi transmits Ibn Masud's view that a patient trader who imports goods to a Muslim city and sells at that day's price is ranked with martyrs.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r9.anchor: روى إبراهيم عن ابن مسعود رضي اله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r10.claim: Ibn Umar says that, after martyrdom, he would prefer to die traveling and seeking God's bounty.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r10.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : ما خلق الله موتة أموتها بعد القتل في سبيل الله أحب إلي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r11.claim: These additional excuses explain why God repeats the permission: each person should recite whatever is easy from the same Qur'an.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r12.claim: The required vigil became an easy portion of recitation and was later superseded by the five obligatory prayers.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p217/r12.anchor: فصار الواجب قيام شيء من على وجه التيسير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r1.claim: The explicit command to establish prayer either favors understanding the prior recitation as independent of formal prayer or specifies that it meant prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r1.anchor: قال ترجيحا لإرادة هذا الثاني أو تنصيصا على إرادة الأول

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r2.claim: Establish the obligatory prayer with all its pillars, conditions, preliminaries, complements, forms, and refinements.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r2.anchor: الكتوبة بجيمع الأمور التي تقوم بها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r3.claim: Give the required zakat from the good wealth God has bestowed; it is the financial pillar alongside prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r3.anchor: من طيب أموالكم التي أنعمنا بها عليكم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r4.claim: The goodly loan includes voluntary acts of charity and worship with body and wealth, offered eagerly and beautifully while healthy and prosperous; God preserves and multiplies it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r4.anchor: من نوافل الخيرات كلها في جميع شرعه برغبة تامة وعلى هيئة جميلة في ابتدائه وانتهائه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r5.claim: The general command covers every good deed, bodily or financial, sent ahead for the afterlife when people can no longer act; God preserves it for them.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r6.claim: A separator may occur between the indefinite terms because the comparative form afʿal min functions like a definite expression and does not take the definite article.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r6.anchor: وجاز وقوع الفصل بين غير معرفتين لأن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r7.claim: Every good deed is repaid, whether done near death or earlier and whether by believer or disbeliever; sincere deeds are rewarded in the afterlife, others in this life.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r7.anchor: سواء كان عند الموت أو في الحياة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r8.claim: The promised reward exceeds that of a bequest made during terminal illness, whose recompense might come in worldly life.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r8.anchor: أي مما لمن أوصى في مرض الموت

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r9.claim: End deeds by seeking forgiveness: even praised worship can produce self-admiration, and no one can render God His due, so servants must acknowledge shortcomings.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r10.claim: God's forgiveness covers sins and their effects until no blame or punishment remains; His mercy then adds generous honor and favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r10.anchor: أي بالغ الستر لأعيان الذنوب وآثارها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r11.claim: The surah explains the Prophet's comprehensive supplication: make religion, worldly life, and afterlife good; make life increase good and death relief from evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r11.anchor: اللهم أصلح لي ديني الذي هو عصمة أمري وأصلح لي دنياي التي فيها معاشي وأصلح لي آخرتي التي إليها منقلبي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r12.claim: The surah's ending returns to its opening: encouragement to act and its reward recall the command to stand before God, while seeking forgiveness stresses the greatness of His station.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p218/r12.anchor: رجع آخر السورة - بالترغيب في العمل وذكر جزائه - على أولها

DURR-FULL:v5p549/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r1.claim: Ali reports that after the command to keep night vigil the Prophet prayed all night until his feet swelled; Gabriel told him to put his feet on the ground, and this verse and the easing command in 73:20 followed.
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r1.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: لما نزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم (يا أيها المزمل قم الليل إلا قليلا)

DURR-FULL:v8p321/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r9.claim: Qatada glosses the durations as less than two thirds, less than half, and less than a third of the night.
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r9.anchor: وفي قوله: {إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم} الآية قال: أدنى من ثلثي الليل وأدنى من نصفه وأدنى من ثلثه

DURR-FULL:v8p321/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r10.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r10.claim: Al-Hasan and Saʿid ibn Jubayr explain that you would not be able to sustain or measure it.
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r10.anchor: عن الحسن وسعيد بن جبير {علم أن لن تحصوه} قال: لن تطيقوه

DURR-FULL:v8p321/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r11.claim: Mujahid says the command to recite what is easy eased night prayer; inability to reckon it refers to sustaining the night vigil, and God then disclosed believers' qualities.
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد {فاقرؤوا ما تيسر منه} قال: أرخص عليهم في القيام {علم أن لن تحصوه} قال: أن لن تحصوا قيام الليل

DURR-FULL:v8p321/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r12.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r12.claim: Qatada says night vigil was initially obligatory; Companions stood until their feet swelled. After a year this passage abrogated that duty, while prayer and zakat remained obligatory without concession.
DURR-FULL:v8p321/r12.anchor: عن قتادة قال: فرض قيام الليل في أول هذه السورة فقام أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى انتفخت أقدامهم

DURR-FULL:v8p322/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r2.claim: Ikrima says they continued for a year, suffering hardship and swollen feet, until the end of the sūra abrogated the initial night-vigil command.
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة {يا أيها المزمل قم الليل} الآية قال: لبثوا بذلك سنة فشق عليهم وتورمت أقدامهم

DURR-FULL:v8p322/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet glosses what is easy to recite as one hundred verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم {فاقرؤوا ما تيسر منه} قال: مائة آية

DURR-FULL:v8p322/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r4.speaker: قيس بن أبي حازم
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r4.claim: Qays recounts Ibn Abbas reciting al-Fatiha and the opening verse of al-Baqara in one rakʿa, then citing this verse as authority for the amount recited.
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r4.anchor: عن قيس بن أبي حازم قال: صليت خلف ابن عباس فقرأ في أول ركعة بالحمد لله وأول آية من البقرة

DURR-FULL:v8p322/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r5.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that the Prophet ordered them to recite al-Fatiha and whatever else was easy.
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال: أمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن نقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب وما تيسر

DURR-FULL:v8p322/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r6.claim: Umar says that, after jihad, he would prefer to die while travelling with his saddle bags seeking God's bounty, then recites the verse about travel and fighting.
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r6.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: ما من حال يأتيني عليه الموت بعد الجهاد في سبيل الله أحب إلي من أن يأتيني

DURR-FULL:v8p322/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports the Prophet saying that a food merchant supplying a Muslim town and selling at the day's market price has the standing of a martyr with God.
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما من جالب يجلب طعاما إلى بلد من بلاد المسلمين

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3381#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3381#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3381#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits from the Prophet that reciting what is feasible here means one hundred verses.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3381#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاقرؤا ما تيسر منه قال : مائة آية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the majority considered the sura Makkan except 73:20 to its end; al-Qurtubi attributes the same view to al-Thaʿlabi.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية : هي في قول الجمهور مكية إلا قوله تعالى : { إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r3.speaker: صاحب الإتقان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r3.claim: The Itqan author cites al-Hakim from ʿAʾisha: the ending was revealed a year after the opening, when night vigil had been imposed before the five prayers, implying the whole sura was Makkan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r3.anchor: وقال في ( الإتقان ) : إن استثناء قوله : { إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r5.claim: ʿAʾisha's report says the ending followed the opening by a year; al-Tabari also reports this timing from Ibn ʿAbbas, while the majority place the ending in Medina years later.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r5.anchor: فقالت عائشة : نزل بعد صدر السورة بسنة ، ومثله روى الطبري عن ابن عباس ، وقال الجمهور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r6.claim: The author prefers a Medinan date for 73:20 onward because it mentions fighting in God's path, unless this predicts the unseen miraculously.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r6.anchor: فالظاهر أن الأصح أن نزول { إن ربك يعلم إلى آخر السورة نزل بالمدينة لقوله تعالى : وءاخرون يقاتلون في سبيل الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that the Prophet and a group of companions prayed at night for ten years after 73:1; 73:20 through “establish prayer” then came after ten years, hence in Medina if his Meccan stay lasted ten years.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r7.anchor: وروى الطبري عن سعيد بن جبير ( قال : لما أنزل الله على نبيئه صلى الله عليه وسلم { يا أيها المزمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r1.claim: Some of ʿAʾisha's reports imply the entire sura is Makkan and its ending came a year after its opening, before obligatory prayer, as transmitted by al-Hakim via the Itqan author.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r1.anchor: فبعضها يقتضي أن السورة كلها مكية وأن صدرها نزل قبل آخرها بسنة قبل فرض الصلاة وهو ما رواه الحاكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r3.claim: That account implies a wholly Medinan sura: ʿAʾisha lived with the Prophet in Medina, and his angry exit suggests he left his home for its adjoining mosque; other reports support mosque prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r3.anchor: ولأن قولها : ( فخرج مغضبا ) يقتضي أنه خرج من بيته المفضي إلى مسجده ، ويؤيده أخبار تثبت قيام الليل في مسجده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r4.claim: The inconsistent narratives may have confused the initial imposition of night vigil with later encouragement to perform it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r4.anchor: ولعل سبب هذا الاضطراب اختلاط في الروايات بين فرض قيام الليل وبين الترغيب فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r6.claim: The opening certainly came in Mecca, while 73:20 to the end came in Medina years later and abrogated the Prophet's duty; ʿAʾisha's claim that vigil preceded the five prayers is anomalous.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r6.anchor: فالذي نعتمد عليه أن أول السورة نزل بمكة لا محالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r9.claim: Night prayer is established as recommended for Muslims; scholars disagree whether its obligation continued for the Prophet, a question the author says need not be pursued.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r9.anchor: على أنه لا خلاف في رفع فرض القيام عن المسلمين . وتقرر أنه مندوب فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r4.claim: The discussion from this point concerns the portion of the sura revealed in Medina, as stated in the introduction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r4.anchor: من هنا يبتدىء ما نزل من هذه السورة بالمدينة كما تقدم ذكره في أول السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r5.claim: The verse shows the Prophet and some companions already prayed at night under the opening command; its “He relented toward you” marks relief for all and abrogates that earlier command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r5.anchor: وصريح هذه الآية ينادي على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقوم من الليل قبل نزول الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r6.claim: Early authorities differed over when and where this verse was revealed and how its ruling relates to the preceding verse; the trusted view is that the opening was Makkan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r6.anchor: واختلف السلف في وقت نزولها ومكانه وفي نسبة مقتضاها من مقتضى الآية التي قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r7.claim: The author rejects al-Tabari's report from Abu Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman from ʿAʾisha, and the similar report from al-Nakhaʿi about the blanket, as evidence that the opening was Medinan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r7.anchor: ولا يغتر بما رواه الطبري عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن عائشة مما يوهم أن صدر السورة نزل بالمدينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r8.claim: The first command obligated night prayer for the Prophet alone; companions in Mecca followed his example. ʿAʾisha thought the five prayers abrogated a duty on Muslims, but the author calls that an interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r8.anchor: في أن القيام الذي شرع في صدر السورة كان قياما واجبا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r9.claim: The first obligation on the community was the five prayers imposed on the Night Journey; if an earlier communal prayer existed, the Miʿraj account would mention its replacement, and the five were equally obligatory on the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r9.anchor: ولو كان لجرى ذكر تعويضه بالصلوات الخمس في حديث المعراج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says only 73:20 abrogated the night vigil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r10.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس لأنه قال : إن قيام الليل لم ينسخه إلا آية : { إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r11.claim: The five prayers did not abrogate the Prophet's night vigil; rather, “recite what is easy” removed the requirement to spend half the night or slightly less.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r11.anchor: ولا أن يختلف في أن فرض الصلوات الخمس لم ينسخ فرض القيام على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سوى أنه نسخ استيعاب نصف الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas recounts staying with his aunt Maymuna: the Prophet awoke around midnight, performed ablutions, prayed thirteen rakʿas, then slept until the dawn caller; Ibn ʿAbbas was a boy, dating it to about 7 or 8 AH.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r1.anchor: وقد بين ذلك حديث ابن عباس ليلة بات في بيت خالته ميمونة أم المؤمنين قال فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r2.claim: The only reported group prayer with the Prophet occurred in Medina during Ramadan after he reserved mosque space; companions joined, then he stayed away one night, saying he feared it might be made obligatory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r2.anchor: إلا حين احتجز موضعا من المسجد لقيامه في ليالي رمضان فتسامع أصحابه به فجعلوا ينسلون إلى المسجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r3.claim: This shows the companions' joint night prayer was not obligatory and did not continue; if any vigil were mandatory for Muslims, praying with the Prophet would fulfill it and there would be no fear of a new duty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r3.anchor: وهو صريح في أن القيام الذي قاموه مع الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يكن فرضا عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet told Hafsa that ʿAbd Allah was righteous and would be better if he prayed at night.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r4.anchor: وقد عضد ذلك حديث ابن عمر ( أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لحفصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r5.claim: The opening praises the Prophet's faithful, earnest fulfillment of the command: he regularly prayed the prescribed half night or slightly less, and went as far as nearly two-thirds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r5.anchor: وافتتاح الكلام ب { إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم } يشعر بالثناء عليه لوفائه بحق القيام الذي أمر به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r6.claim: His near-two-thirds vigil represents the utmost limit, as with resolute messengers; the Prophet compared Moses's completion of the term to choosing the longer ten-year period in 28:29.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r6.anchor: بل أخذ بالأقصى وذلك ما يقرب من ثلثي الليل كما هو شأن أولي العزم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r7.claim: A hadith says the Prophet prayed at night until his feet swelled.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p279/r7.anchor: وقد جاء في الحديث : ( أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقوم من الليل حتى تورمت قدماه )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r1.claim: The emphatic إن marks the statement as important and indirectly expresses that God approves the Prophet’s night vigil, preparing for the later easing as mercy and honor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r1.anchor: وهو كناية عن أنه أرضى ربه بذلك وتوطئة للتخفيف الذي سيذكر في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r2.claim: After the Hijra, the Prophet’s duties in governing, defending Medina, and preparing armies left less daytime leisure than in Mecca, explaining the easing of obligatory and recommended night prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r2.anchor: ما كان له فيه أيام مقامه بمكة ، فظهرت حكمة الله في التخفيف عن رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r3.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet divided his home time among God, family, and himself, then devoted his own share to people, meeting their needs and guiding them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r3.anchor: حديث علي بن أبي طالب ( أنه سئل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أوى إلى منزله فقال : كان إذا أوى إلى منزله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r4.claim: The imperfect يعلم suggests continuing, renewed knowledge and thereby signals that the Prophet’s conduct is pleasing to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r4.anchor: وإيثار المضارع في قوله : { يعلم } للدلالة على استمرار ذلك العلم وتجدده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r5.claim: By contrast, يعلم in 33:18 occurs in a reproach: God has continually known the obstructors’ conduct, and no part of it is hidden from Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r5.anchor: وفي ضده قوله : { قد يعلم الله المعوقين منكم } ( الأحزاب : 18 ) لأنه في معرض التوبيخ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r6.claim: أدنى literally means nearer, from دنو; it is metaphorically used for less because the distance to the nearest thing is small, just as farther can denote more.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r6.anchor: و { أدنى } أصله أقرب ، من الدنو ، استعير للأقل لأن المسافة التي بين الشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r7.claim: أدنى is an adverbial accusative with تقوم: the Prophet stands for a period shorter than two thirds, meaning more than half, as 73:4 indicates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r7.anchor: وهو منصوب على الظرفية لفعل { تقوم } ، أي تقوم في زمان يقدر أقل من ثلثي الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r8.claim: The majority read ثلثي with a vowelled lām, its original form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p280/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { ثلثي } بضم اللام على الأصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r1.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر ويعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r1.claim: These readers put ونصفه وثلثه in the genitive, coordinating them with ثلثي الليل: the vigil is for less than half or less than a third.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r1.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر ويعقوب { ونصفه وثلثه } بخفضهما عطفا على

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r2.claim: These readers put ونصفه وثلثه in the accusative as objects of تقوم, describing standing for two thirds, half, or a third, without going below half or a third.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف بنصب { ونصفه وثلثه } على أنهما منصوبان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r3.claim: The readings describe different nightly patterns as nights and days vary in length; all fit the choice granted in 73:2–4, so the intended meaning does not change.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r3.anchor: وهذه أحوال مختلفة في قيام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالليل تابعة لاختلاف أحوال الليالي والأيام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r4.claim: The parenthetical statement that God measures night and day fits here because He knows all the possible durations and has made them known; readings therefore do not alter the point.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r4.anchor: وبه تظهر مناسبة تعقيب هذه الجملة بالجملة المعترضة ، وهي جملة { والله يقدر الليل والنهار }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects al-Farrāʾ’s assertion that the accusative reading is closer to correct, since the readings preserve the same intended meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r5.anchor: فمن العجاب قول الفراء أن النصب أشبه بالصواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r6.claim: طائفة is nominative, coordinated with إن’s noun after its predicate; this is permitted by treating it as a new clause, as in 9:3.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r6.anchor: و { طائفة } عطف على اسم { إن } بالرفع وهو وجه جائز إذا كان بعد ذكر خبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r7.claim: The construction subtly marks the different status and measure of the Prophet’s vigil and the group’s; 9:3 likewise distinguishes God’s disavowal from the Messenger’s public dealings with polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r7.anchor: فإن بين قيام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقيام الطائفة التي معه تفاوتا في الحكم والمقدار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r8.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r8.claim: Aisha reports in Sahih al-Bukhari that people joined the Prophet’s mosque prayer on successive Ramadan nights, growing in number; he stayed away later for fear the prayer would be made obligatory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p281/r8.anchor: ففي حديث عائشة في ( صحيح البخاري ) ( أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى ذات ليلة في المسجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r1.claim: If معك means figurative association, fellowship, and agreement rather than physical attendance at night prayer, the group includes several Companions and Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, whose night-prayer reports occur separately in Sahih al-Bukhari.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r1.anchor: وإن كانت المعية معية مجازية وهي الانتساب والصحبة والموافقة فقد عددنا منهم : عبد الله بن مسعود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r2.claim: The verse’s opening praises the Prophet for faithfully fulfilling the night vigil and praises the group who followed him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r2.anchor: واعلم أن صدر هذه الآية إيماء إلى الثناء على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في وفائه بقيام الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r3.claim: God’s knowledge that the Prophet stands is an indirect expression of divine approval of their practice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r3.anchor: فالخبر بأن الله يعلم أنك تقوم مراد به الكناية عن الرضى عنهم فيما فعلوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r4.claim: The opening statement prepares for the ensuing explanation that they cannot keep the vigil’s full measure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r4.anchor: والمقصود : التمهيد لقوله : { علم أن لن تحصوه } إلى آخر الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r5.claim: The verb علم is repeated rather than coordinated with وأن سيكون to mark this as a distinct consideration in the easing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r5.anchor: أعيد فعل { علم } في جملة { علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى } الخ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r6.claim: والله يقدر الليل والنهار is a parenthesis between God’s knowledge of the vigil and the statement that they cannot fully measure it; its relevance was explained above.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r6.anchor: وجملة { والله يقدر الليل والنهار } معترضة بين جملتي { إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r7.claim: The clause may be a second predicate of إن after the vigil clause, or an explanatory resumption answering the listener’s expectation; after commending them, God eases their burden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r7.anchor: أن تكون خبرا ثانيا عن { إن } بعد الخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r8.claim: The object pronoun in تحصوه refers to the night standing understood from أنك تقوم.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r9.claim: إحصاء literally means counting, from حصى because pebbles were used to count; here it metaphorically means being able to sustain the many acts of bowing, prostration, and recitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r9.anchor: والإحصاء حقيقته : معرفة عدد شيء معدود مشتق من اسم الحصى جمع حصاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r10.speaker: الحسن وسفيان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r10.claim: Al-Hasan and Sufyan explain إحصاء here as ability to manage the many actions of night prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r10.anchor: وبهذا فسر الحسن وسفيان ، ومنه قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r11.claim: The cited hadith says to be steadfast, since full steadfastness cannot be attained; take on as much as one can bear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r11.anchor: في الحديث استقيموا ولن تحصوا أي ولن تطيقوا تمام الاستقامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r12.claim: أن is the lightened form of الثقيلة, with an omitted pronoun of شأن and a sentential predicate; the negative particle separates it from its verbal predicate in standard usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p282/r12.anchor: أن } مخففة من الثقيلة ، واسمها ضمير شأن محذوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r1.claim: أن and its clause fill both object positions of علم; the sense is that He knew their inability to keep count would in fact occur.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r2.claim: تاب is metaphorical for withholding blame before a lapse occurs: anticipated shortfall resembles an actual sin, so language of repentance describes the lifting of liability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r2.anchor: وفعل { تاب } مستعار لعدم المؤاخذة قبل حصول التقصير لأن التقصير متوقع فشابه الحاصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r3.claim: The address from تحصوه onward targets Muslims who kept night vigil, either by a shift from third to second person or by a general expression narrowed by context; the Prophet himself could count, while illness and other duties are mentioned.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r3.anchor: والوجه أن يكون الخطاب في قوله : { تحصوه } وما بعده موجها إلى المسلمين الذين كانوا يقومون الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r4.claim: فاقرؤوا ما تيسر من القرآن means perform as much prayer as is manageable, since prayer necessarily includes recitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r4.anchor: فصلوا ما تيسر لكم ، ولما كانت الصلاة لا تخلو عن قراءة القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r5.claim: Calling prayer Qurʾān, as in 17:78’s قرآن الفجر for the dawn prayer, concisely encourages both night worship and recitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r5.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { وقرآن الفجر } ( الإسراء : 78 ) أي صلاة الفجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r6.claim: The Quran meant here is what had been revealed before this Medinan verse: all the Meccan Quran and some Medinan revelation; it differs from the earlier command to recite with measured cadence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p283/r6.anchor: والمراد القرآن الذي كان نزل قبل هذه الآية المدنية وهو شيء كثير من القرآن المكي كله وشيء من المدني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r1.claim: The phrase concerns as much night prayer as manageable, not the minimum Quranic recitation required in prayer; even if read as recitation, the amount is unspecified here and clarified by the hadith requiring al-Fātiḥa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r1.anchor: فلا دلالة في هذه الآية على مقدار ما يجزىء من القراءة في الصلاة إذ ليس سياقها في هذا المهيع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r2.claim: The cited Prophetic hadith states that prayer is not valid for one who does not recite the Opening of the Book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r2.anchor: وقد بينه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r3.speaker: جمهور الفقهاء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r3.claim: The majority of jurists require a surah in addition to al-Fātiḥa and consider reciting only part of a surah in obligatory prayer disliked; partial recitation is allowed in night prayer, Ramadan vigil, and necessity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r3.anchor: وهو الواجب عند جمهور الفقهاء ، فيكره أن يقرأ المصلي بعض سورة في الفريضة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r4.claim: A report in the Ṣaḥīḥ says the Prophet became hoarse while reciting and bowed in the middle of a surah, illustrating an exception for night prayer or need.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r4.anchor: ففي ( الصحيح ) ( أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ فأخذته بحة فركع )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأحمد في رواية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa and one report from Ahmad hold that even a short single verse suffices and al-Fātiḥa is not specifically required; they cite 55:64 as an example, while Abu Hanifa’s two companions disagree on both points.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r5.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأحمد في رواية عنه : تجزىء قراءة آية من القرآن ولو كانت قصيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r6.speaker: صاحبا أبي حنيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa’s two companions disagree with him on both whether one short verse suffices and whether al-Fātiḥa is required.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r7.claim: The detailed rules specifying when an imam, follower, or person praying alone must recite are treated in legal manuals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r7.anchor: وتعيين من تجب عليه القراءة من منفرد وإمام ومأموم مبين في كتب الفقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r8.claim: When تاب means accepting repentance, it takes على by implication of مِن; when it means turning away from and regretting sin, it takes a preposition suited to that sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r8.anchor: إذا أريد به قبول توبة التائب عدي بحرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r9.claim: This verse abrogates the set duration of night vigil—half the night or more or less than a third—leaving its amount unmeasured; the vigil’s remaining legal status was explained earlier.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r9.anchor: وقد نسخت هذه الآية تحديد مدة قيام الليل بنصفه أو أزيد أو أقل من ثلثه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r10.claim: The clause about illness and other circumstances is an elaboration of the inability to keep the measure, and gives another easing for additional conditions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r10.anchor: هذه الجملة بدل اشتمال من جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r11.claim: The first broad category of reasons for easing is impaired health, represented by the mention of the sick.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r11.anchor: أعذار اختلال الصحة وقد شملها قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r12.claim: The second category is livelihood work—trade, crafts, farming, and similar necessities—summarized as traveling in search of God’s provision.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p284/r12.anchor: الأشغال التي تدعو إليها ضرورة العيش من تجارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r1.claim: The third category is work for the community: fighting, frontier watch and garrison duty, army management, and sending envoys or ambassadors to spread Islam; it includes the Prophet’s fighting and illness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r1.anchor: الضرب الثالث : أعمال لمصالح الأمة وأشار إليها قوله : { وآخرون يقاتلون في سبيل الله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r2.claim: A hadith reports that the Prophet fell ill and missed the night vigil for one or two nights.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r2.anchor: اشتكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يقم ليلة أو ليلتين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r3.claim: If this verse was revealed in Mecca, it foretells the Muslims’ coming independence and ability against their enemies; if Medinan, it excuses the raids and campaigns they had begun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r3.anchor: وإذا كانت هذه الآية مما نزل بمكة ففيها بشارة بأن أمر المسلمين صائر إلى استقلال وقترة على أعدائهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r4.claim: Some Companions infer the virtue of trade and travel from God’s placing lawful earners alongside fighters; these two reasons honor such activities, while other excused needs resemble illness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r4.anchor: وقد كان بعض الصحابة يتأول من هذه الآية فضيلة التجارة والسفر للتجر حيث سوى الله بين المجاهدين والمكتسبين المال الحلال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud says that one who brings goods to a Muslim city seeking God’s approval and sells them at the day’s price has a standing with God like the martyrs; he cites this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r5.anchor: روي عن ابن مسعود أنه قال ( أيما رجل جلب شيئا إلى مدينة من مدائن المسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that after death in God’s path, he would prefer to die between his travel packs while journeying in search of God’s bounty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عمر : ( ما خلق الله موتة بعد الموت في سبيل الله أحب إلي من أن أموت بين شعبتي رحلي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r7.claim: يضربون في الأرض means traveling across the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r7.anchor: ومعنى { يضربون في الأرض } يسيرون في الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r8.claim: The root image is one body striking another; travel is called striking the earth because يضربون incorporates walking, while the striking sense fades and في marks earth as the place traversed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p285/r8.anchor: وحقيقة الضرب : قرع جسم بجسم آخر ، وسمي السير في الأرض ضربا في الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r1.claim: Seeking God’s bounty means seeking provision; 2:198 uses the expression for trade during the Hajj period.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r1.anchor: والابتغاء من فضل الله طلب الرزق قال تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r2.claim: Here traveling for God’s bounty means business travel: journeys often occupy both night and day, requiring travelers to sleep by day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r2.anchor: فقوله تعالى : { يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله } مراد بالضرب في الأرض فيه السفر للتجارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r3.claim: The pronoun in منه refers to the Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r3.anchor: وفرع عليه مثل ما فرع على الذي قبله فقال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r4.claim: The measure of night prayer is entrusted to what is manageable for all Muslims despite their differing excuses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r4.anchor: وقد نيط مقدار القيام بالتيسير على جميع المسلمين وإن اختلفت الأعذار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r5.claim: The verse either lifts night prayer’s obligation if it had previously been obligatory, or clarifies that it was never obligatory and that Muslims’ voluntary imitation of the Prophet was not binding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية اقتضت رفع وجوب قيام الليل عن المسلمين إن كان قد وجب عليهم من قبل على أحد الاحتمالين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r6.claim: Night prayer was not made obligatory, or its obligation was lifted, because widespread excuses make it burdensome; a general presumption of hardship can remove obligation where individuals otherwise might receive only temporary exemptions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r6.anchor: وعلل عدم وجوبه عليهم بأن الأمة يكثر فيها أصحاب الأعذار التي يشق معها قيام الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r7.claim: This is a rule based on the general likelihood of hardship: like travel prayer remaining two rakʿahs because travel usually brings hardship, according to ʿĀʾisha’s report.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r7.anchor: فتبين أن هذا تعليل الحكم الشرعي بالمظنة والحكم هنا عدمي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r8.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r8.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that prayer was first prescribed as two rakʿahs, then three prayers were lengthened at home while travel prayer remained two.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r8.anchor: على قول عائشة أم المؤمنين : ( إن الصلاة فرضت ركعتين ثم زيد في ثلاث من الصلوات في الحضر وأبقيت صلاة السفر )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r9.claim: The concession was warranted because night prayer is not one of Islam’s pillars, so its religious benefit was not weighty enough to require it universally.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r9.anchor: وأوجب الترخص في قيام الليل أنه لم يكن ركنا من أركان الإسلام فلم تكن المصلحة الدينية قوية فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r10.claim: Night prayer remains governed by the earlier command in 73:2 and the Sunnah’s encouragement of it; Ibn ʿĀshūr says he explained this already.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r10.anchor: وأما حكم القيام فهو ما دل عليه قوله : { قم الليل إلا قليلا } ( المزمل : 2 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r11.claim: The verse grounds legal reasoning from a broadly likely condition and supports general concessions for hardship common to most people, such as advance-payment sale, rather than isolated personal cases.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p286/r11.anchor: فهذه الآية صالحة لأن تكون أصلا للتعليل بالمظنة وصالحة لأن تكون أصلا تقاس عليه الرخص العامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r1.claim: The command to establish prayer reminds believers to guard the obligatory prayers and not neglect them, as stated in 4:103.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r1.anchor: تذكير بأن الصلوات الواجبة هي التي تحرصون على إقامتها وعدم التفريط فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r2.claim: The juxtaposition suggests that the five obligatory prayers discharge believers’ duty, while night prayer is voluntary and greatly beneficial; many transmitted reports support this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r2.anchor: إيماء إلى أن في الصلوات الخمس ما يرفع التبعة عن المؤمنين وأن قيام الليل نافلة لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r3.claim: Prayer and zakah are commonly paired in revelation; Abu Bakr inferred that zakah refusal warrants fighting, telling ʿUmar he would fight anyone who separated them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r3.anchor: حتى استنبط أبو بكر رضي الله عنه من ذلك أن مانع الزكاة يقاتل عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r4.claim: Abu Bakr told ʿUmar that he would fight anyone who distinguished between prayer and zakah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r4.anchor: فقال لعمر رضي الله عنه ( لأقاتلن من فرق بين الصلاة والزكاة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r5.claim: Lending to God means voluntary charity; giving to the poor is likened to a loan because God promises a generous return in the reward of the Last Day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r5.anchor: وإقراض الله هو الصدقات غير الواجبة ، شبه إعطاء الصدقة للفقير بقرض يقرضه الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r6.claim: A good loan is charity given solely for God’s sake and free of reminders or injury; goodness varies by degree and by the qualities valued in each kind of charity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r6.anchor: ووصف القرض بالحسن يفيد الصدقة المراد بها وجه الله تعالى والسالمة من المن والأذى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r7.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr links this expression to the earlier parallels in 2:245 and 64:17, where lending God a good loan is promised multiplied reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r7.anchor: وقد تقدم في سورة البقرة قوله : { من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فيضاعفه له ضعافا كثيرة وفي سورة التغابن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r8.claim: This closing statement summarizes prior commands and gives an omitted command: do good; whatever good you send ahead for yourselves, you will find with God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p287/r8.anchor: وفي الكلام إيجاز حذف . تقدير المحذوف : وافعلوا الخير وما تقدموا لأنفسكم منه تجدوه عند الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r1.claim: The waw may coordinate this command with the preceding statement, making it a concluding exhortation to repair lapses in commanded good, including repentance for neglected obligations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الواو للعطف فيكون معطوفا على جملة { وما تقدموا لأنفسكم } الخ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r2.anchor: و { ما } شرطية . ومعنى تقديم الخير : فعله في الحياة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r3.claim: Doing good in worldly life for its afterlife reward is pictured as a traveler sending ahead luggage, tools, and family to the destination so they are ready on arrival.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r3.anchor: شبه فعل الخير في مدة الحياة لرجاء الانتفاع بثوابه في الحياة الآخرة بتقديم العازم على السفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r4.claim: من خير explains the otherwise indefinite ما.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r4.anchor: و { من خير } بيان لإبهام { ما } الشرطية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r5.claim: Good is what religion identifies as praiseworthy and promises to reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r5.anchor: والخير : هو ما وصفه الدين بالحسن ووعد على فعله بالثواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r6.claim: تجدوه means finding the deed’s reward and recompense; scripture often names compensation by the thing for which it is given.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r6.anchor: ومعنى { تجدوه } تجدوا جزاءه وثوابه ، وهو الذي قصده فاعله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r7.claim: A Prophetic hadith says a person who hoards wealth without paying its due will meet a bald snake on Judgment Day saying, I am your wealth, your treasure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r7.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الذي يكنز المال ولا يؤدي حقه ( مثل له يوم القيامة شجاعا أقرع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r8.claim: The pronoun in تجدوه is the first object of تجدوا and خيرا is its second object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r8.anchor: وضمير الغائب في { تجدوه } هو المفعول الأول ل ( تجدوا ) ومفعوله الثاني { خيرا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r9.claim: The intervening pronoun is a separating pronoun even before an indefinite; this is allowed because أفعل من كذا resembles a definite noun, which cannot take the definite article.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r9.anchor: والضمير المنفصل الذي بينهما ضمير فعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r10.claim: خير is a comparative: the reward found is better than what was sent ahead, meaning the deed’s recompense is multiplied, as 64:17 promises.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r10.anchor: و { خيرا } : اسم تفضيل ، أي خيرا مما تقدمونه إذ ليس المراد أنكم تجدونه من جنس الخير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r11.claim: The separating pronoun here intensifies certainty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r11.anchor: وأفاد ضمير الفصل هنا مجرد التأكيد لتحقيقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r12.claim: وأعظم أجرا either coordinates with خيرا, extending the separating pronoun’s emphasis, or independently carries that emphasis; أجرا is an accusative specification of أعظم.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p288/r12.anchor: وعطف { وأعظم أجرا } على { خيرا } أو هو منسحب عليه تأكيد ضمير الفصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r1.claim: The waw begins an explanatory resumption: after easing night prayer, God directs believers to seek forgiveness in the night’s late hours as another devotional practice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الواو للاستئناف وتكون الجملة استئنافا بيانيا ناشئا عن الترخيص في ترك بعض القيام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r2.claim: Late-night forgiveness seeking accords with 51:18 and with two Prophetic reports about the last third of the night and waking from sleep.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r2.anchor: وهو مشمول لقوله تعالى : { وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون } ( الذاريات : 18 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r3.claim: The Prophet reports that each night, in its final third, God calls for people to pray, ask, or seek forgiveness, promising response, giving, and forgiveness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r3.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ينزل ربنا كل ليلة إلى سماء الدنيا حين يبقى ثلث الليل الآخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r4.claim: The Prophet says that one who wakes at night, recites the stated remembrance, and then asks forgiveness or supplicates will have the request answered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r4.anchor: وقال : ( من تعار من الليل فقال : لا إلاه إلا الله وحده لا شريك له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r5.claim: God’s great forgiveness and mercy explain the command to seek forgiveness and encourage it as likely to be answered; the intensive descriptions hint at that promise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p289/r5.anchor: وجملة { إن الله غفور رحيم } تعليل للأمر بالاستغفار ، أي لأن الله كثير المغفرة شديد الرحمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r7.claim: Variant readings are especially relevant to tafsir because one reading can clarify its counterpart or yield an additional meaning; different readings often expand a single verse’s meanings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r7.anchor: وهي من هذه الجهة لها مزيد تعلق بالتفسير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r8.claim: He considers it likely that revelation came in both or more forms, if all well-known readings are accepted as transmitted from the Prophet, so the readings multiply meanings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r8.anchor: والظن أن الوحي نزل بالوجهين وأكثر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r9.claim: Alternatively, Quranic wording may intentionally accommodate several readings, each adding meanings like multiple verses; he compares this to inclusion, double entendre, and implications of composition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r9.anchor: على أنه لا مانع من أن يكون مجيء ألفاظ القرآن على ما يحتمل تلك الوجوه مرادا لله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r13.claim: An exegete should explain the mutawatir readings because their differences usually expand the verse’s meanings, with multiple readings functioning like multiple Quranic words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r13.anchor: وأنا أرى أن على المفسر أن يبين اختلاف القراءات المتواترة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r15.speaker: العلماء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r15.claim: Scholars address the difficulty in the seven-ahruf hadith through two approaches: some regard it as abrogated, others as still operative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p55/r15.anchor: وللعلماء في معناه أقوال يرجع إلى اعتبارين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r4.claim: The later verse 73:20 relieved the worshippers of the night-prayer burden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r4.anchor: فنزلت: إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم [المزمل: 20] فخفف عنهم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r4.claim: The verse was revealed to ease the continued night vigil, whether that practice had been obligatory or recommended, as discussed earlier.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r4.anchor: نزلت تخفيفا لما كان استمر استعماله من قيام الليل إما على الوجوب أو على الندب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r5.claim: God knows the Prophet and his community vary in how much they stand, sometimes approaching two-thirds, sometimes less than a third, because people cannot measure time accurately without sleep; only God measures night and day truly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r5.anchor: أن الله تعالى يعلم أنك تقوم أنت وغيرك من أمتك قياما مختلفا فيه، مرة يكثر ومرة يقل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r6.claim: God turned them from the burden and directed them to recite whatever is manageable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r6.anchor: أي رجع بهم من الثقل إلى الجنة وأمرهم بقراءة ما تيسر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r7.speaker: الفراء ومنذر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r7.claim: Al-Farra and Mundhir gloss تحصوه as تحفظوه, meaning to retain or keep count of it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r7.anchor: ونحو هذا يعطي عبارة الفراء ومنذر فإنهما قالا تحصوه تحفظوه
