IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r8.claim: They read ونصفه وثلث in the genitive, coordinated with الثلثين; on this reading لن تحصوه concerns keeping count of the time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r8.anchor: وهي قراءة أبي عمرو ونافع وابن عامر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r9.speaker: باقي السبعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r9.claim: The remaining readers among the Seven read ونصفه وثلثه in the accusative, coordinated with أدنى, yielding a different interpretation of لن تحصوه.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r9.anchor: وأما من قرأ «ونصفه وثلثه» بالنصب عطفا على أدنى وهي قراءة باقي السبعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r10.claim: With the accusative reading, the commanded fractions already show that people can estimate time; the inability must mean they cannot sustain so much difficult night prayer, and God eases it out of grace.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r10.anchor: لم يبق إلا أن يكون قوله لن تحصوه لن تستطيعوا قيامه لكثرته وشدته فخفف الله عنكم فضلا منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r11.speaker: الحسن وابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r11.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Jubayr explain تحصوه as تطيعوه, meaning to obey it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r11.anchor: ونحو هذا تعطي عبارة الحسن وابن جبير تحصوه تطيعوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r12.speaker: جمهور القراء والناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r12.claim: Most readers pronounce the lām in وثلثه with a damma.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390/r12.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء والناس «وثلثه» بضم اللام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r1.claim: The majority hold that reciting as much of the Qur'an as is manageable is permission.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r1.anchor: فاقرؤا ما تيسر من القرآن إباحة، هذا قول الجمهور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r2.speaker: ابن جبير وجماعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jubayr and a group treat the recitation as obligatory, requiring at least fifty verses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جبير وجماعة هو فرض لا بد منه ولو خمسين آية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r3.speaker: الحسن وابن سيرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin say night prayer is obligatory even if only the time needed to milk a sheep; al-Hasan adds that one who recites one hundred verses will not be opposed by the Qur'an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن وابن سيرين قيام الليل فرض، ولو قدر حلب شاة، إلا أن الحسن قال: من قرأ مائة آية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r4.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r4.claim: Some scholars regard the two rak'ahs after the evening prayer together with witr as satisfying this command; extra prayer brings extra reward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم: والركعتان بعد العتمة مع الوتر مدخلتان في حكم امتثال هذا الأمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r5.claim: Here أن is a reduced form of the emphatic particle; the implied wording is أنه يكون, with the sīn compensating for the omitted element, as in Abu Mihjan's line.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r5.anchor: علم أن مخففة من الثقيلة. والتقدير أنه يكون، فجاءت السين عوضا من المحذوف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r6.speaker: أبو محجن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r6.claim: The poet's phrase أن لا أذوقها illustrates the compensating لا construction cited by the author.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r6.anchor: ولا تدفنني بالفلاة فإنني ... أخاف إذا ما مت أن لا أذوقها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r7.claim: ضرب في الأرض means traveling for trade, whereas ضرب الأرض can mean walking to relieve oneself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r7.anchor: والضرب في الأرض: هو السفر للتجارة، وضرب الأرض هو المشي للتبرز والغائط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r8.claim: Illness, trade travel, and fighting are human impediments to night prayer, so God eased the vigil on their account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r8.anchor: فذكر الله تعالى أعذار بني آدم التي هي حائلة بينهم وبين قيام الليل وهي المرض والسفر في تجارة أو غزو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r9.claim: The verse commends travel for trade and the marketplace alongside travel for jihad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r9.anchor: وفي هذه الآية فضيلة الضرب في الأرض بل تجارة وسوق لها مع سفر الجهاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r10.claim: Ibn Umar says that after martyrdom he most loves to die between the two sides of his saddle while traveling to seek God's bounty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r10.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمر: أحب الموت إلي بعد القتل في سبيل الله أن أموت بين شعبتي رحلي أضرب في الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r11.claim: The command to recite what is manageable is repeated for emphasis.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r12.claim: Prayer and zakat here are the prescribed obligatory duties.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r13.speaker: من قال إن القيام بالليل غير واجب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r13.claim: Those who deny an obligation of night prayer take the passage to mean: take what is manageable from the burden and preserve the obligatory prayers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r13.anchor: ومن قال إن القيام بالليل غير واجب قال معنى الآية خذوا من هذا الثقل بما تيسر وحافظوا على فرائضكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r14.speaker: من قال إن شيئا من القيام واجب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r14.claim: Those who hold some night prayer obligatory say it is paired with the prescribed duties because it too is obligatory.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r14.anchor: قال: قرنه الله بالفرائض لأنه فرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r15.claim: Lending to God means advancing one's good deeds for Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r15.anchor: وإقراض الله تعالى: هو إسلاف العمل الصالح عنده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r16.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r16.claim: The majority read هو خيرا, treating هو as a pronoun of separation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r16.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «هو خيرا» على أن يكون هو فصلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r17.speaker: محمد بن السميفع وأبو السمال
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r17.claim: They read هو خير in the nominative: هو is the subject and خير its predicate, and the clause supplies the second object of تجدوه.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r17.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن السميفع وأبو السمال «هو خير» بالرفع على أن يكون هو ابتداء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r18.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r18.claim: Some scholars derive seeking forgiveness after prayer from this verse and from 51:17.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r18.anchor: فالاستغفار بعد الصلاة مستنبط من هذه الآية ومن قوله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r19.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r19.claim: Ibn Kathir, in Shibl's transmission, reads وثلثه with a still lām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p390#2/r19.anchor: «وثلثه» بسكون اللام. وقوله تعالى: فاقرؤا ما تيسر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r1.claim: The author says his father used to seek forgiveness three times immediately after salām at every obligatory prayer, transmitting a hadith for the practice.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r1.anchor: وعهدت أبي رحمه الله يستغفر إثر كل مكتوبة ثلاثا بعقب السلام ويأثر في ذلك حديثا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r2.claim: Post-prayer forgiveness can address shortcomings and thoughts that slipped away during the prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r2.anchor: فكأن هذا الاستغفار من التقصير وتفلت الفكر أثناء الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r3.speaker: السلف الصالح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r3.claim: The early pious Muslims prayed until dawn, then sat seeking forgiveness until the dawn prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p391/r3.anchor: وكان السلف الصالح يصلون إلى طلوع الفجر ثم يجلسون للاستغفار إلى صلاة الصبح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r1.claim: The Prophet presents the Qur’an as salvation amid dark tribulations: it recounts past peoples, reports what is to come, judges between people, guides, and never tires scholars or the devout.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r1.anchor: قيل: فما النجاة منها يا رسول الله؟ قال: كتاب الله تعالى، فيه نبأ من قبلكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r2.claim: Anas identifies the Qur’an as the firm handhold mentioned in the cited verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r2.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك في تفسير قوله تعالى: فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r3.claim: The Prophet says that whoever seeks knowledge of earlier and later peoples should deeply explore the Qur’an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r3.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من أراد علم الأولين والآخرين فليثور القرآن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r4.claim: The Prophet says each Qur’anic letter earns ten good deeds, and alif, lam, and mim count as separate letters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r4.anchor: وقال عليه السلام: «اتلوا هذا القرآن، فإن الله يأجركم بالحرف منه عشر حسنات، أما إني لا أقول «الم» حرف، ولكن الألف حرف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r5.claim: In his final sermon while ill, the Prophet leaves the Qur’an and his family as two weighty trusts, urging adherence to the Qur’an’s rulings and respect for his family.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r5.anchor: وروي عنه عليه السلام أنه قال في آخر خطبة خطبها وهو مريض: «أيها الناس إني تارك فيكم الثقلين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r6.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r6.claim: Ja‘far explains that the Qur’an never grows tedious because each generation receives it as fresh, and reflection yields fresh knowledge at every reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r6.anchor: وقيل لجعفر بن محمد الصادق: لم صار الشعر والخطب يمل ما أعيد منها، والقرآن لا يمل؟ فقال: لأن القرآن حجة على أهل الدهر الثاني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r7.speaker: محمد بن سعيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Sa‘id says Qur’anic stories are repeated so that everyone who reads an accessible portion may gain admonition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36/r7.anchor: وقيل لمحمد بن سعيد: ما هذا الترديد للقصص في القرآن؟ فقال: ليكون لمن قرأ ما تيسر منه حظ في الاعتبار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r1.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r1.claim: One reported view locates the Qur’an’s challenge in the pre-eternal speech that is God’s attribute, which Arabs could not produce because they were charged with the impossible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r1.anchor: قال قوم: «إن التحدي وقع بالكلام القديم الذي هو صفة الذات، وإن العرب كلفت في ذلك ما لا يطاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r2.claim: Another reported view says the challenge lies in the book’s truthful accounts and narrated unseen matters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: «إن التحدي وقع بما في كتاب الله تعالى من الأنباء الصادقة، والغيوب المسرودة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r3.claim: Ibn ‘Atiyya says these two explanations demonstrate incapacity only to someone who already accepts the revealed law and Muhammad’s prophethood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r3.anchor: وهذان القولان إنما يرى العجز فيهما من قد تقررت الشريعة ونبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في نفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r4.claim: For an unbeliever, the challenge must independently reveal human inability and that the challenged speech came from the claimant; Arabs could not deny the Qur’an’s composition and eloquence came through Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r4.anchor: وأما من هو في ظلمة كفره فإنما يتحدى فيما يبين له بينه وبين نفسه عجزه عنه، وأن البشر لا يأتي بمثله ويتحقق مجيئه من قبل المتحدي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r5.claim: Failure at this challenge would make every eloquent person know necessarily that Muhammad is a prophet bringing what humans cannot produce unless God specially enables a servant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r5.anchor: فإذا تحديت إلى ذلك وعجزت فيه علم كل فصيح ضرورة أن هذا نبي يأتي بما ليس في قدرة البشر الإتيان به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r6.claim: Ibn ‘Atiyya prefers the majority and expert view: the challenge is the Qur’an’s composition, sound meanings, and continuous eloquence of expression.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r6.anchor: وهذا هو القول الذي عليه الجمهور والحذاق وهو الصحيح في نفسه أن التحدي إنما وقع بنظمه وصحة معانيه وتوالي فصاحة ألفاظه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r7.claim: Its inimitability follows from God’s complete knowledge of all speech, which orders every word to fit what precedes and conveys each successive meaning, unlike humans limited by ignorance, forgetfulness, and distraction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r7.anchor: وجه إعجازه أن الله تعالى قد أحاط بكل شيء علما، وأحاط بالكلام كله علما، فإذا ترتبت اللفظة من القرآن علم بإحاطته أي لفظة تصلح أن تلي الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r8.claim: He rejects the claim that Arabs could compose the Qur’an but were diverted from doing so when Muhammad came.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r8.anchor: وبهذا النظر يبطل قول من قال: «إن العرب كان من قدرتها أن تأتي بمثل القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r9.claim: No created being has ever had the capacity to produce anything like the Qur’an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r9.anchor: والصحيح أن الإتيان بمثل القرآن لم يكن قط في قدرة أحد من المخلوقين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r10.claim: Human speeches and poems require year-long revision and remain open to improvement, but no better word can be found if a Qur’anic word is removed and the Arabic language searched.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r10.anchor: كتاب الله لو نزعت منه لفظة ثم أدير لسان العرب في أن يوجد أحسن منها لم يوجد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r11.claim: People recognize the Qur’an’s artistry in much of it but miss its quality in some places because they fall short of the ancient Arabs’ sound taste and discernment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52/r11.anchor: ونحن تبين لنا البراعة في أكثره ويخفى علينا وجهها في مواضع لقصورنا عن مرتبة العرب يومئذ في سلامة الذوق وجودة القريحة وميز الكلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r1.claim: Adna means less than two-thirds of the night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى أي أقل من ثلثي الليل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأهل الكوفة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir and the Kufans read the fāʾ of nisfahu and thāʾ of thuluthahu with fatḥa; the remaining readers use kasra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأهل الكوفة بفتح الفاء والثاء والباقون بكسرهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r3.claim: The group accompanying the Prophet consists of the believers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r3.anchor: وطائفة من الذين معك يعني المؤمنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r4.claim: God knows the lengths of night and day and therefore knows how much of the night people can pray.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r4.anchor: والله يقدر الليل والنهار يعلم مقاديرهما فيعلم القدر الذي تقومون به من الليل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r5.claim: Muqatil says they could not endure praying two-thirds, one-third, or half of every night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما لن تطيقوا قيام ثلثي الليل ولا ثلث الليل ولا نصف الليل قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r6.claim: Al-Farraʾ says they could not keep track of the night’s exact timings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r6.anchor: والثاني لن تحفظوا مواقيت الليل قاله الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r7.claim: God turned toward them with forgiveness and lightened the requirement.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r7.anchor: فتاب عليكم أي عاد عليكم بالمغفرة والتخفيف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r8.claim: The instruction is to recite whatever is manageable in prayer, without setting a fixed duration.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r8.anchor: فاقرؤوا ما تيسر عليكم من القرآن يعني في الصلاة من غير أن يوقت وقتا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r9.claim: Hasan says this refers to the recitation in the Maghrib and Isha prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن هو ما يقرأ في صلاة المغرب والعشاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r10.claim: The sick, travelers seeking provision through trade, and fighters in God’s path may be unable to keep the night vigil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r10.anchor: علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى فلا يطيقون قيام الليل وآخرون يضربون في الأرض وهم المسافرون للتجارة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r11.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r11.claim: The commentators say the night vigil requirement for Muslims was abrogated by the five daily prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r11.anchor: وذكروا أن هذا نسخ عن المسلمين بالصلوات الخمس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r12.claim: Establish the five daily prayers at their appointed times.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r12.anchor: وأقيموا الصلاة أي الصلوات الخمس في أوقاتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r13.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi refers to his earlier explanation of a goodly loan at al-Hadid 57:18.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r13.anchor: وأقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا وقد سبق بيانه الحديد 18

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says the goodly loan means acts beyond zakat, such as maintaining kinship ties and feeding guests.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r14.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد سوى الزكاة في صلة الرحم وقرى الضيف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r15.claim: Whatever good people send ahead, they will find its reward in the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r15.anchor: وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله أي تجدوا ثوابه في الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r16.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r16.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls huwa an intervening separator, and the commentators understand khayran as better and more rewarding than what is deferred until a deathbed bequest.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p395#2/r16.anchor: قال الزجاج ودخلت هو فصلا وقال المفسرون ومعنى خيرا أي أفضل مما أعطيتم وأعظم أجرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن شبرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r1.claim: Ibn Shibrima reasoned that because no sura has fewer than three verses, one should not recite fewer than three verses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r1.anchor: نظرت كم يكفي الرجل من القرآن فلم أجد سورة أقل من ثلاث آيات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r2.claim: The Prophet said that reciting the last two verses of al-Baqara at night suffices the reciter; Ibn Kathir says this report is agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r2.anchor: فذكر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن من قرأ بالآيتين من آخر سورة البقرة في ليلة كفتاه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir says al-Bukhari’s joined transmission is sound: Abd al-Rahman first heard it from Alqama, then directly from Abu Masud while circumambulating the Kaaba; Ali is Ibn al-Madini and his teacher Sufyan ibn Uyayna.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r3.anchor: عبد الرحمن سمعه أولا من علقمة، ثم لقي أبا مسعود وهو يطوف فسمعه منه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن شبرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r4.claim: Ibn Shibrima was the leading jurist of Kufa in his time, and Ibn Kathir calls his inference a good one.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r4.anchor: وما قاله عبد الله بن شبرمة -فقيه الكوفة في زمانه-استنباط حسن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r5.claim: A Sunan report says prayer requires the Opening and three verses; Ibn Kathir judges the Abu Masud report more authentic, famous, and specific, while finding its fit with al-Bukhari’s chapter heading questionable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r5.anchor: لا صلاة إلا بفاتحة الكتاب وثلاث آيات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r6.claim: In the clearer report for the chapter heading, the Prophet counsels Abdullah ibn Amr, who fasted daily and completed the Quran nightly, to read it over a month, then weekly, and settle on the fast of David.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r6.anchor: فلما طال ذلك عليه ذكر للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال: " "القني به"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r7.claim: After growing old and weak, Abdullah regretted not accepting the Prophet’s concession; he maintained his Quran and fasting routine by reciting a seventh by day and making up fasts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: أنكحني أبي امرأة ذات حسب، فكان يتعاهد كنته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r8.claim: The report adds that some recited the Quran every three or five days, while most followed a seven-day completion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p80#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: في ثلاث وفي خمس وأكثرهم على سبع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r1.claim: The Prophet told Abdullah to read the Quran in a month, then in seven days and not less; Ibn Kathir says this wording apparently bars a completion in fewer than seven days.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: " قال لي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "اقرأ القرآن في شهر"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r2.claim: When Qays ibn Sasaa asked how quickly to read, the Prophet first said every fifteen days, then allowed a weekly completion when Qays said he could do more.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r2.anchor: أنه قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " يا رسول الله، في كم أقرأ القرآن؟ فقال: "في كل خمس عشرة"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r3.claim: Abdullah ibn Masud used to complete the Quran from one Friday to the next outside Ramadan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r3.anchor: كان عبد الله بن مسعود يقرأ القرآن في غير رمضان من الجمعة إلى الجمعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r4.claim: Ubay ibn Kaab used to complete the Quran every eight days.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r4.anchor: عن أبي المهلب قال: كان أبي بن كعب يختم القرآن في كل ثمان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r5.speaker: تميم الداري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r5.claim: Tamim al-Dari used to complete the Quran every seven days.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r5.anchor: وكان تميم الداري يختمه في كل سبع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r6.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha‘i used to complete the Quran every seven days.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r6.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم: أنه كان يختم القرآن في كل سبع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r7.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r7.claim: Ibrahim reports that al-Aswad completed the Quran every six days and Alqama every five days.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r7.anchor: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم قال: كان الأسود يختم القرآن في كل ست

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r8.claim: Taken alone, reports limiting completion to seven days would make the matter clear, but other reports establish that completing it sooner is permissible.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p81/r8.anchor: ولكن دلت أحاديث أخرجوها (4) على جواز قراءته فيما دون ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir grades Ahmad’s chain for Saad ibn Mundhir’s report good, strong, and hasan: Hasan ibn Musa is reliable, Ibn Lahia explicitly heard it, and the other named transmitters are trusted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r1.anchor: وهذا إسناد جيد قوي حسن، فإن حسن بن موسى الأشيب ثقة متفق على جلالته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r2.claim: Saad ibn Mundhir asked whether he could read the Quran in three days; the Prophet answered yes, adding in Abu Ubayd’s version, if he was able, and Saad kept to it until death.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r2.anchor: عن سعد بن المنذر الأنصاري أنه قال: " يا رسول الله، أقرأ القرآن في ثلاث؟ قال: "نعم، إن استطعت"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r3.claim: The Prophet said that one who completes the Quran in fewer than three days does not understand it; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا يفقه من قرأه في أقل من ثلاث "

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r4.claim: A report from Aisha says the Prophet never completed the Quran in fewer than three days; Ibn Kathir calls it unusual and weak because al-Tayyib ibn Sulayman was weakened by al-Daraqutni and was little known.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r4.anchor: أنها سمعت عائشة تقول: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يختم القرآن في أقل من ثلاث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r5.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r5.claim: A number of early and later authorities, including Abu Ubayd, Ishaq, and Ibn Rahawayh, disliked completing the Quran in less than three days; Ibn Kathir says the report from Muadh is sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r5.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل أنه كان يكره أن يقرأ القرآن في أقل من ثلاث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r6.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r6.claim: Abdullah ibn Masud said that whoever reads the Quran in fewer than three days is a rajiz, a hurried or metrical reciter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p82/r6.anchor: عبد الله: من قرأ القرآن في أقل من ثلاث فهو راجز

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r1.claim: Abdullah ibn Masud used to complete the Quran in three days during Ramadan; Ibn Kathir grades this report’s chain sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r1.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن مسعود، عن أبيه؛ أنه كان يقرأ القرآن في رمضان في ثلاث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن شبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r2.claim: A report raised to the Prophet instructs readers to avoid excess and neglect, and not to earn from or amass wealth through the Quran.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r2.anchor: وفي المسند عن عبد الرحمن بن شبل مرفوعا: "اقرؤوا القرآن، ولا تغلوا فيه، ولا تجفوا عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir explains that excess means racing through recitation in the shortest time, which usually prevents reflection; neglect means abandoning recitation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p83/r3.anchor: لا تبالغوا في تلاوته بسرعة في أقصر مدة، فإن ذلك ينافي التدبر غالبا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r1.claim: Abu Hanifa and his adherents hold that al-Fatiha is not specifically required in prayer; any Quran recitation suffices, based on the general wording of this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r1.anchor: فعند أبي حنيفة ومن وافقه من أصحابه وغيرهم أنها لا تتعين، بل مهما قرأ به من القرآن أجزأه في الصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa’s side also cites the Prophet’s instruction to a man who prayed badly to recite whatever Quran was easy, without naming al-Fatiha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r2.anchor: إذا قمت إلى الصلاة فكبر، ثم اقرأ ما تيسر معك من القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r3.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r3.claim: Malik, al-Shafii, Ahmad, their followers, and most scholars require al-Fatiha specifically and consider prayer without it invalid, citing reports that the prayer is deficient or invalid without it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r3.anchor: وهو قول بقية الأئمة: مالك والشافعي وأحمد بن حنبل وأصحابهم وجمهور العلماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir explains khidaj in the report about omitting al-Fatiha as deficient, meaning not complete.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r4.anchor: والخداج هو: الناقص كما فسر به في الحديث: " غير تمام "

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r5.claim: Reports from Ubada ibn al-Samit and Abu Hurayra say there is no prayer without al-Fatiha or the Mother of the Quran; Ibn Kathir notes many reports on the issue.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r5.anchor: لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r6.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r6.claim: Al-Shafii and some scholars require al-Fatiha in every rakah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r6.anchor: ثم إن مذهب الشافعي وجماعة من أهل العلم: أنه تجب قراءتها في كل ركعة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r7.speaker: آخرون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r7.claim: Other scholars say al-Fatiha is required in most rakahs rather than every rakah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: إنما تجب قراءتها في معظم الركعات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r8.speaker: الحسن وأكثر البصريين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r8.claim: Al-Hasan and most Basrans hold that al-Fatiha is required in only one rakah, relying on the unrestricted hadith wording.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p108/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن وأكثر البصريين: إنما تجب قراءتها في ركعة واحدة من الصلوات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه والثوري والأوزاعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r1.claim: Abu Hanifa, his adherents, al-Thawri, and al-Awzai hold that al-Fatiha is not specifically required and another passage suffices, citing this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r1.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه والثوري والأوزاعي: لا تتعين (1) قراءتها، بل لو قرأ بغيرها أجزأه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r2.claim: A report from Abu Said says prayer is not sufficient without al-Hamd and a sura in every rakah, whether obligatory or voluntary; Ibn Kathir questions its soundness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد مرفوعا: " لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ في كل ركعة بالحمد وسورة في فريضة أو غيرها "

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir sets out three views on whether a person praying behind an imam must recite al-Fatiha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r3.anchor: هل تجب قراءة الفاتحة على المأموم؟ فيه ثلاثة أقوال للعلماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r4.speaker: أحدها
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r4.claim: The first view makes al-Fatiha obligatory for the follower just as it is for the imam, relying on the general hadiths already cited.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r4.anchor: أحدها: أنه تجب عليه قراءتها، كما تجب على إمامه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r5.speaker: الثاني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r5.claim: The second view requires no recitation by the follower in either quiet or audible prayer; Ibn Kathir says the prophetic chains for its proof are all unsound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r5.anchor: والثاني: لا تجب على المأموم قراءة بالكلية لا الفاتحة ولا غيرها، لا في الصلاة الجهرية ولا السرية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r6.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r6.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that when someone has an imam, the imam’s recitation is his recitation; Ibn Kathir calls its chain weak and notes Malik reports it as Jabir’s own statement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r6.anchor: " من كان له إمام فقراءة الإمام له قراءة " ولكن في إسناده ضعف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r7.speaker: القول الثالث
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r7.claim: The third view requires the follower to recite in quiet prayers but not audible ones; Ibn Kathir says the evidence supports this position, an old view of al-Shafii and a report from Ahmad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r7.anchor: والقول الثالث: أنه تجب القراءة على المأموم في السرية، لما (7) تقدم، ولا تجب (8) في الجهرية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r8.claim: Reports from Abu Musa and Abu Hurayra instruct worshippers to listen silently when the imam recites; Muslim authenticated the report and Ibn Kathir uses it to support the third view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r8.anchor: إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به؛ فإذا كبر فكبروا، وإذا قرأ فأنصتوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir raises these disputes to show that al-Fatiha has rulings not shared by the other suras.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p109/r9.anchor: والغرض من ذكر هذه المسائل هاهنا بيان اختصاص سورة الفاتحة بأحكام لا تتعلق بغيرها من السور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says attend to daytime needs and devote the night to religion; this applied when night prayer was obligatory, before 73:20 eased it, and Ibn Kathir endorses his account.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r12.anchor: قال: لحوائجك، فأفرغ لدينك الليل. قال: وهذا حين كانت صلاة الليل فريضة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r3.claim: Aisha reports that night vigil was initially obligatory; the Prophet and companions kept it for a year until their feet swelled, then the surah’s ending eased the duty to voluntary prayer. Ibn Kathir cites Ahmad’s full report and Muslim’s similar version.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r3.anchor: فإن الله افترض قيام الليل في أول هذه السورة، فقام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه حولا حتى انتفخت أقدامهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir says the route through Musa ibn Ubayda is weak, and the sound hadith omits the added claim that this surah was revealed then; the report’s wording may suggest a Medinan surah, but it is Meccan, and its eight-month interval conflicts with Ahmad’s year report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r4.anchor: ورواه ابن أبي حاتم من طريق موسى بن عبيدة الربذي، وهو ضعيف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that people initially prayed roughly as much at night as in Ramadan, with close to a year between the surah’s beginning and end; several routes likewise report a year.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r5.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس يقول: أول ما نزل: أول المزمل، كانوا يقومون نحوا من قيامهم في شهر رمضان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r1.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman says the believers kept night vigil for a year until their feet and shins swelled, then 73:20 brought relief; al-Hasan al-Basri agrees.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن قال: لما نزلت: {يا أيها المزمل}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r2.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet and companions prayed until their feet swelled and that the surah’s ending was held in heaven for sixteen months before it descended.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r3.claim: Qatada says they kept night vigil for a year or two until their legs and feet swelled, after which God sent relief at the end of the surah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r3.anchor: وقال معمر، عن قتادة: {قم الليل إلا قليلا} قاموا حولا أو حولين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the Prophet and a group of companions maintained the commanded vigil for ten years, until the final verse eased it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r4.anchor: عن جعفر، عن سعيد -هو ابن جبير-قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command to the Prophet and believers to rise for most of the night burdened them, then 73:20 relieved and broadened the obligation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r5.anchor: علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r2.claim: The Prophet and some companions varied between these portions without aiming at exact fractions, because maintaining the prescribed vigil was difficult.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r2.anchor: تارة هكذا، وتارة هكذا، وذلك كله من غير قصد منكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r3.claim: God measures the night and day so they sometimes match and sometimes one lengthens at the expense of the other.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r3.anchor: تارة يعتدلان، وتارة يأخذ هذا من هذا، أو هذا من هذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r4.claim: God knew the believers could not keep exact count of the required night portion, so He eased the duty and allowed whatever recitation is manageable, meaning night prayer without a fixed duration.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r4.anchor: علم أن لن تحصوه} أي: الفرض الذي أوجبه عليكم {فاقرءوا ما تيسر من القرآن}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r5.claim: Recitation here stands for prayer, as in 17:110, where not raising one’s voice in prayer means not raising it in recitation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r5.anchor: كما قال في سورة سبحان: {ولا تجهر بصلاتك}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r6.speaker: أصحاب الإمام أبي حنيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r6.claim: Hanafi jurists use this verse and the report telling a poor-performing worshipper to read what is easy to argue that al-Fatiha is not required and even one verse suffices.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r6.anchor: استدل أصحاب الإمام أبي حنيفة، رحمه الله، بهذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r7.claim: The majority answer that position with the Prophet’s statement that prayer is invalid without the Opening of the Book, reinforced by reports requiring Umm al-Kitab in every prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p257#2/r7.anchor: أجابهم الجمهور بحديث عبادة بن الصامت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r1.claim: God foreknows that illness, travel for livelihood, and fighting in His path will excuse some Muslims from night vigil; since this Meccan surah preceded legislation of fighting, the prediction is a sign of prophethood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r1.anchor: مكية، ولم يكن القتال شرع بعد، فهي من أكبر دلائل النبوة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r2.claim: The repeated instruction means to perform as much night prayer as is manageable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r2.anchor: أي: قوموا بما تيسر عليكم منه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r3.claim: Al-Hasan condemns a memorizer who prays only the obligatory prayers as one who neglects the Qur'an, and says a little night recitation, even five verses, is required of its bearers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r3.anchor: قال: يتوسد القرآن، لعن الله ذاك، قال الله تعالى للعبد الصالح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r4.claim: A hadith says that one who sleeps until morning has Satan urinate in his ear; commentators differ whether this means missing an obligatory prayer or night vigil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r4.anchor: فقيل معناه: نام عن المكتوبة. وقيل: عن قيام الليل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r5.claim: Two hadiths urge the people of Qur'an to pray witr, one saying to do so and another warning that whoever omits witr is not of the community.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r6.speaker: أبو بكر عبد العزيز
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir notes as an unusually strong position Abu Bakr Abd al-Aziz’s view that Ramadan night vigil is obligatory, adding that God knows best.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r6.anchor: وأغرب من هذا ما حكي عن أبي بكر عبد العزيز، من الحنابلة، من إيجابه قيام شهر رمضان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r7.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet through Ibn Abbas interprets the manageable recitation as one hundred verses; Ibn Kathir later calls this report very strange and says he found it only in al-Tabarani’s collection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p258/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: {فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the hundred-verse report very strange and says he found it only in al-Tabarani’s Mu'jam.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r1.anchor: وهذا حديث غريب جدا لم أره إلا في معجم الطبراني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r2.claim: The verse commands the obligatory prayer and zakah; this indicates zakah was prescribed in Mecca, while its thresholds and payment details were specified in Medina.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r2.anchor: مقادير النصب والمخرج لم تبين إلا بالمدينة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، وعكرمة، ومجاهد، والحسن، وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r3.claim: These early authorities say the final verse abrogated the original obligation of night vigil; reports differ on how long that first obligation lasted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r3.anchor: إن هذه الآية نسخت الذي كان الله قد أوجبه على المسلمين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r4.claim: In the Sahihayn, the Prophet tells a questioner that five daily prayers are required and there is no other obligation unless one volunteers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r4.anchor: ثبت في الصحيحين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لذلك الرجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r5.claim: Lending God a good loan means giving charity, for which God grants the best and most abundant reward; Ibn Kathir links this to 2:245.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r5.anchor: يعني: من الصدقات، فإن الله يجازي على ذلك أحسن الجزاء وأوفره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r1.claim: Whatever good people send ahead will be preserved with God and is better than what they keep for themselves in worldly life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r1.anchor: وهو خير مما أبقيتموه لأنفسكم في الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r2.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r2.claim: The Prophet contrasts wealth sent ahead with wealth left to heirs: a person’s real wealth is what they have given or prepared for the afterlife, while the heir receives what was deferred.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r3.claim: Seek God’s forgiveness often in every affair, since He forgives and shows mercy to those who ask.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p260/r3.anchor: أكثروا من ذكره واستغفاره في أموركم كلها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r1.claim: The Prophet licensed the community to recite in seven ahruf; when Uthman feared division from differences in recitation, he unified them on the official codex, and the community accepted his sound guidance, leaving the other six.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r1.anchor: أن الشارع رخص للأمة التلاوة على سبعة أحرف، ثم لما رأى الإمام أمير المؤمنين عثمان بن عفان، رضي الله عنه، اختلاف الناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r2.claim: The six recitations left by the just Imam eventually became unknown and their traces disappeared, so no one today can recite them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r2.anchor: وتركت القراءة الأحرف الستة التي عزم عليها إمامها العادل في تركها طاعة منها له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r3.claim: Answering how Muslims could leave readings taught by the Prophet, Ibn Kathir says the command was permission and ease, not obligation; if obligatory, every letter would have been transmitted through decisive chains, and their failure to do so shows choice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r3.anchor: إن أمره إياهم بذلك لم يكن أمر إيجاب وفرض، وإنما كان أمر إباحة ورخصة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r4.claim: Ordinary differences in inflection, vowelization, or replacing a letter while the written form agrees are not the seven-letter disputes whose contentiousness entails disbelief; no scholar deems such ordinary recitation debate disbelief.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r4.anchor: فأما ما كان من اختلاف القراءة في رفع حرف ونصبه وجره وتسكين حرف وتحريكه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r5.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r5.claim: Umar reports hearing Hisham recite al-Furqan in unfamiliar forms; each said the Prophet taught him, and the Prophet validated both recitations as revealed, declaring the Quran came in seven ahruf and to recite what is easy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p43/r5.anchor: سمعا عمر بن الخطاب يقول: سمعت هشام بن حكيم يقرأ سورة الفرقان في حياة رسول الله

JISHUMI:v10p7131/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r1.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r1.claim: The Qadi reports that the sura is called Meccan, Medinan, or partly each; Hamza holds it is Meccan except from إن ربك يعلم through the end.
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r1.anchor: قال القاضي: قيل: مكية، وقيل: مدنية، وقيل: بعضها مكية وبعضها مدنية

JISHUMI:v10p7131/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r2.speaker: حمزة
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r2.claim: Hamza classifies the sura as Meccan apart from the passage beginning إن ربك يعلم and continuing to the end.
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r2.anchor: وقال حمزة: إنها مكية إلا قوله: (إن ربك يعلم) إلى آخر السورة

JISHUMI:v10p7131/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r3.claim: The sura has twenty verses in the Kufan count, nineteen in the Basran count, and eighteen in the Medinan count.
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r3.anchor: وهي عشرون آية في الكوفي، وتسع عشرة في البصري، وثماني عشرة في المدني

JISHUMI:v10p7131/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r4.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b transmits from the Prophet that reciting this sura wards off hardship in this world and the next; no grading is stated.
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r4.anchor: عن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم -: أنه من قرأ سورة (المزمل)

JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عافر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r1.claim: These readers put نصفه and ثلثه in the genitive, coordinating them with ثلثي; أدنى then applies to all three measures.
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عافر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: ونصفه وثلثه بالجر فيهما عطفا على (ثلثي)

JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r2.claim: The other readers use the accusative, estimating تقوم نصفه وثلثه; on this reading أدنى applies only to two-thirds.
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالنصب فيهما، على تقدير: تقوم نصفه وثلثه، والأدنى على هذا يختص بثلثيه

JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r4.claim: أدنى means nearer; the present life is called الدنيا because it is closer than the afterlife.
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r4.anchor: والأدنى: الأقرب، ومنه سميت الدنيا؛ لأنها أقرب من الآخرة

JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r5.claim: إحصاء and counting are closely related, with إحصاء meaning to encompass something by calculation.
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r5.anchor: والإحصاء والعد من النظائر، والإحصاء: هو إحاطتك به حسابا

JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r6.claim: Striking through the earth means traveling through it.

JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r8.claim: The phrase وآخرون elliptically means there will be others.

JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r9.claim: خيرا and أعظم are accusative objects of تجدوه; Basran grammarians call the construction صلة, while Kufans call it عماد.
JISHUMI:v10p7143#2/r9.anchor: خيرا وأعظم نصب؛ لأنه مفعول (تجدوه)، أي: تجدوه خيرا وأعظم

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r2.claim: The mitigation after strictness supports the majority view that night prayer was first obligatory and later abrogated, against Abu Ali's view that it was voluntary and Abu Muslim's claim that standing meant reciting.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r2.anchor: فالظاهر يليق بقول الجماعة: إن صلاة الليل كانت واجبة ثم نسخت، دون قول أبي علي أنها كانت نافلة

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r3.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r3.claim: Abu Ali says night prayer was voluntary rather than an obligation.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r3.anchor: دون قول أبي علي أنها كانت نافلة لا فرض

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r4.claim: Abu Muslim takes قيام to mean standing for recitation, but the author objects that recitation had not been obligatory to require mitigation.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r4.anchor: ودون قول أبي مسلم أن القيام للقراءة؛ لأن القراءة لم تكن واجبة حتى خفف

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r5.claim: Prayer may use any available Quranic passage; the Iraqis therefore reject fixing al-Fatiha as a requirement, contrary to al-Shafi'i, since the verse's apparent wording permits broader recitation.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r5.anchor: أنه تجوز الصلاة بما شاء من القرآن، ولا تتعين الفاتحة على ما يقوله أهل العراق، خلاف قول الشافعي

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r6.speaker: بعض مشايخنا
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r6.claim: Some of the author's teachers say a solitary report cannot fix al-Fatiha because that would abrogate the Quran; calling the verse ambiguous about other passages would contradict its apparent sense.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r6.anchor: ومن مشايخنا من يقول: لا يقبل في تعيين الفاتحة خبر الواحد؛ لأنه يقتضي نسخ ما ثبت بالقرآن

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r7.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r7.claim: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, and a report from Abu Hanifa, hold that prayer is valid with three short verses or one long verse.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r7.anchor: ومنها: أن الصلاة تجوز بقراءة ثلاث آيات قصار، أو آية طويلة، وهو قول أبي يوسف ومحمد، ورواية عن أبي حنيفة

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r8.claim: Another report from Abu Hanifa permits prayer with a single verse, relying on the verse's apparent wording.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r8.anchor: ويروى عنه أنه يجوز بآية واحدة، ويستدل بظاهر الآية

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r9.claim: The dispensation applies equally to travel for jihad and travel for trade.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r9.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وآخرون) الآية أنه يستوي في الرخص سفر الجهاد، وسفر التجارة

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r10.claim: The verse indicates that trade and earning a livelihood are permitted.

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r11.claim: Prayer and zakat are obligatory; the definite article is generic in form but conventionally refers to the prescribed prayers and zakat.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r11.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وأقيموا) الآية، على وجوب الصلاة والزكاة، والألف واللام إنما تكون للجنس

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r12.claim: All human deeds are preserved and none is lost, supporting Abu Hashim's doctrine of balancing deeds against Abu Ali's doctrine that deeds cancel one another.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r12.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وما تقدموا) أن جميع ما يعمله العبد محفوظ، لا يضيع منه شيء، فتدل على قول أبي هاشم في الموازنة

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r13.claim: Seeking God's forgiveness and repenting is obligatory at all times because a morally accountable person is rarely free of shortcomings.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r13.anchor: ويدل قوله: (واستغفروا) على وجوب الاستغفار والتوبة في الأحوال كلها؛ لأن المكلف قل ما يخلو من تقصير

JISHUMI:v10p7146/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r14.claim: Establishing prayer, giving zakat, and seeking forgiveness are acts of the servant rather than acts created by God.
JISHUMI:v10p7146/r14.anchor: وتدل أن إقامة الصلاة والزكاة والاستغفار فعل العبد، ليس بخلق الله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r1.claim: Adnā min thuluthay al-layl means less than two thirds; “nearer” is figuratively “less,” since less distance means fewer intervening spaces.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r1.anchor: أقل منهما ؛ وإنما استعير الأدنى وهو الأقرب للأقل ؛ لأن المسافة بين الشيئين إذا دنت : قل ما بينهما من الأحياز

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r2.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r2.claim: The accusative reading means they stand less than two thirds, or stand half or a third, matching the earlier options of a full half, a shorter third, or more than half but less than two thirds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r2.anchor: وقرىء ( ونصفه وثلثه ) بالنصب على أنك تقوم أقل من الثلثين ، وتقوم النصف والثلث : وهو مطابق لما مر في أول السورة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r3.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r3.claim: The genitive reading means less than two thirds, less than half, and less than a third; the available periods are half, a third, and a quarter.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r4.claim: A group of the Prophet's companions also perform the night vigil.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r4.anchor: وطائفة من الذين معك } ويقوم ذلك جماعة من أصحابك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r5.claim: Only God can measure the night and day or know the lengths of their hours; placing God's name before “measures” emphasizes this exclusive power.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r5.anchor: ولا يقدر على تقدير الليل والنهار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r6.claim: The pronoun in “you cannot calculate it” refers to God's measuring; people cannot reliably track or equalize the hours, except by taking the broader, burdensome allowance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r6.anchor: والضمير في { لن تحصوه } لمصدر يقدر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r7.claim: “He relented toward you” means He licensed them to leave the prescribed night vigil, lifting the liability as from a repentant person.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r7.anchor: عبارة عن الترخيص في ترك القيام المقدر . كقوله : { فتاب عليكم وعفا عنكم فالن باشروهن }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r8.claim: Recitation names prayer by one of its pillars, as prayer is also called standing, bowing, or prostration; pray whatever night prayer is feasible. This abrogates the original command, and both are later superseded by the five prayers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r8.anchor: وعبر عن الصلاة بالقراءة ؛ لأنها بعض أركانها ، كما عبر عنها بالقيام والركوع والسجود يريد : فصلوا ما تيسر عليكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r9.claim: An alternative takes the phrase as Qurʾān recitation itself: fifty or a hundred verses, with reports that a hundred makes one among the devout or leaves the Qurʾān unable to argue against him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r9.anchor: قيل هي قراءة القرآن بعينها ؛ قيل : يقرأ مائة آية ومن قرأ مائة آية في ليلة لم يحاجه القرآن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r10.claim: The easing is justified because night vigil is difficult for the sick, people traveling for trade, and those fighting in God's path; God thus equates fighters with travelers seeking lawful earnings.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p643#2/r10.anchor: وقد بين الحكمة في النسخ . وهي تعذر القيام على المرضى ، والضاربين في الأرض للتجارة ، والمجاهدين في سبيل الله . وقيل : سوى الله بين المجاهدين والمسافرين لكسب الحلال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that one who patiently brings goods to a Muslim city seeking God's reward and sells at the day's price is counted among the martyrs before God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r1.anchor: أيما رجل جلب شيئا إلى مدينة من مدائن المسلمين صابرا محتسبا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that, after being killed in God's path, he would prefer to die while traveling on a mount in search of God's bounty over any other death.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r2.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمر : ما خلق الله موتة أموتها بعد القتل في سبيل الله أحب إلي من أن أموت بين شعبتي رجل : أضرب في الأرض أبتغي من فضل الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r3.claim: “He knew” begins a new sentence, answering the implied question about the reason for abrogation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r3.anchor: استئناف على تقدير السؤال عن وجه النسخ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r4.claim: Establishing prayer means the obligatory prayers; zakāh means the obligatory alms, or alternatively zakāt al-fiṭr, since regular zakāh had not yet been required in Mecca.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r5.claim: If zakāh here means the obligatory alms tax, the end of the sūra is Medinan.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r5.anchor: وإنما وجبت بعد ذلك . ومن فسرها بالزكاة الواجبة جعل آخر السورة مدنيا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r6.claim: “Lend God a good loan” can mean voluntary charity, giving obligatory zakāh excellently and sincerely to its rightful recipients, or any good done with one's person or wealth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يريد : سائر الصدقات وأن يريد : أداء الزكاة على أحسن وجه : من إخراج أطيب المال وأعوده على الفقراء ، ومراعاة النية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r7.claim: Khayran is the second object of wajada and a separator; this is allowed although it is not between two definite nouns because afʿal min resists the definite article.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r7.anchor: ثاني مفعولي وجد . وهو فصل . وجاز وإن لم يقع بين معرفتين . لأن أفعل من أشبه في امتناعه من حرف التعريف المعرفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r8.speaker: أبو السمال
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r8.claim: Abū al-Sammāl reads “huwa khayrun wa-aʿẓamu ajran” in the nominative, with a nominal subject and predicate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال ( هو خير وأعظم أجرا ) بالرفع على الابتداء والخبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r9.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r9.claim: The Prophet says whoever recites Sūrat al-Muzzammil will be spared hardship in this world and the next; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p644/r9.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r1.claim: God determines the hours of night and day, either for the acts of His servants or for His decree concerning creation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r1.anchor: يعني يقدر ساعتهما , فاحتمل ذلك وجهين : أحدهما : تقديرهما لأعمال عباده . الثاني : لقضائه في خلقه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r2.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the believers would not be able to sustain night vigil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r2.anchor: لن تطيقوا قيام الليل , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r3.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says they could not calculate half, a third, or a quarter of the night.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r3.anchor: يريد تقدير نصف الليل وثلثه وربعه , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r4.claim: One possibility is that God pardoned earlier shortcomings and told them to recite what they could thereafter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r4.anchor: فتاب عليكم من تقصيركم فيما مضى , فاقرؤوا في المستبقل ما تيسر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r5.claim: A second possibility is that God lightened the obligation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r6.claim: One reading takes “recite what is easy” as prayer, called Qur'an because it contains recitation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r6.anchor: فصلوا ما تيسر من الصلاة , فعبر عن الصلاة بالقرآن لما يتضمنها من القرآن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r7.claim: On that reading, it may refer either to voluntary prayer, since the fixed obligatory prayer is not described as “what is easy,” or to the five prayers replacing night vigil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r7.anchor: ما يتطوع به من نوافله لأن الفرض المقدر لا يؤمر فيه بما تيسر . الثاني : أنه محمول على فروض الصلوات الخمس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r8.claim: For the five-prayer reading, “what is easy” describes strength or weakness and health or illness in performance, not the legally fixed number.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r8.anchor: محمولا على صفة الأداء في القوة والضعف , والصحة والمرض , ولا يكون محمولا على العدد المقدر شرعا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r9.claim: A second reading takes the wording plainly as reciting whatever portion of the Qur'an is easy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r9.anchor: أن المراد بذلك قراءة ما تيسر من القرآن حملا للخطاب على ظاهر اللفظ

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r10.claim: If the command means Qur'an recitation in prayer, it is obligatory because recitation in prayer is obligatory.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r10.anchor: أن المراد به قراءة القرآن في الصلاة فيكون الأمر به واجبا لوجوب القراءة في الصلاة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r11.speaker: مالك والشافعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r11.claim: Malik and al-Shafiʿi require the whole Opening Sura in prayer and forbid replacing it or reciting only part of it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r11.anchor: فقدره مالك والشافعي بفاتحة الكتاب , لا يجوز العدول عنها ولا الاقتصار على بعضها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r12.speaker: أبو حنيفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r12.claim: Abu Hanifa requires one verse from any part of the Qur'an.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r12.anchor: وقدرها أبو حنيفة بآية واحدة من أي القرآن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r13.claim: A second possibility is Qur'an recitation outside prayer; scholars differ whether the unrestricted command makes it obligatory or recommended.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r13.anchor: والوجه الثاني : أن المراد به قراءة القرآن من غير الصلاة , فعلى هذا يكون مطلق هذا الأمر محمولا على الوجوب أو على الاستحباب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r14.claim: One view makes it obligatory so a reader learns the Qur'an's inimitability, proofs of monotheism, and the sending of messengers; memorizing the whole Qur'an remains recommended, not required.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r14.anchor: أنه محمول على الوجوب ليقف بقراءته على إعجازه , ودلائل التوحيد فيه وبعث الرسل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r15.speaker: الأكثرون
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r15.claim: Most scholars treat recitation outside prayer as recommended, reasoning that if recitation were obligatory, memorization would also be obligatory.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r15.anchor: أنه محمول على الاستحباب دون الوجوب , وهذا قول الأكثرين لأنه لو وجب عليه أن يقرأه وجب عليه أن يحفظه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r16.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r16.claim: Al-Dahhak says the command encompasses the entire Qur'an, which God has made easy for people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r16.anchor: جميع القرآن , لأن الله تعالى قد يسره على عباده , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r17.speaker: جويبر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r17.claim: Juyaybir says the command encompasses a third of the Qur'an.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r18.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r18.claim: Al-Suddi sets the amount at two hundred verses.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas sets the amount at one hundred verses.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r20.speaker: أبو خالد الكناني
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r20.claim: Abu Khalid al-Kinani sets the amount at three verses, the length of the shortest sura.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r20.anchor: ثلاث آيات كأقصر سورة , قاله أبو خالد الكناني

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r21.claim: God names illness as a reason for easing the night-vigil burden because it incapacitates people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r21.anchor: ذكر الله أسباب التخفيف , فذكر منها المرض لأنه يعجز

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r22.claim: One interpretation identifies these people as travelers, linking the phrase to 4:101.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r22.anchor: أنهم المسافرون , كما قال عز وجل : { وإذا ضربتم في الأرض فليس عليكم جناح أن تقصروا من الصلاة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r23.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r23.claim: Ibn Masʿud, raising the report to the Prophet, and al-Suddi take them as merchants traveling to seek God's bounty.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r23.anchor: أنه التقلب للتجارة لقوله تعالى : { يبتغون من فضل الله } , قاله ابن مسعود يرفعه , وهو قول السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r24.claim: Those fighting in God's way are the people engaged in jihad for His obedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r25.claim: The instruction abrogates the opening sura's night-vigil obligation and makes the available recitation voluntary; an obligation would not be phrased as doing what is easy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r25.anchor: نسخ ما فرضه في أول السورة من قيام الليل وجعل ما تيسر منه تطوعا ونفلا , لأن الفرض لا يؤمر فيه بفعل ما تيسر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r26.claim: The command concerns the five obligatory prayers performed at their appointed times.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r27.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r27.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets zakat here as obedience to God and sincerity toward Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r27.anchor: أنها ها هنا طاعة الله والإخلاص له , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r28.speaker: الحارث العكلي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r28.claim: Al-Harith al-ʿUkli interprets zakat here as the alms paid at the end of Ramadan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r28.anchor: أنها صدقة الفطر , قاله الحارث العكلي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r29.speaker: قتادة وعكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r29.claim: Qatada and ʿIkrima interpret zakat here as the full due on wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r29.anchor: أنها زكاة الأموال كلها , قاله قتادة وعكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r30.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r30.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the good loan as voluntary deeds performed after obligatory ones.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r30.anchor: أنه النوافل بعد الفروض , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r31.speaker: ابن حبان
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r31.claim: Ibn Hibban identifies the loan with saying “Glory be to God,” “Praise be to God,” “There is no god but God,” and “God is greatest.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r31.anchor: قول سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر , قاله ابن حبان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r32.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r32.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r32.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the good loan is spending on one's family.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r32.anchor: النفقة على الأهل , قاله زيد بن أسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r33.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r33.speaker: عمر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r33.claim: ʿUmar says the good loan is spending in God's cause.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r33.anchor: النفقة من سبيل الله , وهذا قول عمر رضي الله عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r34.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r34.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r34.claim: Al-Mawardi allows the phrase to encompass every act of obedience that earns reward.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r34.anchor: أنه أمر بفعل جميع الطاعات التي يستحق عليها الثواب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r35.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r35.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r35.claim: What is found with God is the reward for what people gave and did.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r35.anchor: يعني تجدوا ثوابه عند الله { هو خيرا } يعني مما أعطيتم وفعلتم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r36.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r36.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r36.claim: Abu Hurayra identifies the greater reward as Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r36.anchor: { وأعظم أجرا } قال أبو هريرة : الجنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r37.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r37.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r37.claim: Al-Mawardi allows the greater reward to mean that each good deed is repaid tenfold.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r37.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ( أعظم أجرا ) الإعطاء بالحسنة عشرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r38.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r38.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r38.claim: The command is to seek forgiveness for one's sins.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r39.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r39.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r39.claim: God is forgiving of what came before repentance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r40.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r40.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r40.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says God is merciful toward people after they repent.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p131/r40.anchor: بكم بعدها , قاله سعيد بن جبير

MUJAHID:v2p701/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p701/r1.speaker: مسروق بن الأجدع
MUJAHID:v2p701/r1.claim: Masruq says this verse is better for Muhammad's community than if each person were given the world.
MUJAHID:v2p701/r1.anchor: عن مسروق بن الأجدع قال هذه الآية خير لأمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من أن يعطى كل رجل منهم مثل الدنيا

MUJAHID:v2p701/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p701/r2.speaker: مسروق بن الأجدع
MUJAHID:v2p701/r2.claim: Masruq says the instruction to recite what is easy abrogated the earlier command to stand at night except a little.
MUJAHID:v2p701/r2.anchor: عن مسروق بن الأجدع قال هذه الآية خير لأمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من أن يعطى كل رجل منهم مثل الدنيا

BURSEVI:v10p168/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p168/r3.claim: Adnā here means 'less than'; using 'nearer' for 'less' is a metonymy, since less distance leaves fewer intervening spaces.
BURSEVI:v10p168/r3.anchor: أي أقل منهما فإطلاق الأدنى على الأقل مجاز مرسل من قبيل إطلاق الملزوم على اللازم

BURSEVI:v10p168/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p168/r4.claim: Night prayer was first prescribed at the opening of the surah; the Prophet and Companions struggled for a year, often praying all night from fear of miscalculating the required portion, until their feet swelled and faces paled.
BURSEVI:v10p168/r4.anchor: روى إنه تعالى افترض قيام اللل في أول هذه السورة

BURSEVI:v10p168/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p168/r5.claim: This ending relaxed the prescribed night portions while retaining night prayer as obligatory as possible; the obligation itself was later superseded by the five daily prayers, since adding duties beyond five is an addition.
BURSEVI:v10p168/r5.anchor: فنسخ تقدير القيام بالمقادير المذكورة مع بقاء فرضية أصل التهجد

BURSEVI:v10p168/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p168/r6.claim: The accusative half and third are coordinated with adnā, describing praying less than two-thirds and praying a half or a third of the night.
BURSEVI:v10p168/r6.anchor: بالنصب عطفا على أدنى والثلث أحد أجزاء الثلثة

BURSEVI:v10p168/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p168/r7.claim: Ṭāʾifatun is nominative, coordinated with the subject implied in taqūmu; min may be explanatory, so the phrase does not prove that night prayer was not prescribed for everyone.
BURSEVI:v10p168/r7.anchor: مروفع معطوف على الضمير في تقوم وجاز ذلك للفصل بينهما أي ويقوم معك طائفة من أصحابك

BURSEVI:v10p168/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p168/r8.claim: A group of the Prophet's Companions joins him in night prayer; this wording promises them favor, and Qut al-qulub notes their inclusion with him in gratitude and good reward.
BURSEVI:v10p168/r8.anchor: وفي قوت القلوب قد قرن الله تعالى قوام الليل برسوله المصطفى عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r1.claim: The verse signifies the heart's frequent escape from the night of its nature through turning to God and away from the self; brief veiling remains by wisdom and is itself mercy. The 'group' with the Messenger of the heart means spiritual powers and bodily members.
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r1.anchor: التأويلات النجمية : يشير إلى انسلاخ رسول القلب

BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r2.claim: The fronted divine subject with the verb 'determines' makes God's exclusive ability to measure night and day emphatic.
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r2.anchor: فإن تقديم الاسم الجليل مبتدأ وبناء يقدر عليه موجب للاختصاص قطعا

BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r3.speaker: الراغب
