BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines taqdīr as making the quantity of a thing clear.
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r3.anchor: قال الراغب : التقدير تبيين كمية الشيء

BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r4.claim: God alone knows the exact hours of night and day and can fulfill the right of worship in each; people can only estimate, and their effort may err.
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r4.anchor: والحاصل إن العالم بمقادير ساعات الليل والنهار على حقائقها هو الله

BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r5.claim: The pronoun in 'you will not calculate it' refers to the implied act of measuring; people cannot determine the times exactly or keep every hour precisely.
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r5.anchor: لن تقدروا على تقدير الأوقات على حقائقها ولن تستطيعوا ضبط الساعات أبدا فالضمير عائد إلى المصدر المفهوم من يقدر

BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r6.speaker: تاج المصادر
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r6.claim: Taj al-Masadir glosses iḥṣāʾ as knowing and counting exhaustively and being able to do so.
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r6.anchor: قال في تاج المصادر الإحصاء دانستن وشمردن بر سبيل استقصا وتوانستن

BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r7.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r7.claim: Al-Raghib defines iḥṣāʾ as collection or attainment by number.

BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r8.claim: The Prophet's saying 'Be upright, and you will not attain it' is cited to illustrate that complete attainment is beyond reach.
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r8.anchor: وروى استقيموا ولن تحصوا أي لن تحصلوا ذلك لأن الحق واحد

BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r9.claim: Some use 'you will not calculate it' alongside the command to rise at night as proof of impossible obligations; the author answers that the wording means difficulty, as when someone says another person is unbearable to look at.
BURSEVI:v10p168#2/r9.anchor: واحتج بعضهم بهذه الآية على وقوع تكليف ما لا يطاق

BURSEVI:v10p169/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p169/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p169/r1.claim: The spiritual journey from nature's night to reality's day proceeds by God's determination, not the seeker's; arrival depends on divine grace, as many travelers turn back without reaching the goal.
BURSEVI:v10p169/r1.anchor: التأويلات النجمية : يعني السلوك من ليل الطبيعة إلى نهار الحقيقة

BURSEVI:v10p169/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p169/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p169/r2.claim: Tāba ʿalaykum is a metaphorical extension from accepting repentance to granting a dispensation; tabʿah means the harm that follows an act.
BURSEVI:v10p169/r2.anchor: بلترخيص على ترك القيام المقدر ورفع التبعة عن التائب ثم استعمل لفظ المشبه به

BURSEVI:v10p169/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p169/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p169/r3.claim: God eased the rule by permitting people to leave the prescribed measure of night prayer and lifting the resulting liability.
BURSEVI:v10p169/r3.anchor: فتاب أي فرخص والتبعة ما يترتب على الشيء من المضرة

BURSEVI:v10p169/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p169/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p169/r4.claim: The phrase means perform whatever night prayer is easy, without a fixed fraction of the night; even a brief amount counts, perhaps four or two rakʿahs.
BURSEVI:v10p169/r4.anchor: أي فصلوا ما تيسر لكم من صلاة الليل غير مقدرة بكونها في ثلث الليل أو نحوه ولو قدر حلب شاة فهذا كون أربع ركعات

BURSEVI:v10p169/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p169/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p169/r5.claim: Recitation names the whole prayer by one of its parts, a metonymic use of part for whole.
BURSEVI:v10p169/r5.anchor: عبر عن الصلاة بالقراءة كما عبر عنها بسائر أركانها على طريق إطلاق اسم الجزء على الكل مجازا مرسلا

BURSEVI:v10p169/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p169/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p169/r6.claim: Night vigil was initially obligatory under the stated options; because it became difficult, this verse abrogated its fixed measure with an easier allowance.
BURSEVI:v10p169/r6.anchor: فتبين أن التهجد كان واجبا على التخيير المذكور فعسر عليهم القيام به فنسخ بهذه

BURSEVI:v10p170/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p170/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p170/r1.claim: The verse also signals gathering in pure hearts the realities, subtleties, spiritual knowledges, and insights revealed according to one's readiness, and concealing them from unfit listeners who might accuse the knower of heresy or unionism.
BURSEVI:v10p170/r1.anchor: التأويلات النجمية : في إشارة الآية يعني أجمعوا واحفظوا

BURSEVI:v10p170/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p170/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p170/r2.claim: Marḍā is the plural of marīḍ, illness being departure from the human being's proper balance.
BURSEVI:v10p170/r2.anchor: مرضا جمع مريض والمرض الحروج عن الاعتدال

BURSEVI:v10p170/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p170/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p170/r3.claim: The sick signify hearts veiled by ego and occupied with worldly love and desire, on which none of the Quran's hidden realities become manifest.
BURSEVI:v10p170/r3.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى مرضى القلوب بحجب الأنانية والاشتغال

BURSEVI:v10p170/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p170/r4.speaker: سنائي
BURSEVI:v10p170/r4.claim: Sanāʾī's poem says a spiritually blind person receives only Quranic letters, just as a blind eye gets only warmth from the sun; Quran's unveiled bride is for one whose faith is cleared of turmoil.
BURSEVI:v10p170/r4.anchor: عجب نبو دكرز قرآن نصيبت نيست جز حرفى كه از خورشيد جز كرمى نيابد شم نابينا

BURSEVI:v10p170/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p170/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p170/r5.claim: Others travel for trade and profit; 'God's bounty' explicitly acknowledges that earnings come from Him, and seeking knowledge is also among the finest gains.
BURSEVI:v10p170/r5.anchor: أي يسافرون فيها للتجارة من ضرب في الأرض سافر فيها ابتغاء الرزق

BURSEVI:v10p170/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p170/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p170/r6.claim: Since the Prophet was present when this verse was revealed, the travelers were not leaving him for instruction; if the surah's ending is Medinan, they could instead be migrating to Medina for learning. The rule also serves later generations.
BURSEVI:v10p170/r6.anchor: وفيه إن معلم الخير وهو رسول الله عليه السلام كان حاضرا عندهم وقت نزول الآية فأين يذهبون إلا أن يجعل آخر السورة مدنيا

BURSEVI:v10p170/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p170/r7.speaker: أبو ذر
BURSEVI:v10p170/r7.claim: Abu Dharr reports that attending a lesson surpasses a thousand units of prayer, a thousand funerals, and a thousand visits to the sick; asked whether Quran recitation is also surpassed, he answers that recitation without action does not benefit.
BURSEVI:v10p170/r7.anchor: وفي حديث أبي ذر رضي الله عنه إنه قال حضور مجلس علم أفضل من صلاة ألف ركعة وأفضل من شهود ألف جنزة

BURSEVI:v10p170/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p170/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p170/r8.claim: Those fighting in God's path are another group; the verse signals that permission to fight enemies will come and equates their merit with lawful earners supporting themselves, dependents, and the needy.
BURSEVI:v10p170/r8.anchor: عطف على مرضى أيضا ويقاتلون صفته وسبيل الله ما يوصل إلى الأجر عند الله كالجهاد

BURSEVI:v10p170/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p170/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p170/r9.claim: The verse places lawful trade for family support and charity on a level with striving in God's path.
BURSEVI:v10p170/r9.anchor: حيث جمع نبيهما قول على أن التجارة بمنزلة الجهاد

BURSEVI:v10p170/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p170/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BURSEVI:v10p170/r10.claim: Ibn Masʿud says that whoever patiently brings goods from a Muslim city and sells them at the day's market price for God's reward is counted among the martyrs.
BURSEVI:v10p170/r10.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه أيما رجل جلب شيئا من مدينة من مدائن المسلمين صابرا محتسبا

MUQATIL:73:20/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:20/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:20/r1.claim: Adna means less: the Prophet and believers prayed part of the night, including half or a third.
MUQATIL:73:20/r1.anchor: { أدنى } يعني أقل { من ثلثي الليل }

MUQATIL:73:20/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:20/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:20/r2.claim: Early Muslims stood in prayer for half or a third of the night for a year before the five prayers were prescribed; the burden became difficult, so God granted relief.
MUQATIL:73:20/r2.anchor: وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين كانوا يقومون في أول الإسلام

MUQATIL:73:20/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:20/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:20/r3.claim: God knows people cannot precisely calculate the first two-thirds, half, or third of the night.
MUQATIL:73:20/r3.anchor: ولا نصف الليل، ولا ثلث الليل، { فتاب عليكم }

MUQATIL:73:20/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:20/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:20/r4.claim: God's turning toward them means he eased the earlier command to rise for most of the night.
MUQATIL:73:20/r4.anchor: { فتاب عليكم } يعني فتجاوز عنكم في التخفيف بعد قوله: { قم الليل إلا قليلا }

MUQATIL:73:20/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:20/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:20/r5.claim: The concession tells them to recite what is easy from the Quran in prayer, without fixing an amount, in the five daily prayers.
MUQATIL:73:20/r5.anchor: { فاقرءوا ما تيسر من القرآن } عليكم في الصلاة { علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى }

MUQATIL:73:20/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:20/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:20/r6.claim: The sick cannot sustain nighttime prayer; travelers seeking provision and fighters in God's path likewise cannot manage it, so the verse grants relief after strictness.
MUQATIL:73:20/r6.anchor: { علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى } فلا يطيوقون قيام الليل لله { وآخرون يضربون في الأرض } تجارا

MUQATIL:73:20/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:20/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:20/r7.claim: They must complete the five prayers and pay the obligatory zakat from their property.
MUQATIL:73:20/r7.anchor: { وأقيموا الصلاة } يعني وأتموا الصلوات الخمس، وأعطوا الزكاة المفروضة من أموالكم

MUQATIL:73:20/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:20/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:20/r8.claim: The night vigil was abrogated for believers but remained obligatory for the Prophet; the first and last portions of the surah were separated by a year, until prayer and zakat became obligatory.
MUQATIL:73:20/r8.anchor: فنسخ قيام الليل على المؤمنين، وثبت قيام الليل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكان بين أول هذه السورة وآخرها سنة حتى فرضت الصلوات الخمس، والزكاة

MUQATIL:73:20/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:20/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:20/r9.claim: Lending God a good loan means voluntary giving with a willing heart, counted as voluntary charity after the obligatory payment.
MUQATIL:73:20/r9.anchor: يعني التطوع { قرضا حسنا } يعني بالحسن طيبة بها نفسه يحتسبها تطوعا بعد الفريضة

MUQATIL:73:20/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:20/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:20/r10.claim: Good sent ahead includes obligatory or voluntary alms; its reward with God is better and greater than what people gave.
MUQATIL:73:20/r10.anchor: يعني من صدقة فريضة كانت أو تطوعا، يقول: { تجدوه عند الله هو خيرا } ثوابا عند الله في التقديم

MUQATIL:73:20/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:20/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:20/r11.claim: Seek forgiveness for sins; God forgives those who ask and is merciful in granting this concession.
MUQATIL:73:20/r11.anchor: من الذنوب { إن الله غفور } لكم عند الاستغفار إذا استغفرتموه { رحيم } [آية: 20] حين رخص لكم بالتوبة

BURSEVI:v10p171/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171/r1.claim: Given the concessions and competing demands, believers should recite as much Quran as is manageable without imposing hardship.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r1.anchor: فاقرأوا ما تيسر من القرآن من غير تحمل المشاق فإن قيل

BURSEVI:v10p171/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171/r2.claim: The Companions were burdened by keeping to the prescribed measure of night prayer, not by night worship itself; it may also have felt heavy before the concession.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r2.anchor: الثقلة لم تكن في قيامه بل في محافظة القدر الفروض كما سبق

BURSEVI:v10p171/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171/r3.claim: He says night worship came easily to many Successors, naming Abu Hanifa, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Fudayl ibn Iyad, Abu Sulayman al-Darani, Malik ibn Dinar, and Ali ibn Bakkar.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r3.anchor: أبو حنيفة وسعيد بن المسيب وفضيل بن عياش وأبو سليمان اداراني ومالك بن دينار وعلي بن بكار

BURSEVI:v10p171/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r4.speaker: علي بن بكار الشامي
BURSEVI:v10p171/r4.claim: Ali ibn Bakkar said that for forty years nothing grieved him except the arrival of dawn, which ended his night vigil.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r4.anchor: قال علي بن بكار الشامي منذ أربعين سنة لم يحزني شيء إلا طلوع الفجر

BURSEVI:v10p171/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r5.speaker: عثمان وتميم الداري
BURSEVI:v10p171/r5.claim: The author notes that Uthman and Tamim al-Dari each completed the Quran in one rakah.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r5.anchor: ثم كان من ر بعضهم إنه ختم القرآن في ركعة واحدة كعثمان وتميم الداري رضي الله عنهما

BURSEVI:v10p171/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p171/r6.claim: One reported interpretation takes the zakat here as zakat al-fitr, since Mecca had no other zakat then, and says it became obligatory later.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r6.anchor: وقيل هي زكاة الفطر إذا لم يكن بمكة زكاة غيرها وإنما وجبت بعدها

BURSEVI:v10p171/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r7.speaker: من فسرها بالزكاة المفروضة
BURSEVI:v10p171/r7.claim: Those who read this as obligatory zakat regard the sura's final passage as Medinan, treating its ruling as one whose legislation followed its revelation.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r7.anchor: ومن فسرها بالزكاة المفروضة جعل آخر السورة مدنيا

BURSEVI:v10p171/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171/r8.claim: The later prescription and payment of zakat signals that God would fulfill His promise to the Messenger, establish His religion, and make it prevail.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r8.anchor: ففيه دلالة على أنه سينجز وعده لرسوله ويقيم دينه ويظهره حتى تفرض الزكاة وتؤدي

BURSEVI:v10p171/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171/r9.claim: Qard literally denotes cutting; a loan is so called because the money is cut off from its owner's property subject to repayment in kind.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r9.anchor: والقرض ضرب من القطع وسمى ما يدفع إلى الإنسان من المال بشرط رد بدله قرضا

BURSEVI:v10p171/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171/r10.claim: The good loan means voluntary charitable spending, distinct from obligatory duties whose repayment is assured; the command urges supererogatory giving.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r10.anchor: أريد به الانفاقات في سبيل الخيرات غير المفروض فإنها كالفرض الذي لا خلف في أدائه وفيه حث على التطوع

BURSEVI:v10p171/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r11.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p171/r11.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that wealth carries a due beyond zakat; giving it well means choosing excellent, useful property for the poor with sincere intention.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r11.anchor: وهو إخراجها من أطيب الأموال وأكثرها نفعا للفقراء بحسن النية

BURSEVI:v10p171/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171/r12.claim: The zakat command requires giving, whereas the loan command additionally qualifies the gift as good; calling charity a loan likens its return to repayment with increase.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r12.anchor: تسمية الإنفاق لوجه الله أقراضا استعارة تشبيها له بالإقراض من يحث إنما أنفقه يعود عليه مع زيادة

BURSEVI:v10p171/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r13.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p171/r13.claim: Some interpret the loan as reciting glorification, praise, the testimony of divine unity, and takbir, as well as spending in God's cause, following Umar's explanation.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r13.anchor: وقال بعضهم هو قول سبحان الله والحمد ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر والنفقة في سبيل الله كما قال عمر رضي الله عنه

BURSEVI:v10p171/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171/r14.claim: Another explanation includes spending on one's household; a hadith says food a Muslim gives himself and his family counts as charity when done with good intention.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r14.anchor: أو النفقة على الأهل وفي الحديث ما أطعم المسلم نفسه وأهل بيته فهو له صدقة أي يؤجر عليه بحسن نيته

BURSEVI:v10p171/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171/r15.speaker: الغزالي
BURSEVI:v10p171/r15.claim: Al-Ghazali transmits al-Baqillani's view that claiming complete freedom from self-interest is unbelief, since freedom from motive is a divine prerogative; apparent God-directed action may conceal a motive.
BURSEVI:v10p171/r15.anchor: روى الامام الغزالي رحمه الله عن القاضي الباقلاني إن ادعاء البراءة من الغرض بالكلية كفر لأن التنزه خاصة إلهية

BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r1.claim: The claim about hidden motives concerns people still on the path of spiritual aspiration; those annihilated from will, the most complete, have no motive, a state known only to their peers or through God's disclosure.
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r1.anchor: هذا وارد على أهل الإرادة وإما أهل الفناء عن الإرادة وهم أل النهاية الأكملون فلا غرض لهم أصلا

BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r2.claim: Whatever good a person sends ahead, whether already mentioned or not, will be found with God as a better and greater reward than what is deferred until a deathbed bequest.
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r2.anchor: أي خير كان مما ذكر وما لم يذكر

BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r3.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r3.claim: Kashf al-Asrar says the reward found with God is better than worldly enjoyment and greater in recompense, since God rewards believers without reckoning.
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r3.anchor: وفي كشف الأسرار تجدوا ثوابه خيرا لكم من متاع الدنيا وأعظم أجرا لأن الله يعطي المؤمن أجره بغير حساب

BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r4.claim: On the main parsing, khayran is the second object of تجدوا after the pronoun object; aʿẓama coordinates with it, and ajran is a specification of the subject relation.
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r4.anchor: قوله خيرا ثاني مفعولي تجدوا وهو تأكيد للمفعول الأول لتجدوه وفصل بينه وبين المفعول الثاني

BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r5.claim: Another grammarian takes وجد here as 'to find' rather than 'to know,' hence it governs one object and khayran is circumstantial from the pronoun.
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم المشهور إن وجد إذا كان بمعنى صادف يتعدى إلى مفعول واحد وهو ههنا بمعناه

BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r6.claim: Ajr denotes the return or recompense yielded by an action, whether worldly or in the hereafter.
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r6.anchor: والأجر ما يعود من ثواب العمل دنيويا كان أو أخرويا

BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r7.claim: A Prophetic report says every person arrives according to what he sent ahead and regrets what he left behind.
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث اعلموا إن كل امرىء على ما قدم قادم وعلى ما خلف نادم

BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r8.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r8.claim: At death, the person asks what he left behind while the angels point to what he sent ahead.
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r8.anchor: وعنه عليه اسلام إن العبد إذا مات قال الإنسان ما خلف وقالت الملائكة ما قدم

BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r9.speaker: عمر رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r9.claim: Passing al-Baqi cemetery, Umar greeted its dead and said their wives had remarried, homes occupied, and wealth divided; a voice replied that what was sent ahead was found, what was spent profited, and what was left behind was lost.
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r9.anchor: ومر عمر رضي الله عنه ببقيع الغرقداى مقبرة المذدينة لأنها كانت منبت الغرقد

BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r10.claim: A Persian couplet exhorts readers to send good ahead before death because there is no route to lasting life.
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r10.anchor: قدم لنفسك قبل موتك صالحا واعمل فليس إلى الخلود سبيل

BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r11.speaker: عمر رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r11.claim: When Umar gave a poor man dates mixed with milk, he answered critics that the poor man's Lord knew the value of the gift.
BURSEVI:v10p171#2/r11.anchor: فقال عمر لكن رب المسكين يدري ما هو

BURSEVI:v10p172/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p172/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p172/r1.claim: A Persian couplet says to cast good into the water: even if the fish does not know, God knows, supporting hidden charitable giving.
BURSEVI:v10p172/r1.anchor: تونيكى كن بآب اندازاى شاه اكر ما هي نداند داند الله

BURSEVI:v10p172/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p172/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p172/r2.claim: Seek God's forgiveness continually, at every time and in every condition, because people seldom escape negligence or shortcoming.
BURSEVI:v10p172/r2.anchor: سلوا الله المغفرة لذنوبكم في جميع أوقاتكم وكافة أحوالكم فإن الإنسان قلما يخلوه عن تفريط

BURSEVI:v10p172/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p172/r3.speaker: السلف الصالح
BURSEVI:v10p172/r3.claim: The righteous early Muslims prayed until dawn, then sat seeking forgiveness until the dawn prayer.
BURSEVI:v10p172/r3.anchor: وكان السلف الصالح يصلون إلى طلوع الفجر ثم يجلسون للاستغفار إلى صلاة الصبح

BURSEVI:v10p172/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p172/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p172/r4.claim: He recommends formulas of forgiveness drawn from Quranic divine names, including 'I ask forgiveness of God, for God is Oft-Returning' and 'O Lord, forgive and show mercy.'
BURSEVI:v10p172/r4.anchor: واستحب الاستغفار على الأسماء من القرآن مثل أن يقول استغفر الله إنه كان توابا استغفر الله إن الله غفور رحيم

BURSEVI:v10p172/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p172/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p172/r5.claim: Ghafur forgives sins other than associating partners with God, while Rahim turns bad deeds into good deeds.
BURSEVI:v10p172/r5.anchor: يغفر ما دون أن يشرك به

BURSEVI:v10p172/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p172/r6.speaker: عين المعاني
BURSEVI:v10p172/r6.claim: Ayn al-Maʻani glosses Ghafur as covering the failings of the ignorant and negligent, and Rahim as easing their burden.
BURSEVI:v10p172/r6.anchor: وفي عين المعاني غفور يستر على أهل الجهل والتقصير رحيم يخفف عن أهل الجهل والتوفير

BURSEVI:v10p172/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p172/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p172/r7.claim: Knowing that God's forgiveness is not daunted by any sin should make a person ask forgiveness more often; the request is sound with humility, complete with repentance, and empty without either.
BURSEVI:v10p172/r7.anchor: ثم إن كان مع الانكسار فهو صحيح وإن كان مع التوبة فهو كامل وإن كان عريا عنهما فهو باطل

BURSEVI:v10p172/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p172/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p172/r8.claim: He says writing the master formula of forgiveness and giving it to someone struggling to die will loosen the person's tongue and ease death, a remedy he says has been tried repeatedly.
BURSEVI:v10p172/r8.anchor: ومن كتب سيد الاستغفار وجرعه لمن صعب عليه الموت انطلق لسانه وسهل عليه الموت وقد جرب مرارا

BURSEVI:v10p172/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p172/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p172/r9.claim: He gives the master formula: acknowledge God as Lord and creator, affirm servitude and covenant, seek refuge from one's deeds, confess favors and sin, and ask forgiveness from God alone.
BURSEVI:v10p172/r9.anchor: اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت خلقتني وأنا عبدك وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما استطعت

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r1.claim: Adnā means less; “nearer” is used metaphorically because shorter distance leaves fewer intervening spaces.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r1.anchor: اقل فاستعير الادنى وهو الأقرب لأن المسافة بين الشيئين إذا دنت قل ما بينهما من الاحياز

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r2.claim: The lām in thuluthay is read with ḍamma, except by Hishām.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r3.claim: The dual and third fractions are accusative for Makkan and Kufan readers, linked to adnā; those reading them genitive link them to “two thirds.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r3.anchor: منصوبان عطف على أدنى مكي وكوفي ومن جرهما عطف على ثلثي

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r4.claim: “A group” is coordinated with the pronoun in “you rise”; the coordination needs no emphatic pronoun because intervening words separate them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r4.anchor: عطف على الضمير في تقوم وجاز بلا توكيد لوجود الفاصل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r5.claim: A group of the Prophet's companions also rose for that amount of the night.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r5.anchor: أي ويقوم ذلك المقدار جماعة من أصحابك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r6.claim: Only God can calculate the night and day and know their hours; placing His name first signals His exclusive power to measure them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r6.anchor: أي لا يقدر على تقدير الليل والنهار ولا يعلم مقادير ساعاتهما إلا الله وحده

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r7.claim: After they stood until their feet swelled, God knew they could not sustain these measures without severe hardship.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r7.anchor: ثم انهم قاموا حتى انتفخت اقدامهم فنزل ﴿ علم أن لن تحصوه ﴾ لن تطيقوا قيامه على هذه المقادير إلا بشدة ومشقة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r8.claim: God's turning toward them means He eased the burden and removed the obligation of night vigil.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r8.anchor: فخفف عليكم واسقط عنكم فرض قيام الليل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r9.claim: Reciting what is easy in prayer is obligatory, while reciting it outside prayer is recommended.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r9.anchor: في الصلاة والأمر للوجوب أي وفي غيرها والأمر للندب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r10.claim: This means what is available and not difficult for you.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r10.anchor: ﴿ ما تيسر ﴾ عليكم ﴿ من القرآن ﴾ روى أبو حنيفة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r11.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that reciting one hundred verses at night keeps one from being counted among the heedless, and two hundred makes one among the devout.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r11.anchor: روى أبو حنيفة عن أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه قال من قرأ مائة آية في ليلة لم يكتب من الغافلين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r12.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r12.claim: Some interpret “the Qurʾān” here as prayer, because recitation is one of its pillars; the command is to pray what night prayer is manageable.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r12.anchor: وقيل أراد بالقرآن الصلاة لأنه بعض أركانها أي فصلوا ما تيسر عليكم ولم يتعذر من صلاة الليل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r13.claim: This command abrogated the first night-prayer command, and the five daily prayers later abrogated it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r13.anchor: وهذا ناسخ للاول ثم نسخ هذا بالصلوات الخمس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r14.claim: The easing is explained by the hardship night vigil would impose on the sick, travelers, and those fighting in God's path.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r14.anchor: ثم بين الحكمة في النسخ وهي تعذر القيام على المرضى والمسافرين والمجاهدين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r15.claim: “An” is lightened from the emphatic particle, the sīn replaces its shadda, and its subject is omitted.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r15.anchor: أي أنه مخففة من الثقيلة والسين بدل من تخفيفها وحذف اسمها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r16.claim: Travelers seek God's bounty through trade or the pursuit of knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r16.anchor: يسافرون ﴿ يبتغون ﴾ حال من ضمير يضربون ﴿ من فضل الله ﴾ رزقه بالتجارة أو طلب العلم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r17.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r17.claim: God places the fighter and the lawful earner on equal footing, because earning lawful provision is jihad.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r17.anchor: سوى بين المجاهد والمكتسب لأن كسب الحلال جهاد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r18.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r18.speaker: ابن مسعود
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r18.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a patient, reward-seeking merchant who brings goods to a Muslim town and sells at that day's price is counted with the martyrs before God.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r18.anchor: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه ايما رجل جلب شيئا إلى المدينة من مدائن المسلمين صابرا محتسبا فباعه بسعر يومه كان عند الله من الشهداء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r19.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r19.speaker: ابن عمر
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r19.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that, after death in God's cause, he prefers dying while traveling to earn God's bounty.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r19.anchor: وقال ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما ماخلق الله موته أموتها بعد القتل في سبيل الله أحب إلي من أن أموت بين شعبتي رجل أضرب في الأرض ابتغى من فضل الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r20.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r20.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r20.claim: The command to recite what is manageable is repeated because the Companions were extremely scrupulous.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r21.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r21.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r21.claim: The prayer to be established is the obligatory prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r21.anchor: ﴿ وأقيموا الصلاة ﴾ المفروضة ﴿ وآتوا الزكاة ﴾ الواجبة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r22.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r22.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r22.claim: The zakat to be paid is obligatory alms.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r22.anchor: ﴿ وآتوا الزكاة ﴾ الواجبة ﴿ وأقرضوا الله ﴾ بالنوافل والقرض لغة القطع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r23.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r23.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r23.claim: Lending to God means voluntary good works; the root of qarḍ is cutting, as the giver cuts that amount from personal wealth and gives it away.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r23.anchor: بالنوافل والقرض لغة القطع فالمقرض بقطع ذلك القدر من ماله فيدفعه إلى غيره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r24.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r24.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r24.claim: The loan is attributed to God so donors do not lord it over the poor: the poor assist them in worship, so the donor owes them gratitude rather than claiming a favor.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r24.anchor: وإنما أضافة إلى نفسه لئلا يمن على الفقير فيما يتصدق به عليه وهذا لأن الفقير معاون له في تلك القربة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r25.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r25.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r25.claim: A good loan is given from lawful wealth and with sincerity.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r26.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r26.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r26.claim: What people find with God is the reward of their good deeds; the clause answers the conditional.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r27.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r27.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r27.claim: “He is” is an inflectional separator; it is allowed although not between two definite nouns because the comparative resembles a definite noun, being unable to take the article.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r27.anchor: فالمفعول الثاني لتجدوه خيرا وهو فصل وجاز وإن لم يقع بين معرفتين لأن أفعل ما أشبه المعرفة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r28.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r28.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r28.claim: What is sent ahead is better than what is left behind, and brings greater, more abundant reward.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r28.anchor: مما خلفتم وتركتم فالمفعول الثاني لتجدوه خيرا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r29.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r29.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r29.claim: Ask forgiveness for sins and for falling short in good works.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r29.anchor: واستغفروا من السيآت والتقصير في الحسنات

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r30.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r30.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r30.claim: God conceals the sins and shortcomings of those who sin.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r31.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r31.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r31.claim: God is merciful by easing matters for those who exert themselves in worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p292#5/r31.anchor: يخفف عن أهل الجهد والتوفير وهو على ما يشاء قدير

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the Prophet and Companions prayed at night for ten years before verse 20 came down and eased the burden.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: مكث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه عشر سنين يقومون الليل،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r1.claim: Verse 20 explains the earlier command to stand at night and abrogates its obligatory status, as discussed above; taqūmu means “you pray” and adnā means “less.”
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r1.anchor: هذه الآية تفسير لقوله تعالى: { قم الليل إلا قليلا * نصفه أو انقص منه قليلا * أو زد عليه } كما تقدم، وهي الناسخة

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r2.speaker: ابن السميقع وأبو حيوة وهشام
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqa, Abū Ḥaywa, and Hishām in the Syrian reading tradition use a sukūn on the lām of thuluthay.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميقع وأبو حيوة وهشام عن أهل الشام { ثلثي } بإسكان اللام.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r3.speaker: قراءة العامة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r3.claim: The common genitive reading coordinates “half” and “third” with “two-thirds”: stand less than two-thirds, less than half, or less than a third; Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim prefer it.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r3.anchor: { ونصفه وثلثه } بالخفض قراءة العامة عطفا على «ثلثي» المعنى: تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r4.speaker: ابن كثير والكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr and the Kūfans read “half” and “third” in the accusative, coordinating them with “less”: stand less than two-thirds, or stand half or a third.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير والكوفيون «ونصفه وثلثه» بالنصب عطفا على «أدنى» التقدير: تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ prefers the accusative because the verse first says “less than two-thirds” and then gives the actual lesser amounts, half and a third.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r5.anchor: قال الفراء: وهو أشبه بالصواب لأنه قال أقل من الثلثين، ثم ذكر نفس القلة لا أقل من القلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r6.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r6.claim: Al-Qushayrī suggests they could regularly manage a third or half and sometimes more, but the burden of two-thirds kept them from attaining it.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r6.anchor: القشيري: وعلى هذه القراءة يحتمل أنهم كانوا يصيبون الثلث والنصف لخفة القيام عليهم بذلك القدر،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r7.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r7.claim: Al-Qushayrī also suggests they were commanded to pray half the night, with permission to increase toward two-thirds or decrease toward one-third.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أنهم أمروا بقيام نصف الليل، ورخص لهم في الزيادة والنقصان، فكانوا ينتهون في الزيادة إلى قريب من الثلثين،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r8.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r8.claim: A further possibility from al-Qushayrī is a prescribed half, ranging from one-third to two-thirds; some maintained it and others left it until abrogation.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أنهم قدر لهم النصف وأنقص إلى الثلث، والزيادة إلى الثلثين، وكان فيهم من يفي بذلك،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r9.claim: Some said God obligated one quarter of the night and worshippers fell short of it; al-Qurṭubī dismisses this as arbitrary assertion.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: إنما افترض الله عليهم الربع، وكانوا ينقصون من الربع. وهذا القول تحكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r10.claim: God knows the exact measures of night and day, whereas people estimate through effort and may be mistaken.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r10.anchor: أي يعلم مقادير الليل والنهار على حقائقها، وأنتم تعلمون بالتحري والاجتهاد الذي يقع فيه الخطأ.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r11.claim: The phrase means people cannot know the exact measure or fulfill it; an alternative says they cannot endure night prayer, but the first is stronger because the whole night was never imposed.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r11.anchor: وقيل: أي لن تطيقوا قيام الليل. والأول أصح فإن قيام الليل ما فرض كله قط.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r12.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r12.claim: Muqātil and others report that the initial command burdened the worshippers: unsure of the fractions, they stood until morning, fearing an error, until their feet swelled and faces paled; God then showed mercy and eased it.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r12.anchor: قال مقاتل وغيره: لما نزلت { قم الليل إلا قليلا * نصفه أو انقص منه قليلا * أو زد عليه } شق ذلك عليهم،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r13.claim: The particle an is a lightened form of the emphatic particle; exact calculation was beyond them, since exceeding the measure would burden them and falling short would distress them.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r13.anchor: و «أن» مخففة من الثقيلة أي علم أنكم لن تحصوه لأنكم إن زدتم ثقل عليكم، واحتجتم إلى تكليف ما ليس فرضا،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r14.claim: Fatā ʿalaykum can mean God pardoned them, implying they had left some of what was commanded; it can also mean He turned from imposing the prayer when they could not bear it.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r14.anchor: أي فعاد عليكم بالعفو، وهذا يدل على أنه كان فيهم في ترك بعض ما أمر به. وقيل: أي فتاب عليكم من فرض القيام

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r15.claim: Since tawba means return, the phrase describes a return from heavy obligation to relief and from hardship to ease.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20/r15.anchor: وأصل التوبة الرجوع كما تقدم فالمعنى رجع لكم من تثقيل إلى تخفيف، ومن عسر إلى يسر.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r1.claim: Another gloss says God creates night and day in measured proportions, as in 25:2; Ibn al-ʿArabī says created measure has no legal consequence by itself, though God attaches obligations to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: معنى { والله يقدر الليل والنهار } يخلقهما مقدرين كقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says created measure itself carries no ruling; God connects to it whichever duties He wills.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r2.anchor: ابن العربي: تقدير الخلقة لا يتعلق به حكم، وإنما يربط الله به ما يشاء من وظائف التكليف.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r3.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r3.claim: One view takes the command literally as Qurʾān recitation during night prayer; al-Suddī specifies one hundred verses.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says someone who recites one hundred verses in a night will not have the Qurʾān plead against him.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r4.anchor: الحسن: من قرأ مائة آية في ليلة لم يحاجه القرآن.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r5.speaker: كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r5.claim: Kaʿb says one who recites one hundred verses at night is recorded among the devout; al-Qurṭubī prefers this report’s view.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r5.anchor: وقال كعب: من قرأ في ليلة مائة آية

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r6.speaker: سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r6.claim: Saʿīd says the amount is fifty verses.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r7.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r7.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr says ten verses keep a worshipper from being counted heedless, one hundred make him devout, and one thousand make him among the muqaṇṭarīn; al-Qurṭubī cites it to support Kaʿb’s hundred-verse view.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r7.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام: " من قام بعشر آيات لم يكتب من الغافلين، ومن قام بمائة آية كتب من القانتين،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r8.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r8.claim: A second view takes “recite” to mean “pray,” since prayer is called Qurʾān, as in the expression for the dawn prayer at 17:78; Ibn al-ʿArabī says this better fits the subject of the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r8.anchor: ابن العربي: وهو الأصح لأنه عن الصلاة أخبر، وإليها يرجع القول.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r9.claim: Al-Qurṭubī prefers actual recitation because it follows the apparent wording; taking it as prayer is figurative, naming the whole act by one of its parts.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r9.anchor: قلت: الأول أصح حملا للخطاب على ظاهر اللفظ، والقول الثاني مجاز فإنه من تسمية الشيء ببعض ما هو من أعماله.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r10.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r10.claim: Some scholars say this command abrogated the fixed night standing, including its half-night amount and permitted increase or decrease.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r10.anchor: قال بعض العلماء: قوله تعالى: { فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه } نسخ قيام الليل ونصفه، والنقصان من النصف والزيادة عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r11.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r11.claim: Those scholars offer two possibilities: this command imposed a new duty replacing the old one, or it was itself later abrogated by 17:79, where night vigil is called a voluntary extra for the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r11.anchor: ثم احتمل قول الله عز وجل: { فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه } معنيين أحدهما أن يكون فرضا ثانيا

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r12.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r12.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says Sunnah must resolve the two possibilities and finds that the Prophet’s Sunnah establishes no obligatory prayer beyond the five daily prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r12.anchor: قال الشافعي: فكان الواجب طلب الاستدلال بالسنة على أحد المعنيين، فوجدنا سنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تدل على أن لا واجب من الصلاة إلا الخمس.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r13.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r13.claim: Al-Qushayrī says the well-known view is that night prayer was abrogated for the community but remained obligatory for the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r13.anchor: قال القشيري أبو نصر: والمشهور أن نسخ قيام الليل كان في حق الأمة، وبقيت الفريضة في حق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r14.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r14.claim: Another view reported by al-Qushayrī says the fixed amount was abrogated while the underlying obligation remained.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#2/r14.anchor: ثم احتمل قول الله عز وجل: { فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه } معنيين أحدهما أن يكون فرضا ثانيا

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r1.speaker: قوم (مذهب الحسن)
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r1.claim: By analogy with the obligatory minimum of sacrificial offering in 2:196, some held that a small amount of night prayer remained obligatory; this is Hasan's school.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r1.anchor: فالهدي لا بد منه، كذلك لم يكن بد من صلاة الليل، ولكن فوض قدره إلى اختيار المصلي، وعلى هذا فقد قال قوم:

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r2.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r2.claim: Al-Shafi'i held that the obligation of night prayer was abrogated altogether, so it is not obligatory.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: نسخ بالكلية، فلا تجب صلاة الليل أصلا وهو مذهب الشافعي.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r3.claim: The remaining obligation may have applied to the Prophet alone, with its amount left to his choice.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r3.anchor: ولعل الفريضة التي بقيت في حق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هي هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r4.claim: On the view that night prayer is no longer obligatory, the command means to recite and pray if one wishes and finds it easy.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r4.anchor: معناه اقرؤوا إن تيسر عليكم ذلك، وصلوا إن شئتم.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r5.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r5.claim: Some held that the complete abrogation also covered the Prophet, and that calling the prayer a nafl means a genuinely voluntary act.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r5.anchor: وصار قوم إلى أن النسخ بالكلية تقرر في حق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أيضا، فما كانت صلاة الليل واجبة عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r6.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r6.claim: One account says the required amount was first abrogated, then the remaining duty was ended by the prescribed prayer times; extra prayers beyond the five are voluntary.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r6.anchor: ومن قال: نسخ المقدار وبقي أصل وجوب قيام الليل ثم نسخ، فهذا النسخ الثاني وقع ببيان مواقيت الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r7.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r7.claim: Another account makes 17:79 the abrogating command, addressed to the Prophet and the community, as the original night-prayer command was general too.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r7.anchor: وقيل: وقع النسخ بقوله تعالى: { ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك } والخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r8.claim: Some say the duty lasted beyond the Hijra and was abrogated in Medina, since fighting was prescribed there; on that account the Meccan prayer-time verses preceded abrogation by 17:79.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r8.anchor: وقد قيل: إن فريضة الله امتدت إلى ما بعد الهجرة، ونسخت بالمدينة لقوله تعالى: { علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas said that when the Messenger arrived, the verse ended the obligation of night prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نسخ قول الله تعالى: { إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم }

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r10.claim: The verse explains the easing: illness, travel for trade, and campaigning could make night prayer difficult and risk missing prayer, so God lightened the duty for all.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r10.anchor: بين سبحانه علة تخفيف قيام الليل، فإن الخلق منهم المريض، ويشق عليهم قيام الليل

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r11.claim: Here أن is the lightened form of أنَّ, meaning “He knew that it would happen.”
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r11.anchor: و «أن» في «أن سيكون» مخففة من الثقيلة أي علم أنه سيكون.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r12.claim: The verse places lawful earners who support themselves and their families and do good alongside fighters, indicating that earning money can rank like jihad.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#3/r12.anchor: سوى الله تعالى في هذه الآية بين درجة المجاهدين والمكتسبين المال الحلال للنفقة على نفسه وعياله،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r1.claim: The Prophet said that a food importer who carries provisions between towns and sells at that day's price has the rank of martyrs with God.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r1.anchor: ما من جالب يجلب طعاما من بلد إلى بلد فيبيعه بسعر يومه إلا كانت منزلته عند الله منزلة الشهداء

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r2.claim: Ibn Masud said a patient trader who brings goods to a Muslim city and sells at the day's price earns the rank of martyrs with God.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r2.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: أيما رجل جلب شيئا إلى مدينة من مدائن المسلمين صابرا محتسبا،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r3.claim: Ibn Umar said that, after dying in God's cause, he preferred no death to dying on his saddle while travelling to seek God's bounty.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: ما خلق الله موتة أموتها بعد الموت في سبيل الله أحب إلي من الموت بين شعبتي رحلي،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r4.speaker: طاوس
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r4.claim: Tawus likened caring for a widow and a poor person to fighting in God's path.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r4.anchor: وقال طاوس: الساعي على الأرملة والمسكين كالمجاهد في سبيل الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r5.speaker: بعض السلف
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r5.claim: A pious merchant instructed his agent to sell grain on reaching Basra; after the agent delayed for a higher price, the owner ordered all proceeds given to Basra's poor, fearing hoarding.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r5.anchor: وعن بعض السلف أنه كان بواسط، فجهز سفينة حنطة إلى البصرة، وكتب إلى وكيله: بع الطعام يوم تدخل البصرة،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r6.claim: Ibn Umar found a Meccan youth who regularly attended the mosque selling food; he urged him toward livestock, saying food sellers welcome scarcity while herders welcome rain.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r6.anchor: ويروي أن غلاما من أهل مكة كان ملازما للمسجد، فافتقده ابن عمر،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r7.claim: The command means to pray whatever is possible: an accessible amount of night prayer was first required, then abrogated when the five daily prayers were prescribed.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r7.anchor: أي صلوا ما أمكن فأوجب الله من صلاة الليل ما تيسر، ثم نسخ ذلك بإيجاب الصلوات الخمس

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r8.speaker: البخاري وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r8.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reports that some, including al-Bukhari, held that this verse established a two-rakʿa night-prayer duty.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r8.anchor: قال ابن العربي وقد قال قوم: إن فرض قيام الليل سن في ركعتين من هذه الآية قاله البخاري وغيره،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r9.claim: A Prophetic report says Satan ties three knots at a sleeper's head; remembrance, ablution, and prayer untie them, while the sleeper otherwise wakes sluggish and ill-tempered.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#4/r9.anchor: يعقد الشيطان على قافية رأس أحدكم إذا هو نام ثلاث عقد، يضرب على كل عقدة مكانها: عليك ليل طويل فارقد

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r1.claim: In Samura ibn Jundub's vision report, a man whose head was crushed had taken the Quran and rejected it and slept through an obligatory prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الرؤيا قال: «أما الذي يثلغ رأسه بالحجر فإنه يأخذ القرآن فيرفضه

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says the Prophet described a man who slept all night as having Satan urinate in his ears.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r2.anchor: وحديث عبد الله بن مسعود قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reads unqualified references to prayer in these reports as the obligatory prayer, which undercuts the claim that they establish obligatory night prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r3.anchor: فقال ابن العربي: فهذه أحاديث مقتضية حمل مطلق الصلاة على المكتوبة فيحمل المطلق على المقيد لاحتماله له،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r4.claim: The Prophet told Abdullah ibn Amr not to imitate a man who used to pray at night and then stopped.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r4.anchor: وفي الصحيح واللفظ للبخاري: قال عبد الله بن عمرو: وقال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r5.claim: Abdullah ibn Umar dreamed angels took him toward Hell; after Hafsa relayed it, the Prophet called him a good man who should pray at night.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#5/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: كان الرجل في حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا رأي رؤيا

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r1.claim: Ibn Umar thereafter slept little; the author says that if missing night prayer were sinful, the angel would not have reassured him.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r1.anchor: فكان بعد لا ينام من الليل إلا قليلا فلو كان ترك القيام معصية لما قال له الملك: لم ترع.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r2.speaker: مالك والشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r2.claim: Malik and al-Shafi'i require reciting the Fatiha in prayer; neither leaving it for another passage nor reciting only part suffices.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r2.anchor: فقال مالك والشافعي: فاتحة الكتاب لا يجزيء العدول عنها، ولا الاقتصار على بعضها،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa requires at least one verse from anywhere in the Quran; another report from him sets the minimum at three verses, the shortest surah's length.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r3.anchor: وقدره أبو حنيفة بآية واحدة، من أي القرآن كانت. وعنه ثلاث آيات لأنها أقل سورة.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r4.claim: The author endorses Malik and al-Shafi'i's requirement of reciting the Fatiha in prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r4.anchor: والصحيح ما ذهب إليه مالك والشافعي، على ما بيناه في سورة «الفاتحة» أول الكتاب والحمد لله.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r5.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r5.claim: If this means Quran recitation outside prayer, al-Mawardi says the command may mean obligation or recommendation; most recommend it because a duty to recite would entail a duty to memorize.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r5.anchor: قال الماوردي: فعلى هذا يكون مطلق هذا الأمر محمولا على الوجوب، أو على الاستحباب دون الوجوب.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r6.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r6.claim: Another view makes Quran reading obligatory so a person encounters its inimitability, proofs of divine unity, and evidence for the messengers; memorization remains recommended, not obligatory.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r6.anchor: الثاني أنه محمول على الوجوب ليقف بقراءته على إعجازه، وما فيه من دلائل التوحيد وبعث الرسل،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r7.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says the amount meant is the whole Quran, which God has made easy for His servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r7.anchor: أحدها جميع القرآن لأن الله تعالى يسره على عباده قاله الضحاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r8.speaker: جوبير
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r8.claim: Juwair reports that the required amount is one third of the Quran.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r9.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r9.claim: Al-Suddi says the amount is two hundred verses.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says the amount is one hundred verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r10.anchor: الرابع مائة آية قاله ابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r11.speaker: أبو خالد الكناني
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r11.claim: Abu Khalid al-Kinani says the amount is three verses, the length of the shortest surah.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r11.anchor: الخامس ثلاث آيات كأقصر سورة قاله أبو خالد الكناني.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r12.claim: The prayer to be established is the five obligatory prayers at their appointed times.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r13.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r13.claim: Ikrima and Qatada understand zakat here as the obligatory alms due on one's property.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r13.anchor: الواجبة في أموالكم قاله عكرمة وقتادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r14.speaker: الحارث العكلي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r14.claim: Al-Harith al-Akli says this refers to the alms at the end of Ramadan, since wealth-zakat was prescribed later.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r14.anchor: وقال الحارث العكلي: صدقة الفطر لأن زكاة الأموال وجبت بعد ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r15.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r15.claim: Some interpret the command as voluntary charity.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r16.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r16.claim: Some interpret it as all acts of goodness.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r16.anchor: وقيل: كل أفعال الخير. وقال ابن عباس:

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets it as obedience to God and sincerity toward Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r17.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: طاعة الله والإخلاص له.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r18.claim: A good loan to God is spending wholesome wealth solely to seek God's approval.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#6/r18.anchor: القرض الحسن ما قصد به وجه الله تعالى خالصا من المال الطيب.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r1.claim: The author says the good-loan explanation was already given in Surat al-Hadid.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets the good loan as spending on one's family.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r2.anchor: وقال زيد ابن أسلم: القرض الحسن النفقة على الأهل.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r3.claim: Umar ibn al-Khattab interprets the good loan as spending in God's path.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r3.anchor: وقال عمر بن الخطاب: هو النفقة في سبيل الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r4.claim: The author notes that this wording also occurs in al-Baqara (2:110).
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله } «البقرة».

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r5.claim: Umar gave a poor man a dish of dates mixed with milk; when someone said the man would not know its value, Umar replied that the man's Lord knew.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r5.anchor: وروي عن عمر بن الخطاب أنه اتخذ حيسا يعني تمرا بلبن فجاءه مسكين فأخذه ودفعه إليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r6.claim: Umar took the promise to mean that good sent ahead is better than what is left behind, inherited, or withheld through miserliness.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r6.anchor: وكأنه تأول { وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله هو خيرا } أي مما تركتم وخلفتم،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra says the greater reward is Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r7.anchor: { وأعظم أجرا } قال أبو هريرة: الجنة ويحتمل

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r8.claim: Alternatively, the reward is greater because each good deed is repaid tenfold.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون أعظم أجرا لإعطائه بالحسنة عشرا.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r9.claim: خيرا and أعظم are the second objects of تجدوه; هو is a separating word for Basran grammarians and an ʿimād support word for Kufans, with no syntactic case.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r9.anchor: ونصب «خيرا وأعظم» على المفعول الثاني ل «تجدوه» و «هو»: فصل عند البصريين، وعماد في قول الكوفيين، لا محل له من الإعراب.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r10.claim: أجرا is an accusative of specification (tamyiz).
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r10.anchor: و «هو»: فصل عند البصريين، وعماد في قول الكوفيين، لا محل له من الإعراب. و «أجرا» تمييز.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r11.claim: The command means to ask God to forgive one's sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r11.anchor: { واستغفروا الله } أي سلوه المغفرة لذنوبكم

QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r12.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says God forgives what preceded repentance and shows mercy to people afterward.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:20#7/r12.anchor: { إن الله غفور } لما كان قبل التوبة { رحيم } لكم بعدها قاله سعيد بن جبير.

RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r7.claim: An objection says the genitive reading in 73:20 means the Prophet rose for less than one third, apparently leaving a required third undone.
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r7.anchor: فمن قرأ نصفه وثلثه بالخفض كان المعنى أنك تقوم أقل من الثلثين

RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r8.claim: Al-Razi answers that people estimated a third by judgment and might fall slightly short of the exact divine measure, which explains the statement that they could not calculate it.
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r8.anchor: إنهم كانوا يقدرون الثلث بالاجتهاد ، فربما أخطأوا في ذلك الاجتهاد

RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r1.claim: Adnā, literally nearer, is used here for less: when two things are closer, fewer intervals lie between them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r1.anchor: وإنما استعير الأدنى وهو الأقرب للأقل لأن المسافة بين الشيئين إذا دنت قل ما بينهما

RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r2.claim: With the accusative reading, the phrase means the Prophet rises less than two thirds and also rises half and a third; with genitive, less than each of two thirds, half, and a third.
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r2.anchor: والمعنى أنك تقوم أقل من الثلثين وتقوم النصف

RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r3.claim: As explained under 73:2, this phrasing does not entail that the Prophet left an obligatory amount undone.
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r3.anchor: إنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان تاركا للواجب

RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r4.claim: The group with the Prophet refers to his companions, who also rose for the stated portion of the night.
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#3/r4.anchor: وهم أصحابك يقومون من الليل هذا المقدار المذكور

RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r1.claim: Only God knows the exact measures of the divisions of night and day.
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r1.anchor: يعني أن العالم بمقادير أجزاء الليل والنهار ليس إلا الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r2.claim: The pronoun refers to an implied verbal noun: you cannot calculate each portion of night and day exactly, nor secure the measure by caution without great hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r2.anchor: الضمير في { أن لن تحصوه } عائد إلى مصدر مقدر

RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r3.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r3.claim: Muqatil says people prayed all night because they feared failing to reach the amount of vigil imposed on them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل : كان الرجل يصلي الليل كله مخافة

RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r4.claim: Some cite لن تحصوه as evidence that people were commanded to do what they could not bear; al-Razi replies it means the task is difficult, not impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r4.anchor: احتج بعضهم على تكليف مالا يطاق

RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r5.claim: The rebuttal compares it to saying one cannot bear to look at someone when the intended sense is that the sight is burdensome.
RAZI-FULL:v30p164#4/r5.anchor: ما أطيق أن أنظر إلى فلان إذا استثقل النظر إليه

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r1.claim: Fatā ʿalaykum means God licensed them to leave the measured night vigil, like His pardon in 2:187.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r1.anchor: هو عبارة عن الترخيص في ترك القيام المقدر

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r2.claim: One view takes recitation to mean prayer, naming the whole by one of its parts, since Quranic recitation is part of prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r2.anchor: الصلاة لأن القراءة أحد أجزاء الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r3.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r3.claim: Al-Hasan specifies the prayer meant by the phrase as the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r3.anchor: قال الحسن : يعني في صلاة المغرب والعشاء

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r4.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r4.claim: Others say night vigil was abrogated in stages: first this verse replaced its obligation with an easier amount, then the five daily prayers replaced that duty.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r4.anchor: بل نسخ وجوب ذلك التهجد واكتفى بما تيسر منه

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r5.claim: The second main view takes the phrase as Quran recitation itself, for studying it and preventing it from being forgotten.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r5.anchor: قراءة القرآن بعينها والغرض منه دراسة القرآن ليحصل الأمن من النسيان

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r6.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r6.claim: One reported measure is a hundred verses; another says that reading a hundred verses earns the status of the devout.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r6.anchor: قيل : يقرأ مائة آية ، وقيل : من قرأ مائة آية كتب من القانتين

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r7.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r7.claim: Another view sets the amount at fifty verses.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r7.anchor: وقيل : خمسين آية ومنهم من قال

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r8.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r8.claim: Others consider a short surah sufficient because night vigil was reduced to remove hardship, and lengthy recitation would recreate hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r8.anchor: بل السورة القصيرة كافية ، لأن إسقاط التهجد إنما كان دفعا للحرج

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says night vigil ceased to be obligatory for the Prophet's companions and became voluntary, but remained obligatory for the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r9.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال : سقط عن أصحاب رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r10.claim: The easing is explained by illness and the demands on travelers seeking livelihood and fighters: these groups could not sustain the earlier night-vigil requirement.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r10.anchor: والمعنى لتعذر القيام على المرضى والضاربين في الأرض للتجارة والمجاهدين في سبيل الله

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r11.claim: The ill cannot manage night worship; travelers and fighters already perform strenuous daytime work, so little sleep would make hardship accumulate.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r11.anchor: فلو لم يناموا في الليل لتوالت أسباب المشقة عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r12.claim: The stated reason did not apply to the Prophet, whose daytime remained spacious according to 73:7, so the night-vigil obligation was not abrogated for him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r12.anchor: وهذا السبب ما كان موجودا في حق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r13.claim: The verse notably places fighters and lawful earners on equal footing.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r13.anchor: ومن لطائف هذه الآية أنه تعالى سوى بين المجاهدين والمسافرين للكسب الحلال

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r14.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that whoever patiently and devoutly brings goods to a Muslim city and sells at the day's price is counted by God among the martyrs.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r14.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود : ( أيما رجل جلب شيئا إلى مدينة من مدائن المسلمين

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r15.claim: The repeated command to recite what is easy reinforces the concession.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r15.anchor: ثم أعاد مرة أخرى قوله : { فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه } وذلك للتأكيد

RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r16.claim: The obligatory alms are understood as zakat; another view takes the reference as zakat al-fitr, since formal zakat was not yet prescribed in Mecca, and those reading it as obligatory zakat infer that the surah's ending is Medinan.
RAZI-FULL:v30p165/r16.anchor: وقيل : زكاة الفطر لأنه لم يكن بمكة زكاة

RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r1.claim: The phrase can mean all charitable giving, zakat paid excellently, or every good deed involving one's person or wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r1.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أوجه أحدها : أنه يريد سائر الصدقات

RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r2.claim: On the zakat reading, excellence means giving the best, most useful property, with sincere intention, seeking God's pleasure, and paying an eligible recipient.
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r2.anchor: من أطيب الأموال وأكثرها نفعا للفقراء ومراعاة النية وابتغاء وجه الله

RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says good deeds stored with God are better and more rewarding than wealth deferred for a bequest at death.
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : تجدوه عند الله خيرا وأعظم أجرا

RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the reward is better than worldly enjoyment; al-Razi prefers Ibn Abbas's interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج : وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله

RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r5.claim: The accusative khayran adds emphasis and intensification; Abu al-Sammal instead reads khayrun nominative, as a predicate construction.
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r5.anchor: إلا أنه قال : هو خيرا للتأكيد والمبالغة ، وقرأ أبو السمال هو خير وأعظم أجرا بالرفع

RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r6.claim: The command seeks forgiveness for sins and shortcomings, especially those in night vigil.
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r6.anchor: لذنوبكم والتقصيرات الصادرة منكم خاصة في قيام الليل

RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r7.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r7.claim: Muqatil holds that God is forgiving of all sins, including those of persistent sinners; the wording includes both repentant and persistent sinners, and forgiveness limited to penitents would be an obligatory act rather than praise.

RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r8.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r8.claim: The alternative view takes God's forgiveness here to concern those who persist in sin; Muqatil argues this better establishes praise than a promise only to the repentant.
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r8.anchor: والثاني : أنه غفور لمن يصر على الذنب

RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p166/r9.claim: The final description means God forgives believers' sins and is merciful to them.

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r1.claim: The night vigil in this verse is the form of vigil commanded in verses 1–8.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r1.anchor: The form of night vigil mentioned in the first sentence relates to that enjoined in vv. 1–8

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r2.claim: Probably revealed about twelve months after verses 1–8, this verse removed the night vigil’s obligatory status and made it voluntary.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r2.anchor: Most likely revealed some twelve months after those verses, the present verse revoked the obligatory status of the night vigil and made it voluntary

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r3.claim: The group with the Prophet were Companions who copied his practice and reportedly stood until their feet swelled.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r3.anchor: A group of those who are with thee refers to the small group of Companions who emulated the Prophet’s practice at that time, standing in prayer until their feet were swollen

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r4.claim: After the first sentence, the address shifts from the Prophet alone to the Prophet and his Companions together.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r4.anchor: After the first sentence, this verse changes from addressing the Prophet in the second-person singular to addressing the Prophet and his Companions in the second-person plural.

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r5.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r5.claim: The statement that they would not keep count means the Companions could not all fulfill the full night-vigil obligation.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r5.anchor: You will not keep count of it indicates that the Prophet’s Companions would not all be able to perform the obligation in full (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r6.claim: God relented by reducing the vigil requirement and letting them recite as much Quran in prayer as was easy.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r6.anchor: Therefore, He has relented unto you by lessening the requirement to stand in vigil and allowing them to recite as much of the Quran as is easy for them in prayer

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r7.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r7.claim: Some held that those who know the Quran should still recite at least fifty or one hundred verses.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r7.anchor: According to some, those who know the Quran should still recite a minimum of fifty or one hundred verses

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r8.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r8.claim: Another view lowers the minimum recitation for those who know the Quran to five verses.

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r9.claim: Night vigil is difficult for the sick, travelers, and fighters, so they need only perform what is not too taxing.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r9.anchor: For those who are sick, traveling, or fighting, performing the night vigil is difficult, so they need only perform that which is easy of it
