STUDYQURAN:73:20/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r10.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r10.claim: Some infer from the mention of fighting that this verse dates from the Medinan period, since fighting began there.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r10.anchor: The mention of fighting in this verse has caused some to surmise that it is from the Madinan period, as fighting did not begin until then.

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r11.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r11.claim: Others see the fighting as foreshadowing the trials faced by the early Muslim community.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r11.anchor: Others see it as foreshadowing the travails that the early Muslim community would face (IK).

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r12.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r12.claim: “Perform the prayer” refers to the obligatory daily prayers.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r12.anchor: Perform the prayer refers to the obligatory daily prayers (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r13.claim: This is the first mention of alms (zakāh) in revelation’s chronological order.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r13.anchor: This verse contains the first mention of alms

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r14.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r14.claim: Some interpret zakāh here as the obligatory alms.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r14.anchor: Some interpret it as a reference to the obligatory alms

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r15.claim: Because zakāh’s specific form was not yet institutionalized, the verse may refer to charity generally.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r15.anchor: but since the specific form of zakāh was not institutionalized at this time, it may refer to charity in general.

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r16.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r16.claim: Some say payment of alms was required in the Makkan period, while its detailed rules were established only in the Madinan period.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r16.anchor: Some say that the requirement to pay alms was established during the Makkan period, but that the specifics were not established until the Madinan period (IK)

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r17.claim: Lending a goodly loan means spending effort and wealth for religion’s cause; in 5:12 and here it is linked with prayer and almsgiving.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r17.anchor: To lend unto God a goodly loan (2:245; 5:12; 57:11, 18; 64:17) indicates expending effort and wealth for the cause of religion

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r18.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r18.claim: Whatever good believers send ahead for themselves comprises all their good deeds in this life.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r18.anchor: Whatever good you send forth for your souls refers to all good deeds performed by believers in this life (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r19.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r19.claim: Spending in God’s way during life is better than what one keeps for oneself or leaves as inheritance.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r19.anchor: what one spends in the way of God in this life is better than what one keeps for oneself or leaves behind as an inheritance (IK).

STUDYQURAN:73:20/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r20.claim: The reward also alludes to the increase of good deeds in the Hereafter, as in the parable of multiplied grain in 2:261 and related verses.
STUDYQURAN:73:20/r20.anchor: It also alludes to the manner in which good deeds are increased in the Hereafter, as in 2:261

TAB-FULL:v23p361/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command to the Prophet and believers to pray most of the night was difficult, then 73:20 eased it by allowing whatever recitation was manageable.
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {قم الليل إلا قليلا نصفه أو انقص منه قليلا أو زد عليه ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} [المزمل: 3]

TAB-FULL:v23p361/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r2.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r2.claim: Saʿid reports that the Prophet and some Companions maintained the commanded night vigil for ten years, until the final passage of the sura lightened the duty.
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r2.anchor: عن سعيد، قال: لما أنزل الله على نبيه: {يا أيها المزمل} [المزمل: 1] قال: مكث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v23p361/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r3.speaker: عكرمة والحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r3.claim: Ikrima and al-Hasan say the night-prayer command was abrogated by the verse saying God knew they could not keep its measure and permitted easy recitation.
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة والحسن، قالا: قال في سورة المزمل {قم الليل إلا قليلا نصفه أو انقص منه قليلا

TAB-FULL:v23p361/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r4.claim: Qatada says they kept the night vigil for a year or two, until their shins and feet swelled; relief came at the end of the sura.
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {قم الليل إلا قليلا} [المزمل: 2] قاموا حولا أو حولين حتى انتفخت سوقهم

TAB-FULL:v23p361/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r5.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman reports that people prayed for a year until swollen feet and shins were relieved when 73:20 instructed them to recite what was manageable.
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r5.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن، قال: لما نزلت: {يا أيها المزمل} [المزمل: 1] قاموا بها حولا حتى ورمت

TAB-FULL:v23p361/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r6.claim: Al-Hasan concludes that night prayer became voluntary after having been obligatory.
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: الحمد لله تطوع بعد فريضة

TAB-FULL:v23p376/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says night prayer was first obligatory, then God eased and removed that obligation for the Prophet and community; the later night vigil is voluntary for Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r6.anchor: وهذا حين كانت صلاة الليل فريضة، ثم إن الله من على العباد فخففها ووضعها

TAB-FULL:v23p393/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p393/r1.speaker: قراء المدينة والبصرة
TAB-FULL:v23p393/r1.claim: The general readers of Medina and Basra read wa-nisfihi wa-thuluthihi in the genitive, meaning less than two thirds, half, or a third of the night.
TAB-FULL:v23p393/r1.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان معروفتان صحيحتا المعنى، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب

TAB-FULL:v23p393/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p393/r2.speaker: قراء مكة والكوفة
TAB-FULL:v23p393/r2.claim: Some Meccan readers and the general readers of Kufa read the words in the accusative, taking them to mean that he also stands half or a third of the night.
TAB-FULL:v23p393/r2.anchor: وقرأ ذلك بعض قراء مكة وعامة قراء الكوفة بالنصب

TAB-FULL:v23p393/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p393/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p393/r3.claim: Al-Tabari accepts both readings as established and sound in meaning, so either is correct to recite.
TAB-FULL:v23p393/r3.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان معروفتان صحيحتا المعنى، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب

TAB-FULL:v23p394/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r1.claim: God knew those charged with night prayer could not sustain it; when they weakened, He granted relief and eased the obligation.
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، {علم أن لن تحصوه} [المزمل: 20] أن لن تطيقوه

TAB-FULL:v23p394/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r2.claim: Al-Hasan glosses la tuḥṣūhu as not being able to bear the night prayer.
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، {علم أن لن تحصوه} [المزمل: 20] أن لن تطيقوه

TAB-FULL:v23p394/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r3.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r3.claim: Saʿid likewise understands the phrase to mean that they would be unable to sustain the prayer.
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r3.anchor: عن جعفر، عن سعيد، {علم أن لن تحصوه} [المزمل: 20] يقول: أن لن تطيقوه

TAB-FULL:v23p394/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r4.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r4.claim: Sufyan also glosses the phrase as inability to sustain it.
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r4.anchor: عن سفيان، {علم أن لن تحصوه} [المزمل: 20] قال: أن لن تطيقوه

TAB-FULL:v23p394/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r5.claim: The Prophet tells Ibn ʿAmr of two easy but rarely maintained devotions that bring Paradise: ten each of glorifying, praising, and magnifying God after each prayer, plus a hundred before sleep; Satan distracts people from them in prayer and delays them until they sleep.
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «خلتان لا يحصيهما رجل مسلم إلا أدخلتاه الجنة، وهما يسير، ومن يعمل بهما قليل،

TAB-FULL:v23p394/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r6.claim: Qatada takes the unmeasurable burden to be the night vigil prescribed for the believers, followed by the instruction to recite what is manageable.
TAB-FULL:v23p394/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، {علم أن لن تحصوه} [المزمل: 20] قيام الليل كتب عليكم {فاقرءوا ما تيسر من القرآن}

TAB-FULL:v23p396/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r1.claim: The eased command is to recite whatever Qur'an is manageable during the night prayer, replacing the earlier prescribed measure of night vigil.
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r1.anchor: وقوله: {فاقرءوا ما تيسر من القرآن} يقول: فاقرءوا من الليل ما تيسر لكم من القرآن في صلاتكم

TAB-FULL:v23p396/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r2.claim: When asked about someone who memorized the Qur'an but only performs obligatory prayers, al-Hasan condemns neglecting its night recitation and says even fifty verses suffice.
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r2.anchor: قلت للحسن: يا أبا سعيد، ما تقول في رجل قد استظهر القرآن كله عن ظهر قلبه، فلا يقوم به، إنما يصلي المكتوبة؟

TAB-FULL:v23p396/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the manageable amount is one hundred verses.
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r3.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: {فاقرءوا ما تيسر من القرآن} قال: مائة آية

TAB-FULL:v23p396/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says that whoever recites a hundred verses at night will not have the Qur'an argue against him.
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r4.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: من قرأ مائة آية في ليلة لم يحاجه القرآن

TAB-FULL:v23p396/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r5.speaker: كعب
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r5.claim: Kaʿb says a person who recites a hundred verses in a night is counted among the worshippers.
TAB-FULL:v23p396/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح، عن كعب، قال: من قرأ في ليلة مائة آية كتب من العابدين

TAB-FULL:v23p397/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r1.claim: God anticipates illness that weakens some from night prayer, travel and trade that exhaust others, and fighting for His cause; He therefore lifts the obligation and leaves them to recite what they can at night.
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: علم ربكم أيها المؤمنون أن سيكون منكم أهل مرض قد أضعفه المرض عن قيام الليل

TAB-FULL:v23p397/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r2.claim: The pronoun in minhu, “of it,” refers to the Qur'an.
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r2.anchor: والهاء في قوله {منه} [البقرة: 60] من ذكر القرآن

TAB-FULL:v23p397/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r3.claim: Qatada reports that night prayer was imposed at the sura's beginning; Muhammad and his Companions stood for a year until their feet swelled, then after twelve months the easing made it voluntary after having been obligatory.
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: ثم أنبأ بخصال المؤمنين، فقال: {علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى

TAB-FULL:v23p398/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p398/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p398/r1.claim: Establish the five obligatory prayers throughout day and night and give the obligatory alms to their rightful recipients.
TAB-FULL:v23p398/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة} [المزمل: 20] فهما فريضتان واجبتان، لا رخصة لأحد فيهما

TAB-FULL:v23p398/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p398/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p398/r2.claim: Qatada calls prayer and zakat two binding duties for which no one has a dispensation and says they must be fulfilled for God.
TAB-FULL:v23p398/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة} [المزمل: 20] فهما فريضتان واجبتان، لا رخصة لأحد فيهما

TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r1.claim: Lending to God means spending wealth in His cause.

TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the loan as voluntary giving in addition to the obligatory zakat.

TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r3.claim: Good deeds sent ahead in worldly life—including charity, spending in God's cause, prayer, fasting, and pilgrimage—will be found with God on the Day of Resurrection with greater reward.
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r3.anchor: يقول: وما تقدموا أيها المؤمنون لأنفسكم في دار الدنيا من صدقة أو نفقة تنفقونها في سبيل الله

TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r4.claim: The command is to ask God to forgive sins so that He may pardon them.
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r4.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: وسلوا الله غفران ذنوبكم يصفح لكم عنها

TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r5.claim: God forgives servants who repent of their sins and, in His mercy, does not punish them after repentance.
TAB-FULL:v23p398#2/r5.anchor: إن الله ذو مغفرة لذنوب من تاب من عباده من ذنوبه، وذو رحمة أن يعاقبهم عليها من بعد توبتهم منها

TAB-FULL:v1p46/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r1.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r1.claim: Abu Bakra reports that Gabriel asked the Prophet to recite on one letter, Michael urged him to request more, and the allowance rose to six or seven; the forms are sufficient if mercy and punishment verses are not mismatched.
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r1.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة، عن أبيه، قال: قال رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v1p46/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r2.claim: Tabari says the seven ahruf differ in wording while agreeing in meaning, like hallum and ta'al, rather than differing in meanings that change legal rulings.
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r2.anchor: فقد أوضح نص هذا الخبر أن اختلاف الأحرف السبعة، إنما هو اختلاف ألفاظ، كقولك هلم وتعال

TAB-FULL:v1p46/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r3.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says the reciters he heard were close in their readings, so people should read as taught and avoid affectation, like saying hallum or ta'al.
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r3.anchor: عن شقيق، قال، قال عبد الله

TAB-FULL:v1p46/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r4.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says anyone who reads on a letter should not switch; he adds that he would seek someone more knowledgeable than himself about God's Book.
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r4.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عمن سمع ابن مسعود، يقول: «من قرأ منكم على حرف، فلا يتحولن

TAB-FULL:v1p46/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r5.speaker: رجل من أصحاب عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r5.claim: An unnamed companion of Abdullah reports his instruction that anyone who reads on a letter should not move to another.
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r5.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عابس، عن رجل من أصحاب عبد الله، عن عبد الله بن مسعود، قال

TAB-FULL:v1p46/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r6.claim: Tabari explains “letter” here as a person's recitation or reading, a usage like naming a poem a poet's “word,” rather than switching among Quran topics or alphabet characters.
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r6.anchor: وإنما عنى رحمة الله عليه، أن من قرأ بحرفه، وحرفه: قراءته

TAB-FULL:v1p46/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r7.claim: A reader should not abandon a Companion's reading from one of the seven ahruf out of aversion; rejecting any one of them amounts to rejecting the whole Quran.
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ بحرف أبي، أو بحرف زيد، أو بحرف بعض من قرأ من أصحاب رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v1p46/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r8.claim: Tabari says disbelief in one letter, meaning a transmitted reading among the seven, is disbelief in all of it.
TAB-FULL:v1p46/r8.anchor: فإن الكفر ببعضه كفر بجميعه، والكفر بحرف من ذلك كفر بجميعه

SULAMI:v2p356#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r1.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says people cannot sustain the commanded worship or keep their deeds sound and free of defects; God relents and accepts their deeds by grace.
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : أي لن تطيقوا القيام بأمره ولن تضبطوا أعمالكم بالصحة والبرأة من العيوب فتاب عليكم فعاد عليكم بفضله

SULAMI:v2p356#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r2.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī warns that one who meets God through His gifts is cut off from the Giver by the gifts and veiled from the Essence by the attributes.
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r2.anchor: مع أن من لقيه بنعمه كان منقطعا عن المنعم بالنعم ومحجوبا بالصفات عن الذات

SULAMI:v2p356#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r3.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r3.claim: Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad interprets the recitation as what affords the heart humility and the inner secret clarity.
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r3.anchor: عن جعفر بن محمد في قوله : ^ ( فاقرءوا ما تيسر من القرآن ) ^ قال : ما تيسر لكم فيه خشوع القلب وصفاء السر

SULAMI:v2p356#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r4.claim: Some say that spending for God's pleasure is better than holding back out of stinginess.
SULAMI:v2p356#4/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : ما تنفقوه في مرضات الله خير لكم من الإمساك والشح

SULAMI:v2p357/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p357/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p357/r1.claim: The good advanced for God is better and greater in reward than what is considered for one's heirs.

SULAMI:v2p357/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p357/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p357/r2.claim: The passage urges seeking God's forgiveness in every circumstance or respect.
SULAMI:v2p357/r2.anchor: واستغفروا الله على الوجوه كلها لأن الصدقة على ثلاث اوجه

SULAMI:v2p357/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p357/r3.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p357/r3.claim: Charity may arise from ostentation, desire, or affliction; what is wholly for God is rare and attained only by the righteous brought near.
SULAMI:v2p357/r3.anchor: لأن الصدقة على ثلاث اوجه : رياء وهوى وبلاء وما كان من ذلك خالصا لوجه الله تعالى فهو عزيز ولا يصل إليه إلا الأبرار المقربون

TABATABAI:73:20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r1.claim: The verse eases the earlier night-prayer command by allowing what is manageable from the Quran, without abrogating the original instruction to stand the specified portions.
TABATABAI:73:20/r1.anchor: ولسان الآية هو التخفيف بما تيسر من القرآن من غير نسخ لأصل الحكم السابق

TABATABAI:73:20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r2.claim: Reports place this Meccan verse eight months, a year, or ten years after the sura's opening verses.
TABATABAI:73:20/r2.anchor: وقد ورد في غير واحد من الأخبار أن الآية مكية نزلت بعد ثمانية أشهر أو سنة أو عشر سنين

TABATABAI:73:20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r3.claim: Prayer followed by obligatory zakat and distinguished from voluntary charity suggests zakat here is obligatory, which was instituted in Medina after the Hijra.
TABATABAI:73:20/r3.anchor: وإنما فرضت الزكاة بالمدينة بعد الهجرة

TABATABAI:73:20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:20/r4.claim: Some say zakat was imposed in Mecca without specified thresholds, while Medina later specified its thresholds.
TABATABAI:73:20/r4.anchor: وقول بعضهم إن الزكاة فرضت بمكة من غير تعيين الأنصباء

TABATABAI:73:20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r5.claim: The claim that Meccan zakat was imposed without specifying thresholds is unsupported.

TABATABAI:73:20/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:20/r6.claim: Some propose that the verse was revealed earlier but its legal ruling took effect later; the author calls this unsupported.
TABATABAI:73:20/r6.anchor: قول بعضهم إنه من الممكن أن تكون الآية مما تأخر حكمه عن نزوله

TABATABAI:73:20/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r7.claim: The delayed-ruling proposal is also conjecture without evidence.

TABATABAI:73:20/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r8.claim: Mentioning fighting would not suit the early mission's circumstances, so the verse is apparently Medinan; some others also favor this dating.
TABATABAI:73:20/r8.anchor: فالظاهر أن الآية مدنية وليست بمكية وقد مال إليه بعضهم

TABATABAI:73:20/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r9.claim: Addressing God as your Lord intimates divine mercy and care; noting that He knows the Prophet's vigil also suggests gratitude for his effort, as in 17:19.
TABATABAI:73:20/r9.anchor: تلويح إلى شمول الرحمة والعناية الإلهية

TABATABAI:73:20/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r10.claim: Adna is a comparative from nearness, conventionally meaning just less than an amount: a count near ten is nine, not eleven.
TABATABAI:73:20/r10.anchor: وقد جرى العرف على استعمال أدنى فيما يقرب من الشيء وهو أقل

TABATABAI:73:20/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r11.claim: The waw is additive: on some nights the Prophet stands just under two-thirds, on others half, and on others a third.
TABATABAI:73:20/r11.anchor: لمطلق الجمع والمراد أنه يعلم أنك تقوم في بعض الليالي

TABATABAI:73:20/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r12.claim: Those with the Prophet means his fellow believers, and min is partitive; some of them also kept night vigil.
TABATABAI:73:20/r12.anchor: فالآية تدل على أن بعضهم كان يقوم الليل كما كان يقومه النبي

TABATABAI:73:20/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r13.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:20/r13.claim: Another parsing takes min as explanatory; the author dismisses this reading.
TABATABAI:73:20/r13.anchor: وقيل { من } بيانية، وهو كما ترى

TABATABAI:73:20/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r14.claim: God knows because He is the creator and determiner; determining night and day entails determining their thirds, halves, and two-thirds.
TABATABAI:73:20/r14.anchor: في مقام التعليل لقوله { إن ربك يعلم } والمعنى وكيف لا يعلم

TABATABAI:73:20/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20/r15.claim: The verse names Allah in connection with measurement because determining measures is a matter of creation, and all creation belongs to Him.
TABATABAI:73:20/r15.anchor: لأن التقدير من شؤون الخلق والخلق إلى الله الذي إليه ينتهي كل شيء

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r1.claim: Ihsa means obtaining a measure or number and encompassing the thing.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r1.anchor: الاحصاء تحصيل مقدار الشيء وعدده والإحاطة به

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r2.claim: The pronoun in lan tuhsuhu may refer to measuring night or to standing for its prescribed thirds, half, or near two-thirds.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r2.anchor: وضمير { لن تحصوه } للتقدير أو للقيام مقدار ثلث الليل

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r3.claim: Calculating fixed portions through nights of changing annual length is hard for ordinary people, especially those sleeping early without staying awake all night to be certain.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r3.anchor: وإحصاء ذلك مع اختلاف الليالي طولا وقصرا في أيام السنة مما لا يتيسر لعامة المكلفين

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r4.claim: God knew that the prescribed night amount could not be calculated with ease by the generality of those obligated.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r4.anchor: علمه تعالى بعدم تيسر إحصاء المقدار الذي أمروا بقيامه

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r5.claim: Here God's tawba toward people means His merciful turning to them through easing the burden.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r5.anchor: توبته تعالى ورجوعه إليهم بمعنى انعطاف الرحمة الإلهية عليهم بالتخفيف

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r6.claim: God's turning in mercy can enable repentance or obedience, lift some duties, or ease them; 9:118 describes Him turning to people so that they might repent.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r6.anchor: فلله سبحانه توبة على عباده ببسط رحمته عليهم وأثرها توفيقهم للتوبة أو لمطلق الطاعة

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r7.claim: A distinct usage is God's return to people after their repentance, whose effect is forgiveness of their sins.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r7.anchor: كما أن له توبة عليهم بمعنى الرجوع إليهم بعد توبتهم وأثرها مغفرة ذنوبهم

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r8.claim: The command eases the amount of night vigil for the generality of believers because they cannot calculate the specified portions; it does not cancel the original rule for those able to keep it.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r8.anchor: التخفيف في قيام الليل من حيث المقدار لعامة المكلفين

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r9.claim: The difficulty applies to the obligated group collectively, not every person: the Prophet and some companions could keep the portions, so others receive a concession while the original option remains.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r9.anchor: إنما لا يتيسر لمجموع المكلفين لا لجميعهم ولو امتنع لجميعهم ولم يتيسر لأحدهم

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r10.claim: Night vigil is recommended for other believers, although the address to the Prophet appears obligatory.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r10.anchor: والحكم استحبابي لسائر المؤمنين وإن كان ظاهر ما للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من الخطاب الوجوب

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r11.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r11.claim: Commentators disagree whether the original night command meant prayer or Quran recitation outside prayer.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r11.anchor: وللقوم في كون المراد بقيام الليل الصلاة فيه أو قراءة القرآن خارج الصلاة

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r12.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r12.claim: One reported legal view makes night vigil obligatory for both the Prophet and believers.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r12.anchor: في كونه واجبا على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والمؤمنين

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r13.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r13.claim: Another reported view recommends night vigil for everyone.

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r14.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r14.claim: A third view makes it obligatory for the Prophet and recommended for others.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r14.anchor: أو واجبا على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم مستحبا لغيره

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r15.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r15.claim: Commentators also disagree whether the easing abrogated the earlier ruling or changed the commanded prayer into reciting what is manageable.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r15.anchor: ثم في نسخ الحكم بالتخفيف بما تيسر بهذه الآية أو تبديل الصلاة من قراءة ما تيسر من القرآن أقوال

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r1.claim: Illness, travel, and fighting provide another reason for easing exact night portions, since calculating them is especially difficult in those circumstances.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى مصلحة أخرى مقتضية للتخفيف في أمر القيام ثلث الليل أو نصفه

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r2.claim: Traveling in search of God's bounty means journeying between lands for livelihood through trade.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r2.anchor: والمراد بالضرب في الأرض للابتغاء من فضل الله طلب الرزق بالمسافرة من أرض إلى أرض للتجارة

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r3.claim: The repeated concession to recite what is manageable reinforces the easing.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r3.anchor: وقوله { فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا } تكرار للتخفيف تأكيدا

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r4.claim: The pronoun in minhu refers to the Quran.

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r5.claim: Prayer should be performed in a way suited to the amount of time spent standing.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r5.anchor: والمراد الإتيان بالصلاة على ما يناسب سعة الوقت الذي قاموا فيه

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r6.claim: The prayer to be established is obligatory: if the verse is Medinan, it is the five daily prayers; if Meccan, it is whatever prayers were then prescribed.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r6.anchor: والمراد بالصلاة المأمور بإقامتها الفريضة فإن كانت الآية مدنية فالفرائض الخمس اليومية

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r7.claim: The zakat commanded is obligatory zakat.

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r8.claim: Lending God a good loan means financial donations in His cause beyond obligatory zakat.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r8.anchor: والمراد بإقراضه تعالى غير الزكاة من الإنفاقات المالية في سبيل الله

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r9.claim: Pairing prayer, zakat, and charity signals that religious duties remain in force; the easing does not spread to every obligation, as in 58:13.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r9.anchor: وعطف الأمر بإقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة والإقراض للتلويح إلى أن التكاليف الدينية على حالها

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r10.claim: Min khayr explains the relative pronoun, and khayr means all obedience, obligatory and recommended.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r10.anchor: والمراد بالخير مطلق الطاعة أعم من الواجبة والمندوبة

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r11.claim: Huwa is either a separator pronoun or an emphatic repetition of the object pronoun in tajiduhu.

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r12.claim: Obedience sent ahead for the afterlife is found with God on the day of meeting, better than anything done or left undone and greater in reward.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r12.anchor: خيرا من كل ما تعملون أو تتركون وأعظم أجرا

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r13.claim: The closing command is to seek God's forgiveness; His description as forgiving and merciful intimates a promise of pardon and mercy.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r13.anchor: وقوله { واستغفروا الله إن الله غفور رحيم } ختم الكلام بالأمر بالاستغفار

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r14.claim: The author allows that seeking forgiveness may mean performing all acts of obedience, since they are means to God's forgiveness.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r14.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يكون المراد بالاستغفار الإتيان بمطلق الطاعات لأنها وسائل يتوسل بها إلى مغفرة الله

TABATABAI:73:20#3/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r15.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r15.claim: Abu Ja'far's report says the Prophet observed and announced the night vigil, people struggled to calculate the portions and sometimes stayed until dawn fearing error, and God eased it; it adds that every prophet prayed at night, never beginning early in the evening.
TABATABAI:73:20#3/r15.anchor: في تفسير القمي في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

TABATABAI:73:20#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r1.claim: The Abu Ja'far report presents the sura's opening as requiring night prayer and its ending as abrogating that duty; al-Tabataba'i says his preceding discussion addresses this view.
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r1.anchor: أقول محصل الرواية أن صدر السورة توجب صلاة الليل وذيلها تنسخها

TABATABAI:73:20#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r2.claim: Similar reports through Sunni routes from Ibn Abbas and others also describe abrogation of the opening night-prayer command.
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r2.anchor: وروي ما يقرب منه من طرق أهل السنة عن ابن عباس وغيره

TABATABAI:73:20#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report cited by al-Majma through al-Haskani, al-Kalbi, and Abu Salih, identifies the accompanying group as Ali and Abu Dharr.
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r3.anchor: روى الحاكم أبو القاسم إبراهيم الحسكاني بإسناده عن الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس

TABATABAI:73:20#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r4.speaker: الرضا عن أبيه عن جده
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r4.claim: A report from al-Rida, his father, and his grandfather says what is easy to recite is what brings humility of heart and purity of the inner self.
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r4.anchor: روي عن الرضا عن أبيه عن جده عليهم السلام قال ما تيسر منه لكم فيه خشوع القلب

TABATABAI:73:20#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r5.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r5.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh report from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet explained what is easy as one hundred verses.
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r5.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم والطبراني وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس عن النبي

TABATABAI:73:20#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r6.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports Ibn Masud quoting the Prophet: a trader who imports food to a Muslim town and sells at the day's price has the rank of a martyr; the Prophet then recited this verse.
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r6.anchor: وفيه أخرج ابن مردويه عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال قال رسول الله

TABATABAI:73:20#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r7.speaker: سماعة
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r7.claim: In al-Qummi's tafsir, Zur'ah transmits Sama'ah's answer that a goodly loan is something other than zakat.
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r7.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي بإسناده عن زرعة عن سماعة قال سألته عن قول الله

TABATABAI:73:20#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r8.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r8.claim: Ali's hadith of the four hundred advises frequent seeking of forgiveness to attract provision and advancing whatever good one can; its final phrase derives from 73:20.
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r8.anchor: وفي الخصال عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام في حديث الأربعمائة أكثروا الاستغفار تجلبوا الرزق

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r4.speaker: عائشة
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha says night prayer was obligatory at the surah's beginning; the Prophet and companions performed it for a year, then the closing passage eased it and made it voluntary.
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r4.anchor: قلت لعائشة انبئيني عن قيام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says ten years elapsed between the surah's opening and its passage of relief.
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r5.anchor: كان بين أول السورة وآخرها الذي نزل فيه التخفيف عشر سنين عن سعيد بن جبير

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r6.speaker: ابن كيسان ومقاتل
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r6.claim: Ibn Kaysān and Muqātil place the command in Mecca before the five prayers and say those prayers abrogated it.
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r6.anchor: كان هذا بمكة قبل فرض الصلوات الخمس ثم نسخ بالخمس عن ابن كيسان ومقاتل

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a year separated the surah's beginning and end, and the believers initially prayed about as long as in Ramadan.
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r7.anchor: كانوا يقومون نحوا من قيامهم في شهر رمضان

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r8.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrima say the final verse abrogated the first.
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r8.anchor: إن الآية الأخيرة نسخت الأولى عن الحسن وعكرمة

TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r9.claim: The verses do not require abrogation; the better reading is that night prayer is strongly recommended, not obligatory.
TABRISI:73:1-10#3/r9.anchor: وليس في ظاهر الآيات ما يقتضي النسخ فالأولى أن يكون الكلام على ظاهره

TABRISI:73:20/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأهل الكوفة
TABRISI:73:20/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and the Kufans read half and a third in the accusative.
TABRISI:73:20/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأهل الكوفة نصفه وثلثه بالنصب

TABRISI:73:20/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:73:20/r2.claim: The remaining readers use the genitive for half and a third.

TABRISI:73:20/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:73:20/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the accusative reading attaches half and a third to adnā, itself accusative.
TABRISI:73:20/r3.anchor: من نصب حمله على أدنى وأدنى في موضع نصب

TABRISI:73:20/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:73:20/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says adnā means nearer, yielding the sense that one also stands half and a third of the night.
TABRISI:73:20/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة أدنى أقرب فكأنه قال

TABRISI:73:20/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:73:20/r5.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan objects that this cannot mean nearer than half and a third; he understands it as less than those amounts.
TABRISI:73:20/r5.anchor: وليس المعنى عليه فيما بلغنا لأن المعنى يكون على أدنى من نصفه

TABRISI:73:20/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:73:20/r6.claim: For the genitive reading, Abū al-Ḥasan understands a concession to pray less than the required amount.
TABRISI:73:20/r6.anchor: فأما الذين قرؤوا بالجر فعلى أن يكون المعنى إنكم إن لم تؤدوا ما فرض الله عليكم

TABRISI:73:20/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20/r7.claim: Adnā means nearer to, or less than, two thirds; the pronoun refers to night, with prayer near two thirds on some nights and near half or a third on others.
TABRISI:73:20/r7.anchor: الهاء تعود إلى الليل أي نصف الليل وثلث الليل

TABRISI:73:20/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20/r8.claim: Another view makes the pronoun refer to two thirds, making the prayer nearer to half or a third of that amount.
TABRISI:73:20/r8.anchor: إن الهاء تعود إلى الثلثين أي وأقرب من نصف الثلثين

TABRISI:73:20/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20/r9.claim: With the accusative reading, the phrase means standing half and a third of the night.
TABRISI:73:20/r9.anchor: وإذا نصبت فالمعنى تقوم نصفه وثلثه

TABRISI:73:20/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:73:20/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the accompanying group as Abū ʿAlī and Abū Dharr.
TABRISI:73:20/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { وطائفة من الذين معك } قال أبو علي وأبو ذر

TABRISI:73:20/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20/r11.claim: God apportions night and day so people can act during them as commanded.
TABRISI:73:20/r11.anchor: يقدر أوقاتهما لتعملوا فيها على ما يأمركم به

TABRISI:73:20/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r12.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:73:20/r12.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the meaning is that God misses none of what people do.
TABRISI:73:20/r12.anchor: لا يفوته علم ما تفعلون عن عطاء

TABRISI:73:20/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20/r13.claim: The verse means God knows how much of the night people will stand in prayer.
TABRISI:73:20/r13.anchor: يعلم القدر الذي تقومونه من الليل

TABRISI:73:20/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r14.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:73:20/r14.claim: Muqātil says people prayed at night fearing they would fail to reach the commanded amount, so God says they cannot calculate it precisely.
TABRISI:73:20/r14.anchor: كان الرجل يصلي الليل مخافة أن لا يصيب ما أمر به من القيام

TABRISI:73:20/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r15.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:73:20/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they prayed until their feet swelled, and God told them they could not truly keep count.

TABRISI:73:20/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20/r16.claim: Another explanation is that they could not sustain night prayer consistently and would fall short.
TABRISI:73:20/r16.anchor: لن تطيقوا المداومة على قيام الليل ويقع منكم التقصير فيه

TABRISI:73:20/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r17.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:73:20/r17.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says God made night prayer voluntary rather than obligatory.
TABRISI:73:20/r17.anchor: بأن جعله تطوعا ولم يجعله فرضا عن الجبائي

TABRISI:73:20/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20/r18.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means no liability is imposed, or that God eased the burden.

TABRISI:73:20/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r19.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:73:20/r19.claim: Most exegetes take the command as reciting whatever is manageable in night prayer.
TABRISI:73:20/r19.anchor: يعني في صلاة الليل عن أكثر المفسرين

TABRISI:73:20/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20/r21.claim: Some say to pray whatever is manageable, calling prayer Qurʾan because it includes recitation.
TABRISI:73:20/r21.anchor: فصلوا ما تيسر من الصلاة وعبر عن الصلاة بالقرآن لأنها تتضمنه

TABRISI:73:20/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r22.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:73:20/r22.claim: Most exegetes treat recitation outside prayer as recommended, not obligatory, since obligation would entail memorization.
TABRISI:73:20/r22.anchor: محمول على الاستحباب عند الأكثرين دون الوجوب لأنه لو وجبت القراءة لوجب الحفظ

TABRISI:73:20/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20/r23.speaker: بعضهم
TABRISI:73:20/r23.claim: Some hold recitation obligatory because it reveals the Qurʾan's inimitability and proofs of monotheism and prophethood, while memorization remains recommended.
TABRISI:73:20/r23.anchor: محمول على الوجوب لأن القارىء يقف على إعجاز القرآن وما فيه من دلائل التوحيد

TABRISI:73:20#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:73:20#2/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the manageable amount is fifty verses.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r1.anchor: فقال سعيد بن جبير خمسون آية

TABRISI:73:20#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:73:20#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the manageable amount is one hundred verses.

TABRISI:73:20#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:73:20#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says whoever reads one hundred verses in a night will not have the Qurʾan litigate against him.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r3.anchor: وعن الحسن قال: من قرأ مائة آية في ليلة

TABRISI:73:20#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r4.speaker: كعب
TABRISI:73:20#2/r4.claim: Kaʿb says reading one hundred verses in a night counts a person among the devout.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r4.anchor: وقال كعب: من قرأ مائة آية في ليلة

TABRISI:73:20#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r5.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:73:20#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says the amount is two hundred verses.

TABRISI:73:20#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r6.speaker: جويبر
TABRISI:73:20#2/r6.claim: Juwaybir says it is a third of the Qurʾan, since God made recitation easy for His servants.

TABRISI:73:20#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20#2/r7.claim: The apparent meaning is an amount of recitation that a person wants and finds agreeable.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن معنى ما تيسر مقدار ما أردتم وأحببتم

TABRISI:73:20#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20#2/r8.claim: The prospect of illness is one reason God gives for easing night prayer.

TABRISI:73:20#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:73:20#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains traveling in God's bounty as journeys for trade and profit.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r9.anchor: يسافرون للتجارة وطلب الأرباح عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:73:20#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20#2/r10.claim: Believers fighting in God's path are another reason for easing the night prayer.

TABRISI:73:20#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r11.speaker: الرضا
TABRISI:73:20#2/r11.claim: Al-Riḍā, quoting his father and grandfather, says manageable recitation is what brings humility of heart and purity of inner self.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r11.anchor: عن الرضا ع عن أبيه عن جده ع قال ما تيسر منه لكم فيه خشوع القلب

TABRISI:73:20#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20#2/r12.claim: Establish prayer according to the limits God made obligatory.

TABRISI:73:20#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20#2/r13.claim: The zakat commanded here is obligatory alms.

TABRISI:73:20#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20#2/r14.claim: Lending God a good loan means spending in God's cause and in causes He commands or encourages.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r14.anchor: أنفقوا في سبيل الله والجهات التي أمركم الله وندبكم

TABRISI:73:20#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20#2/r15.claim: What people send ahead is obedience; they will find its reward with God, better than miserliness and shortcoming.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r15.anchor: أي طاعة { تجدوه } أي تجدوا ثوابه

TABRISI:73:20#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20#2/r16.claim: Huwa may be an emphatic separator, called faṣl by Basrans and ʿimād by Kufans, or an adjective of the object pronoun.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r16.anchor: يسمى فصلا عند البصريين وعمادا عند الكوفيين ويجوز

TABRISI:73:20#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20#2/r17.claim: Seeking forgiveness means asking God to forgive; He covers sins, pardons, and shows mercy.

TABRISI:73:20#2/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r18.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:73:20#2/r18.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a patient, God-seeking merchant who brings goods to a Muslim city and sells at the day's price is like the martyrs.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r18.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: أيما رجل جلب شيئا

TABRISI:73:20#2/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r19.speaker: ابن عمر
TABRISI:73:20#2/r19.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that after dying in God's path, he would most wish to die traveling while seeking God's bounty.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r19.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: ما خلق الله موتة أموتها

TABRISI:73:20#2/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20#2/r20.claim: One view says the verse is Medinan because prayer and zakat were not made obligatory in Mecca.
TABRISI:73:20#2/r20.anchor: هذه الآية مدنية ويدل عليها أن الصلاة والزكاة لم توجبا بمكة

TABRISI:73:20#2/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:20#2/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:20#2/r21.claim: Another view says prayer and zakat were already obligatory in Mecca, so the verse is Meccan.

FARRA:v3p198/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p198/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p198/r9.claim: Asim and al-Aʿmash read the following fractions in the accusative; Medinans and Hasan read genitive. The accusative better makes half and a third specify the lesser amount, as “less than a thousand: eight or nine hundred,” rather than further explaining “less.”
FARRA:v3p198/r9.anchor: ومن نصب أراد: تقوم أدنى من الثلثين، فيقوم النصف أو الثلث

FARRA:v3p199/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p199/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p199/r1.claim: The Prophet and a group of Muslims used to stand in prayer at night before the prayer obligation; it became difficult for them, so this concession was revealed.
FARRA:v3p199/r1.anchor: وطائفة من الذين معك (20) كان النبي صلى الله عليه، وطائفة من المسلمين يقومون الليل قبل أن تفرض الصلاة، فشق ذلك عليهم، فنزلت الرخصة.

FARRA:v3p199/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p199/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p199/r2.claim: A rare, unread construal takes the Prophet’s prayer as reaching one-third: less than two-thirds and half, but not below a third. Al-Farra says the phrase may mean “the third.”
FARRA:v3p199/r2.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يخفض النصف، وينصب الثلث لتأويل قوم: أن صلاة النبي صلى الله عليه انتهت إلى ثلث الليل، فقالوا: إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من الثلثين، ومن النصف، ولا تنقص من الثلث، وهو وجه شاذ لم يقرأ به أحد.

FARRA:v3p199/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p199/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p199/r3.claim: Al-Farra says established reciters are more knowledgeable about interpretation than hadith transmitters.
FARRA:v3p199/r3.anchor: وأهل القراءة الذين يتبعون أعلم بالتأويل من المحدثين.

FARRA:v3p199/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p199/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p199/r4.claim: They would not be able to keep track of the night’s appointed times.

FARRA:v3p199/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p199/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p199/r5.claim: What is manageable to recite means one hundred verses or more.

FARRA:v3p199/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p199/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p199/r6.claim: A report says that whoever recites ten verses is not counted among the heedless.
FARRA:v3p199/r6.anchor: وقد ذكروا : أنه من قرأ عشر آيات لم يكتب من الغافلين،

FARRA:v3p199/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p199/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p199/r7.claim: Anything the worshipper revives of the night counts as nāshiʾa.
FARRA:v3p199/r7.anchor: وكل شيء أحياه المصلي من الليل فهو ناشئة.

FARRA:v3p199/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p199/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p199/r8.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: وأقيموا الصلاة (20) يعنى: المفروضة.

THALABI:v10p59/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p59/r3.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v10p59/r3.claim: ʿĀʾisha says the Prophet feared congregational night prayer would become obligatory; it was imposed for eight months, then verse 20 relieved them and left only voluntary night prayer.
THALABI:v10p59/r3.anchor: وروى أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن عائشة، قالت:

THALABI:v10p65/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p65/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v10p65/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a patient trader who brings goods to a Muslim city seeking God’s reward and sells at the day’s price has the rank of martyrs.
THALABI:v10p65/r1.anchor: عن فرقد السبخي عن إبراهيم عن ابن مسعود، قال: أيما رجل جلب شيئا

THALABI:v10p65/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p65/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v10p65/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that, after death while fighting for God, he would most prefer to die while traveling to seek God’s bounty.
THALABI:v10p65/r2.anchor: عن أبيه، قال: سمعت ابن عمر، يقول: ما خلق الله عز وجل موتة

THALABI:v10p65/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p65/r3.speaker: علي بن موسى الرضا
THALABI:v10p65/r3.claim: ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā interprets what is easy to recite as humility of the heart and purity of the inner self.
THALABI:v10p65/r3.anchor: عن جعفر بن محمد في هذه الآية، قال: ما تيسر لكم منه خشوع القلب

THALABI:v10p65/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p65/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p65/r4.claim: Whatever good people send ahead, they find with God better than stinginess and shortfall, and greater in reward than what they might otherwise have failed to give.
THALABI:v10p65/r4.anchor: وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله هو خيرا من الشح والتقصير

THALABI:v10p65/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p65/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p65/r5.claim: Khayran and aʿẓama are accusative as a second object; Basrans call huwa a separator, Kufans a support, with no syntactic case.
THALABI:v10p65/r5.anchor: ونصب خيرا وأعظم على المفعول الثاني، وهو فصل في قول البصريين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p345/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p345/r10.speaker: الوالبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p345/r10.claim: Al-Wālibī’s narration says the believers found the initial night-prayer requirement difficult, so God eased it and revealed the allowance for those who would be ill.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p345/r10.anchor: في رواية الوالبي: لما نزلت هذه الآية شق ذلك على المؤمنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p345/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p345/r11.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p345/r11.claim: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī says the night-prayer command was given in Mecca and was abrogated after the Prophet came to Medina by the remainder of the sūra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p345/r11.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء (الخراساني) (¬3) كان هذا بمكة، فلما قدم النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- المدينة نسختها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r1.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī reports that after the opening night-prayer command, the believers stood for a year until their feet and legs swelled; the recitation allowance then came and relieved them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي (¬6)، # وقال) (¬1): (إنه) (¬2) لما نزلت: {يا أيها المزمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r2.claim: Maqātil says this allowance was revealed in Mecca, before the five prayers were made obligatory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p348/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كان هذا بمكة قبل أن (تفرض الصلوات) (¬5) الخمس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r3.claim: They take adnā as less, as in 2:61, where the same word means something inferior.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬4)، ومقاتل (¬5): أقل، كقوله: {أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r4.claim: The preferred reading has the accusative half and third coordinated with adnā; the sense is that the Prophet stood less than two thirds, and stood half or a third.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ونصفه وثلثه} (عطف على قوله: (أدنى (¬8)) و (أدنى) في موضع نصب (¬9)، والتقدير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r5.speaker: من قرأ بالجر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r5.claim: The genitive reading connects half and third to the preposition min, meaning less than two thirds, half, and a third.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r5.anchor: ومن قرأ بالجر (¬1) حمله على الحال في قوله: {من ثلثي الليل} والمعنى: أدنى من ثلثي الليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as standing half the night and a third of it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: وتقوم نصفه وثلثه (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r7.speaker: أبو الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r7.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan says the obligation was a third or more; the genitive reading would imply they failed to fulfill it, which is not the intended sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r7.anchor: (وقال أبو الحسن: الذي افترض الثلث، وأكثر من الثلث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r8.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r8.claim: The author of the verse arrangement says that on the genitive reading the minimum obligation was one quarter, which they did not fall below.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p382/r8.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: الأقل الذي افترض عليهم: الربع، لم ينقصوا # من الربع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r1.claim: The group with the Prophet consists of his believing companions, who prayed a third or half of the night with him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (2)، ومقاتل (3): يعني أصحابه الذين آمنوا به، كانوا يقومون معه ثلثا ونصفا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r2.claim: God knows the measures of a third, half, and two thirds of the night, as well as its other portions and times.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r3.claim: They cannot know the exact measures or endure keeping the night vigil according to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r3.anchor: ويعلم أنكم: {لن تحصوه} (أي لن تطيقوا معرفة حقائق ذلك، والقيام فيه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r4.claim: Maqātil says some prayed the whole night for fear of missing the prescribed amount; the clause means that they would not calculate it accurately, with an lightened from the doubled particle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل: كان الرجل يصلي الليل كله مخافة أن لا يصيب ما أمر الله به من قيام ما فرض عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r5.claim: God turned toward them with pardon and relief.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as God excusing them for what they could not fully comprehend.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فعفا عنكم ما لم تحيطوا بعلمه (11)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p385/r7.claim: Maqātil explains the phrase as God passing over them by easing the obligation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this instruction addresses people other than the Prophet: night prayer ceased to be obligatory for the Companions and became voluntary, while remaining obligatory for the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد غير النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-، فسقط عن أصحاب النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قيام الليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r2.claim: Maqātil says to recite in prayer as much Qurʾān as is easy, without setting a fixed amount.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the instruction as referring to the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r3.anchor: قال الحسن: يعني في صلاة المغرب والعشاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r4.speaker: عائشة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha says night prayer became voluntary after previously being obligatory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r4.anchor: وقالت عائشة (رضي الله عنها) (¬6) في هذه الآية: صار قيام الليل تطوعا بعد أن كان فرضا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r5.speaker: الحسن والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Suddī explain the easy recitation as one hundred verses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r5.anchor: وروي عن الحسن (¬1) (والسدي (¬2)) (¬3) في تفسير: {ما تيسر من القرآن} أنه مائة آية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r6.claim: The sick are excused because they cannot manage night prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r6.anchor: ثم عذرهم، وذكر عذرهم، فقال: {علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى} يعني فلا يطيقون قيام الليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r7.claim: Travelers seeking God’s bounty are traders seeking provision and are excused because they cannot manage night prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r7.anchor: يعني المسافرين للتجارة يطلبون من رزق الله، فلا يطيقون قيام الليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r8.claim: Those fighting in God’s path are mujahids excused because they cannot manage night prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p386/r8.anchor: يعني المجاهدين لا يطيقون قيام الليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r1.claim: The pronoun in minhu refers to the Qurʾān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r1.anchor: فاقرءوا ما تيسر} (¬5) عليكم. {منه} أي من القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says believers were permitted to pray as much as was manageable, without a fixed duration or amount; this early permission was later abrogated by the five daily prayers, as exegetes also say.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r2.anchor: وقال (عبد الله بن مسلم) (¬6) بن قتيبة: رخص لهم أن يقوموا ما أمكن وخف لغير مدة معلومة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r3.claim: Maqātil says to perform the prayers at their proper times; night prayer was lifted from the believers but remained obligatory for the Prophet alone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r3.anchor: وقوله: {وأقيموا الصلاة}. قال مقاتل: يعني وأتموها لوقتها، فنسخ قيام الليل عن المؤمنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these are obligations in their proper places and at their proper times.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في قوله: {وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة} يريد هذه فريضة عليكم في محلها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the good loan as voluntary giving beyond zakat, including maintaining kinship and hosting guests.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r5.anchor: {وأقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا}. قال ابن عباس: يريد سوى الزكاة من صلة الرحم، وقرى الضيف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r6.claim: Maqātil identifies the good loan as zakat given willingly and cheerfully.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p387/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني الزكاة (¬7) يعطيها طيبة بها نفسه، وهو معنى قوله: (حسنا) (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r1.claim: Good deeds advanced for oneself include obligatory or voluntary charity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r1.anchor: يعني من صدقة فريضة كانت أو تطوع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r2.claim: One finds its reward in the afterlife, better than what one gave.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r2.anchor: تجدوا ثوابه في الآخرة أفضل مما أعطيتم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the reward is better and greater than what a person postpones until bequeathing it at death; al-Wāḥidī explicitly prefers this explanation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: تجدوه عند الله هو خيرا وأعظم أجرا من الذي تؤخر إلى وصيتك عند الموت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains the advance as any act of obedience, which is better with God than worldly enjoyment; al-Wāḥidī favors Ibn ʿAbbās’s explanation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من طاعة تجدوه خيرا عند الله لكم من متاع الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r5.claim: The command is to seek God’s forgiveness for sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r5.anchor: أي: لذنوبكم، إن الله غفور الذنوب للمؤمنين، رحيم بهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r6.claim: Maqātil says God forgives the believers’ sins and is merciful to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r6.anchor: إن الله غفور الذنوب للمؤمنين، رحيم بهم. (قاله مقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God is forgiving and merciful to one who does not persist in sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p388/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: غفور رحيم لمن لم يصر على ذنب

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494#9/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494#9/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494#9/r1.claim: Lan tuḥṣūhu means that you will not be able to manage or endure it.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r4.claim: God knows that Muhammad prays and recites for less than two thirds of the night, and also for half and one third of it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r4.anchor: إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم } للصلاة والقراءة { أدنى } أقل { من ثلثي الليل ونصفه وثلثه } أي: وتقوم نصفه وثلثه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r5.claim: God measures the night and day and knows the lengths of their periods.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r5.anchor: وطائفة من الذين معك، والله يقدر الليل والنهار } فيعلم مقادير أوقاتهما

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r6.claim: Knowing people could not sustain the night vigil, God relented by lightening it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r6.anchor: علم أن لن تحصوه } لن تطيقوا قيام الليل { فتاب عليكم } رجع لكم إلى التخفيف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r7.claim: They are permitted to pray and recite whatever is possible and easy, without a fixed amount of recitation or duration.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r7.anchor: فاقرؤوا ما تيسر من القرآن } رخص لهم أن يقوموا، فيقرؤوا ما أمكن وخف بغير مقدار معلوم من القراءة والمدة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r8.claim: God lightened the night vigil because illness, travel for trade, and fighting in God's path made it burdensome.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r8.anchor: علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى } فيثقل عليهم قيام الليل، وكذلك المسافرون للتجارة والجهاد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r9.claim: Those traveling through the land are seeking God's bounty through trade.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r9.anchor: وآخرون يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r10.claim: Others are fighting in God's path.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r10.anchor: وآخرون يقاتلون في سبيل الله } يريد: أنه خفف قيام الليل لما علم من ثقله على هؤلاء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r11.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r11.claim: The commentators say this easing occurred in early Islam and was later abrogated by the five daily prayers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r11.anchor: قال المفسرون: وكان هذا في صدر الإسلام، ثم نسخ بالصلوات الخمس

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r12.claim: Any good deeds sent ahead will be found with God as better and greater in reward than what was left behind.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r12.anchor: وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله هو خيرا وأعظم أجرا } مما خلفتم وتركتم.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r13.claim: Ask God's forgiveness; He forgives believers' sins and is merciful to them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:18-20/r13.anchor: واستغفروا الله إن الله غفور } [لذنوب المؤمنين { رحيم } بهم].

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r5.claim: After the command was revealed, the Prophet and a group of believers prayed at night and held themselves to measured portions until the practice became difficult.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r5.anchor: فلما نزل هذه الآية قام رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، وطائفة من المؤمنين معه، أدنى من ثلثي الليل ونصفه وثلثه، وأخذ المسلمون أنفسهم بالقيام على المقادير حتى شق ذلك عليهم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r6.claim: God knows they cannot calculate the night’s portions or sustain the prescribed vigil, so relents and permits whatever night prayer is feasible without a fixed duration.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r6.anchor: والله يقدر الليل والنهار فيعلم مقدار ثلثيه ونصفه وثلثه، وسائر أجزائه ومواقيته، ويعلم أنكم أن لن تحصوه أي: لن تطيقوا معرفة حقائق ذلك والقيام فيه فتاب عليكم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r7.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r7.claim: The exegetes say the night-vigil requirement belonged to early Islam and was later abrogated by the five daily prayers.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p214/r7.anchor: وكان هذا في صدر الإسلام، ثم نسخ بالصلوات الخمس. كذلك قال المفسرون:

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r1.speaker: رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r1.claim: The Prophet said the Qurʾan was revealed in seven aḥruf, each wholesome and sufficient, and instructed believers to recite as they wished.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r1.anchor: بقول النبي، صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: «نزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف، كلها شاف كاف، فاقرؤوا كيف شئتم»

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r2.claim: Some wrongly interpret the seven aḥruf as promise, warning, lawful, unlawful, exhortations, parables, and argument.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r2.anchor: وقد غلط في تأويل هذا الحديث قوم فقالوا: السبعة الأحرف: وعد، ووعيد، وحلال، وحرام، ومواعظ، وأمثال، واحتجاج.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r3.speaker: آخرون
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r3.claim: Others wrongly say the seven aḥruf are seven dialects within a single word.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي سبع لغات في الكلمة.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r4.claim: Another group wrongly defines them as lawful and unlawful, commands and prohibitions, reports of past and future events, and parables.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r4.anchor: وقال قوم: حلال، وحرام، وأمر، ونهي، وخبر ما كان قبل، وخبر ما هو كائن بعد، وأمثال.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r5.claim: Saying that someone recites in the aḥruf of Abu ʿAmr or ʿĀṣim does not mean any of those proposed categories.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r5.anchor: ومن قال: فلان يقرأ بحرف أبي عمرو أو بحرف عاصم فإنه لا يريد شيئا مما ذكروا.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r6.claim: As far as the author knows, no Qurʾanic word can validly be recited in seven distinct ways.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r6.anchor: وليس يوجد في كتاب الله حرف قرىء على سبعة أوجه- يصح، فيما أعلم.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r7.claim: He instead understands the seven aḥruf as seven linguistic forms distributed across the Qurʾan, supported by the Prophet’s instruction to recite what is easy.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r7.anchor: وإنما تأويل قوله، صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r8.speaker: عمر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r8.claim: ʿUmar reports that the Prophet approved both his and Hisham ibn Ḥakīm’s differing recitations of Sūrat al-Furqān as revealed, then repeated the seven-aḥruf instruction.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r8.anchor: وقال عمر: سمعت هشام بن حكيم بن حزام يقرأ سورة الفرقان على غير ما أقرؤها، وقد كان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أقرأنيها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r9.claim: Reciting the readings of ʿAbd Allāh, Ubayy, or Zayd counts as reciting in that reader’s ḥarf.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r9.anchor: فمن قرأه قراءة عبد الله فقد قرأ بحرفه، ومن قرأ قراءة أبي فقد قرأ بحرفه، ومن قرأ قراءة زيد فقد قرأ بحرفه.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r10.claim: Ḥarf can mean a detached alphabetic letter, one word, an entire utterance, a sermon, or a complete poem; Arabic speakers call a poet’s whole poem his “word.”
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p29/r10.anchor: والحرف يقع على المثال المقطوع من حروف المعجم، وعلى الكلمة الواحدة، ويقع الحرف على الكلمة بأسرها، والخطبة كلها، والقصيدة بكمالها.

MAJAZ:v2p274/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p274/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p274/r2.claim: The phrase is equivalent to ‘you will find it with God as good’; the word huwa can be omitted.
MAJAZ:v2p274/r2.anchor: «تجدوه عند الله هو خيرا» (20) تجدوه عند الله خيرا.

ELMALILI:73:20/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20/r1.claim: There is agreement that this verse came later than the opening night-vigil command and softened or adjusted it; scholars differ about whether it was revealed in Mecca or Medina and how the easing or abrogation worked.
ELMALILI:73:20/r1.anchor: bu âyetin sonradan nâzil olup sûrenin evvelindeki kıyâm-ı leyl emrini tahfif ve ta‘dîl etmiş olduğunda ittifak vardır. Ancak yine Mekke’de mi yoksa sonradan Medine’de mi nâzil olduğunda

ELMALILI:73:20/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r2.speaker: عائشة
ELMALILI:73:20/r2.claim: A report from Aisha says the verse came eight months after the opening command, restored the originally near-obligatory night vigil to its basic prescribed amount, abrogated the extra burden, and left the excess voluntary.
ELMALILI:73:20/r2.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe’den bu âyetin يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُزَّمِّلُ قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ’den sekiz ay sonra nâzil olup baştan farîza gibi yazılmış olan kıyâm-ı leyli

ELMALILI:73:20/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:73:20/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the original vigil was very burdensome and believers kept it like their Ramadan vigil; God then eased it through the clause commanding them to recite what was manageable, graciously widening rather than narrowing the duty, about a year later.
ELMALILI:73:20/r3.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan da: “Müzzemmil’in evvelindeki إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا

ELMALILI:73:20/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r4.speaker: قتادة
ELMALILI:73:20/r4.claim: Qatada says the believers kept night vigil for one or two years after the opening command, until their feet and legs swelled; the command to recite what was easy then brought them relief.
ELMALILI:73:20/r4.anchor: Katâde’den: “يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُزَّمِّلُ nâzil oldu, bir sene veya iki sene kıyam ettiler

ELMALILI:73:20/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r5.speaker: الحسن
ELMALILI:73:20/r5.claim: Hasan reports that Muslims kept night vigil for a year, with some able to do so and others unable, until the concession came; after an obligation, the vigil became voluntary worship.
ELMALILI:73:20/r5.anchor: Hasan’dan: “يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُزَّمِّلُ âyeti nâzil olunca müslimler

ELMALILI:73:20/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r6.speaker: سعيد
ELMALILI:73:20/r6.claim: Sa‘id reports that the Prophet and a group of companions continued the commanded vigil for ten years, until this passage was revealed and lightened the duty.
ELMALILI:73:20/r6.anchor: Abd b. Humeyd’in, Ya‘kūb, Ca‘fer tarîkiyle[^10] Sa‘îd’den rivayetinde

ELMALILI:73:20/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ELMALILI:73:20/r7.claim: Some scholars call the verse Medinan; Abu Hayyan describes that as the majority position, but Elmalılı says it does not appear to be the majority view.

ELMALILI:73:20/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20/r8.claim: The Medinan dating is sometimes inferred from the zakat command; Elmalılı replies that Medina fixed zakat’s recipients and shares, not zakat’s basic obligation, since Meccan sūras also mention it.
ELMALILI:73:20/r8.anchor: Medine’de farz kılınan asl-ı[^13] zekât olmayıp Sûre-i Berâe âyeti mûcebince masriflerin, nasiblerin tâyini

ELMALILI:73:20/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20/r9.claim: Elmalılı considers the mention of fighting a clearer sign that at least one or two clauses are Medinan: permission to fight was agreed to be Medinan, and even the prediction of fighters preparatorily signals that permission and its abrogating circumstances.
ELMALILI:73:20/r9.anchor: Bizim kanaatimizce bu âyetin Medenî [5439] olduğunu andıran bir karîne daha vardır; وَءَاخَرُونَ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ fıkrasıdır.

ELMALILI:73:20/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20/r10.claim: Because no other Meccan verse explicitly mentions fighting, this clue seems clearer than zakat; Elmalılı concludes that at least some sentences of the verse must be Medinan, even if not the whole verse.
ELMALILI:73:20/r10.anchor: buradan başka Mekkî bir âyette kıtalden sarâhaten bahsedilmemiş bulunmasına nazaran bunun Medenî olması bize zekât fıkrasından daha vâzıh görünüyor

ELMALILI:73:20/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r11.speaker: author
