ELMALILI:73:20/r11.claim: The verse reduces the severity and amount of the opening night-vigil duty; after the five daily prayers became obligatory, evening and night prayers remained within the night vigil, while tahajjud changed from obligatory to recommended.
ELMALILI:73:20/r11.anchor: bu âyet sûrenin başındaki gece kıyâmı emrinin şiddetini, mikdârını tahfif etmiş, beş vakit namaz farz kılındıktan sonra akşam, yatsı gece kıyâmı cümlesinden kalarak teheccüdün[^14] vücûbu nedbe tehavvül eylemiştir.

ELMALILI:73:20/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20/r12.claim: The reported vigil durations indicate a maximum slightly under two thirds of the night, a middle amount of one half, and a minimum of one third.
ELMALILI:73:20/r12.anchor: demek ki a‘zamî kıyam müddeti sülüsândan biraz eksik (اَوْ زِدْ), vasatîsi nısf[^15], asgarîsi (اَوِ انْقُصْ) sülüs[^16] oluyordu.

ELMALILI:73:20/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20/r13.claim: In the reading under discussion, wa-nisfahu and wa-thuluthahu are accusative and coordinated with adna.
ELMALILI:73:20/r13.anchor: Bu kıraatte وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ mansub olarak أَدْنَىٰ üzerine ma‘tuftur.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r1.claim: Ednâ means nearer or less; here it describes the amount of night vigil as less than the stated fractions.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r2.speaker: Nâfi‘, Ebû Amr, İbn Âmir, Ebû Ca‘fer, Ya‘kūb
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r2.claim: These readers construe the fractions in genitive coordination with two-thirds, yielding: less than two-thirds, half, and one-third of the night.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r2.anchor: Nâfi‘, Ebû Amr, İbn Âmir, Ebû Ca‘fer, Ya‘kūb kıraatlerinde ise ثُلُثَىِ üzerine atıf ile mecrur okunur.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r3.claim: On this construction the maximum is below two-thirds, the middle amount below half, and the minimum below one-third, about a quarter.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r3.anchor: vasatîsi nısıftan az sülüs, asgarîsi de [5440] sülüsten az, rubu‘miktarıdır.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r4.claim: For a twelve-hour night, he estimates the least vigil at three or four hours, the middle at four or five, and the greatest at six or seven.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r4.anchor: Şu hâlde on iki saatlik bir gecede ekalli üç veya dört saat, ortası dört veya beş saat, en fazlası da altı veya yedi saat kalkılıyormuş demek olur.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r5.claim: The Prophet rose, along with a group of his Companions; this shows that not everyone rose, either because the duty was not obligatory for all or because some could not endure it.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r5.anchor: Sen de kalkıyorsun seninle beraber olanlardan bir tâife de yani ashabından bir cemaat de kalkıyor

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r6.claim: God alone measures and knows the true amount of night and day, and knows all time.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r6.anchor: -İkisinin de hakīkī mikdârını ancak[^18] O biçer ve O bilir ve O bütün zamanı bilir.-

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r7.claim: One sense of not being able to calculate it is that people cannot precisely tally every night's hours and fractions, since day and night vary and sleep prevents discernment.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r7.anchor: Bunda iki mâna vardır. Birisi her gecenin saatlerini bütün küsûrâtıyla ale’s-seviyye ve tamamen sayacak vechile takdir edemezsiniz.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r8.claim: Because this exact vigil is beyond everyone, even those able to keep it, such as the Prophet and some Companions, suffer by adding extra time as a precaution.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r8.anchor: sen ve bazı ashabın gibi yapacak olanlarınız da ihtiyat olmak için fazlasını tutarak zahmetler, meşakkatler çekersiniz.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r9.claim: The interpretation that the pronoun refers to God's measure of the night, adopted by al-Kashshāf and many others, is sound in itself, but can wrongly suggest the initial command was ill-judged.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r9.anchor: ve birçoklarının ihtiyar ettiği bu mâna haddizâtında doğru olmakla beraber

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r10.speaker: Taberî
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r10.claim: Al-Tabari refers the pronoun to the night vigil itself: in the future, none of you will manage to complete it fully; the author finds this simpler and smoother.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r11.claim: God eternally knew that believers could not all sustain the demanding vigil; the initial command was temporary preparation for the future, and the time had now come to ease it.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r11.anchor: ibtidâen sûrenin başında işaret edildiği vechile ilerisi için bir hazırlık mâhiyetinde olarak vermiş

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r12.claim: God turns again to them with grace and mercy, as He accepts the repentance of those who return to Him, and relieves the burden of the heavy vigil.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r12.anchor: Allah sizlere ilm ü lutfuyla yeniden nazar buyurdu tevbe ve salâh ile müracaat edenlere tevbelerinin kabûlüyle tekrar nazar ve merhamet buyurduğu gibi

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r13.claim: The easing does not abolish night vigil or recitation: rise and recite whatever is easy, without a fixed fraction of the night or a requirement of prolonged, measured recitation.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r13.anchor: asl-ı kıyam emri nesholunmuyor; yine kalkın, fakat nısfı veya daha azı veya daha çoğu mikdarlarıyla ve uzun uzadıya tertil kaydıyla mukayyed olmayarak

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r14.speaker: Müfessirînden birçokları
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r14.claim: Many exegetes take recitation as a part-for-whole reference to prayer, since recitation is one of its pillars, and understand the command as praying at night as much as is easy.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r14.anchor: Kıraat namazın erkânından olduğu için cüz zikrolunup kül murad olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r15.speaker: Bir kısım müfessirîn
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r15.claim: Some say this meant the evening and night prayers, with the obligation of tahajjud lifted and left voluntary and discretionary.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r15.anchor: akşam ve yatsı namazları diyenler olmuş, teheccüdün vücûbu nesholunup tetavvu‘ve ihtiyâra bırakıldığını söyleyenler olmuştur

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r16.claim: If recitation is detached from prayer or vigil, it cannot ease the hardship of the earlier night-vigil command; at most it would address the command to recite with measured cadence, contrary to the passage's relieving context.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r16.anchor: Fi’lvâki‘bu kıraatte namaz veya kıyam kaydı gözetilmediği surette قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا emrindeki zorluğun Kur’an’dan kolay geleni okumakla tahfif

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r17.claim: He preserves the literal sense of Qur'an as recitation while retaining prayer: the earlier command means rise for prayer, and here the easy Quranic portion is read within that prayer; the easing is conveyed by context.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r17.anchor: hem Kur’an ve kıraatin hakikat mânası muhafaza edilmek hem de namaz mânası gözetilmek için قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ’de قُمْ اِلَى الصَّلاَةِ takdîrinde

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r18.speaker: Diğer bir kısım müfessirîn
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r18.claim: Another group takes the imperative as ordinary Quran recitation, not night prayer, and says at least fifty verses should be read each night.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r18.anchor: Diğer bir kısım müfessirîn ise فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ gece namazla değil, aynen Kur’an kıraatiyle emirdir.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r19.claim: The imperative's apparent force remains obligation: night vigil and recitation are still obligatory, but need not be performed at an uncountable length and may be as much as is easy.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r19.anchor: emrin zâhiri yine vücub içindir. Yani gece kıyam ve kıraat yine farz, ancak evvelki gibi ihsâ edilemeyecek vechile çok olmak şart değil

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r20.claim: If this first command means prayer, its obligation too is abrogated by the later recitation and establish-prayer commands.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r20.anchor: bunun da neshi ikinci فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ ve وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ emirleriyle vâki‘olmuş olur

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r21.claim: If it means Quran recitation alone, then some Quran must be recited every night, whether during prayer or outside it.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r21.anchor: her gece biraz Kur’an okumak bu vechile farz olmuş olur

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r22.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r22.claim: Some exegetes take the command as recommendation or permission because the wording delegates the amount to what is easy; Abu Hayyan calls this the majority position.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r22.anchor: kāil olmuşlardır[^27] ki Ebû Hayyân buna cumhur kavli demiştir.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r23.claim: Taken absolutely, the easy amount cannot be fixed, since what is bearable without fatigue varies with each person and circumstance.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r23.anchor: hâlin ihtilâfına göre fark edebileceğinden zâhirine nazaran tâyin olunamaz.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r24.speaker: Mutlak kıraat mânasına hamledenler
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r24.claim: Exegetes who take this as unrestricted recitation appeal to customary practice and the predecessors' habit to set a minimum of fifty verses.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r24.anchor: ve eslâfın itiyadına nazaran lâekal elli âyet olmalıdır demişlerdir.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r25.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r25.claim: One report from Abu Hanifa sets the minimum obligatory recitation in prayer at one short verse.

ELMALILI:73:20#2/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r26.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r26.claim: A second report from Abu Hanifa requires enough recitation for the name Quran to apply and for it not to resemble ordinary human speech.
ELMALILI:73:20#2/r26.anchor: 2. “Kur’an” ismi ıtlak olunacak ve bir insan hitâbına benzemeyecek kadar olmalıdır.

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r1.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r1.claim: A third report requires at least three short verses or one long verse; this is also the two disciples' position and the relied-upon fatwa.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r1.anchor: 3. Lâekal üç kısa âyet veya bir uzun âyet olmalıdır.

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r2.speaker: İmameyn
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r2.claim: The view requiring three short verses or one long verse is also held by the two disciples and is the position used for fatwa.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r2.anchor: Bu rivayet İmameyn’in de kavlidir, müftâ bih olan da budur.

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r3.speaker: İmam Mâlik ve Şâfiî
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r3.claim: Malik and al-Shafi‘i require at least al-Fatiha, citing the prophetic report that there is no prayer without the Opening of the Book.

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r4.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r4.claim: Abu Hanifa distinguishes wajib from fard: the hadith makes al-Fatiha wajib, while this verse makes unspecified Quran recitation fard; deliberate omission requires repeating the prayer, but accidental omission without prostration of forgetfulness does not require repeating it after the time has passed, though repetition is recommended.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r4.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam vâcib ile farzı fark ederek bu hadis ile namazda Fâtiha’nın vücûbu sâbit ise de

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r5.claim: By agreement, min in from the Quran is explanatory: the easy amount is a portion still validly called Quran, such as a sura or one or several verses.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r5.anchor: مِنَ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ’de يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ bi’l-ittifak beyâniyedir.

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r6.claim: God knew in advance that some believers would be ill, others travel seeking His bounty, and others fight in His way, making the demanding night vigil difficult or impossible.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r6.anchor: Allah ilm-i ezelîsinde bildi ki sizin içinizden hastalar olacak

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r7.claim: Mentioning traders seeking God's bounty beside fighters in His way signals that their rewards are close to one another.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r7.anchor: bunların ikisinin de ecirde birbirlerine yakın olduklarına işaret vardır.

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r8.speaker: Hazret-i Ömer
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r8.claim: Umar said that, after jihad, his most beloved death would come while seeking God's bounty between two mountain branches, and he recited this verse.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r8.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer radıyallahu anh’tan rivayet etmişlerdir ki

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r9.speaker: Resûlullah (İbn Mes‘ûd rivayeti)
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r9.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says the Prophet promised a station with God to anyone who brings food to a Muslim town and sells it at that day's price; he then recited these verses.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r9.anchor: İbn Merdûye’nin İbn Mes‘ûd’dan rivayet ettiği bir hadiste de Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem: “Her kim Müslüman beldelerinden birine bir taâm celbeder

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r10.claim: Given the many legitimate needs that prevent night vigil, believers are told to recite whatever is easy from the Quran.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r10.anchor: Hâsılı bunlar ve bunlar gibi gözetilmeleri ve çalışmaları lâzım gelen birtakım mazeret ashabı[^34]

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r11.claim: The commands require performing the obligatory prayers at their appointed times and paying zakat.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r11.anchor: sade farz olan vakit namazını kılın ve zekâtı verin

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r12.claim: Lend God a goodly loan means spend for good causes with sincere intention, as though lending in order to receive the reward later.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r12.anchor: ileride sevâbını almak üzere hüsn-i niyet ve ihlâs ile ödünç verir gibi hayr yolunda infâkātta bulunun

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r13.claim: Whatever good people send ahead for themselves, they will find with God as good and with a still greater reward.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r13.anchor: Ve çünkü nefisleriniz için her ne hayr takdim ederseniz Allah yanında onu hayr

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r14.claim: Believers should seek God's forgiveness in all circumstances because He is forgiving and merciful and grants the supplicant success through His mercy.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r14.anchor: Hem de Allah’a istiğfar ederek bütün ahvâlinizde mağfiretini isteyin

ELMALILI:73:20#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r15.claim: The closing supplication asks God to forgive and show mercy to the author and the believers who preceded them in faith, by the sanctity of what He revealed to His Messenger.
ELMALILI:73:20#3/r15.anchor: اَللّٰهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا وَلْإِِخْوَانِنَا الَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِالْإِْيمَانِ

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r6.claim: Verse 20 later describes practice as close to two-thirds of the night, half of it, or a third.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:1/r6.anchor: İleride, 20. âyette ise bu sürenin, üçte ikisine yakın, yarısı, üçte biri olarak uygulandığı bildirilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r1.claim: The initial requirement to rise during a set part of the night became difficult in practice, so the obligation was eased; alternatively, the command was encouragement rather than a strict requirement to observe a set time and pray.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r1.anchor: Uygulamada hem gece namaza kalkma hem de istenen vakti tesbit etme hususunda zorluk ortaya çıkınca

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r2.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r2.claim: Some hold that night prayer was initially obligatory for both the Prophet and the community, then became voluntary for the community while remaining obligatory for the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r2.anchor: Gece namazının başlangıçta hem Hz. Peygamber’e hem de ümmete farz kılındığını, daha sonra halkın zorlandığı ortaya çıkınca onlar için nâfile, Hz. Peygamber için farz haline getirildiği görüşünde olanlar da vardır (Şevkânî, V, 371-372).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r3.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r3.claim: One interpretation takes “recite what is easy” to mean praying as much tahajjud as is easy during the night.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r3.anchor: a) Geceleri kolayınıza gelen miktarda teheccüt namazı kılın

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r4.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r4.claim: A second interpretation takes it to mean reciting as much of the Qur'an, and whichever verses, as are easy during night prayer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r4.anchor: b) Gece namazında Kur’an’dan kolayınıza gelen miktarda okuyun (bk. Şevkânî, V, 371-372; İbn Âşûr, XXIX, 283-284).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r5.speaker: Ebû Bekir İbnü’l-Arabi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reports both that “recitation” stands for prayer and that the passage means recitation itself.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r5.anchor: Ebû Bekir İbnü’l-Arabi bu âyet hakkında şu yorumların yapıldığını söyler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r6.claim: Illness, travel for livelihood or other purposes, and jihad for defense, freedom, or independence bring divine ease; night prayer becomes recommended rather than obligatory.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r6.anchor: hastalıktan, geçim temini için veya başka maksatlarla yapılan yolculuklardan; vatan savunması, özgürlük, bağımsızlık vb. yüce amaçlarla cihadda bulunmak gibi mazeretlerden dolayı Allah Teâlâ kullarına kolaylık lutfetmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r7.claim: The closing section commands proper prayer, zakat, good works, charity, and compassionate help for the poor, promising multiplied reward with God in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r7.anchor: namazlarını usul ve âdâbına uygun olarak kılmalarını, zekâtlarını vermelerini, Allah rızâsı için hayır yapmalarını, iyilikte bulunmalarını, fakirlere karşı şefkat ve merhametle davranıp onlara yardım etmelerini buyurmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r8.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r8.claim: Commentators usually identify the prayer here as the five daily prayers and zakat as obligatory alms; the authors reject that dating because both formal duties became obligatory years later.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r8.anchor: Müfessirler genellikle burada geçen, “Namazı kılın, zekâtı verin” cümlesindeki namazı beş vakit namaz, zekâtı da farz olan zekât olarak yorumlamışlarsa da sûrenin tamamının Mekke döneminde inen ilk sûrelerden olduğunu dikkate alırsak bu yoruma katılmak mümkün değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r9.claim: Instead, the verse aims to cultivate awareness of the duties of prayer and zakat and begin their earliest practices.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r9.anchor: Buna göre âyette, İslâm’ın beş temel şartından ikisini teşkil eden namaz ve zekât ibadetlerine ilişkin yükümlülük bilincini oluşturmanın ve bunların ilk uygulamalarını başlatmanın amaçlandığı söylenebilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r10.claim: Since people cannot avoid mistakes despite their care in worldly life, the sūra ends by commanding them to ask God's forgiveness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:20/r10.anchor: Kullar dünya hayatında ne kadar dikkat ederlerse etsinler hatadan kurtulamayacakları için sûrenin son cümlesinde Allah’tan bağışlanma istemeleri emredilmiştir.

BAQILLANI:v1p204/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r1.claim: The examples demonstrate a general method: every sūra, including those not discussed, equally proves inimitability, though the proof is more evident in some passages and subtler in others.
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r1.anchor: في الدلالة على الإعجاز والكفاية في التمنع والبرهان

BAQILLANI:v1p204/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r2.claim: Qur’anic signs fall into two classes: a self-contained verse or verse-ending that shines in discourse, and a phrase of several words whose individual words each reach the utmost eloquence.
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r2.anchor: قد اعتمدنا على أن الآيات تنقسم إلى قسمين أحدهما ما يتم بنفسه أو بنفسه وفاصلته

BAQILLANI:v1p204/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r3.claim: A Qur’anic word remains unmistakably superior when embedded in a long speech; joined to its peers, the words become a necklace of jewels, while each alone resembles a scattered gem.
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r3.anchor: فإذا ضمت إلى أخواتها وجاءت في ذواتها أرتك القلائد منظومة

BAQILLANI:v1p204/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r4.claim: He avoids inserting Qur’anic wording into poetry, but says its distinct beauty would stand out even to someone unfamiliar with the Qur’an, who would recognize it as foreign to the surrounding speech.
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r4.anchor: ولولا ما أكره من تضمين القرآن في الشعر لأنشدتك ألفاظا وقعت مضمنة لتعلم كيف تلوح عليه

BAQILLANI:v1p204/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r5.claim: Qur’anic phrases combine eloquence, invention, fluency, rarity, and a distinctive style and ordering.
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r5.anchor: ثم تناسبها في البلاغة والإبداع وتماثلها في السلاسة والإغراب ثم انفرادها بذلك الأسلوب

BAQILLANI:v1p204/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r6.claim: Other speech becomes uneven as it ranges through meanings and subjects, narrowing its options and exposing effortful artifice.
BAQILLANI:v1p204/r6.anchor: وأنت ترى غيره من الكلام يضطرب في مجاريه ويختل تصرفه في معانيه ويتفاوت التفاوت الكثير

BURHAN:v1p265/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p265/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p265/r1.claim: Earlier scriptures lacked the Qur'an's miraculous arrangement and were not made easy to memorize, unlike the reasons offered for its division into sūras.
BURHAN:v1p265/r1.anchor: فإن قلت فهلا كانت الكتب السالفة كذلك قلت لوجهين أحدهما أنها لم تكن معجزات من ناحية النظم والترتيب والآخر أنها لم تيسر للحفظ

BURHAN:v1p265/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p265/r2.speaker: الزمخشرى
BURHAN:v1p265/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī notes that earlier scriptures too were revealed in sūras, and that authors divide books into titled chapters.
BURHAN:v1p265/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشرى الفوائد فى تفصيل القرآن وتقطيعه سورا كثيرة وكذلك أنزل الله التوراة والإنجيل والزبور

BURHAN:v1p265/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p265/r3.speaker: الزمخشرى
BURHAN:v1p265/r3.claim: Dividing a broad subject into types and classes is more impressive and grand than presenting it as one undivided chapter.
BURHAN:v1p265/r3.anchor: أن الجنس إذا انطوت تحته أنواع وأصناف كان أحسن وأفخم من أن يكون بابا واحدا

BURHAN:v1p265/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p265/r4.speaker: الزمخشرى
BURHAN:v1p265/r4.claim: Finishing a sūra or chapter renews a reader's energy, like reaching a milestone on a journey; this also motivates dividing the Qur'an into parts and fifths.
BURHAN:v1p265/r4.anchor: ومنها أن القارىء إذا ختم سورة أو بابا من الكتاب ثم أخذ فى آخره كان أنشط له وأبعث على التحصيل

BURHAN:v1p265/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p265/r5.speaker: أنس
BURHAN:v1p265/r5.claim: Anas reports that a man who recited al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān was held in high regard among them.
BURHAN:v1p265/r5.anchor: ومنه حديث أنس كان الرجل إذا قرأ البقرة وآل عمران جل فينا

BURHAN:v1p265/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p265/r6.speaker: الزمخشرى
BURHAN:v1p265/r6.claim: Mastering a sūra makes a memorizer feel he has acquired an independent portion of God's book, magnifying what he learned; hence sūra recitation in prayer is preferable.
BURHAN:v1p265/r6.anchor: ومنها أن الحافظ إذا حذق السورة اعتقد أنه أخذ من كتاب الله طائفة مستقلة فيعظم عنده ما حفظه ومنه حديث أنس

BURHAN:v1p265/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p265/r7.speaker: الزمخشرى
BURHAN:v1p265/r7.claim: Division brings similar forms and counterparts together, allowing meanings and composition to be noticed in relation to one another.
BURHAN:v1p265/r7.anchor: ومنها أن التفصيل يسبب تلاحق الأشكال والنظائر وملاءمة بعضها لبعض وبذلك تتلاحظ المعانى والنظم

BURHAN:v1p379/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p379/r1.speaker: أحمد
BURHAN:v1p379/r1.claim: Aḥmad forbids departing from the ʿUthmānic codex's orthography, whether in a yāʾ, wāw, alif, or any other letter.
BURHAN:v1p379/r1.anchor: وقال الإمام أحمد رحمه الله تحرم مخالفة خط مصحف عثمان فى ياء أو واو أو ألف أو غير ذلك

BURHAN:v1p379/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p379/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p379/r2.claim: The strict preservation rule belonged to the early period, when knowledge of the script was fresh; today, deviation risks confusing readers.
BURHAN:v1p379/r2.anchor: وكان هذا فى الصدر الأول والعلم حى غض وأما الأن فقد يخشى الإلباس

BURHAN:v1p379/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p379/r3.speaker: عز الدين بن عبد السلام
BURHAN:v1p379/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salām says the Qur'an should no longer be written in the early orthography, lest ignorant readers alter it.
BURHAN:v1p379/r3.anchor: ولهذا قال الشيخ عز الدين بن عبد السلام لا تجوز كتابة المصحف الآن على الرسوم الأولى باصطلاح الأئمة لئلا يوقع فى تغيير من الجهال

BURHAN:v1p379/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p379/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p379/r4.claim: The author rejects applying that ban absolutely: abandoning an old practice because of ignorant people could cause knowledge to disappear.
BURHAN:v1p379/r4.anchor: ولكن لا ينبغى إجراء هذا على إطلاقه لئلا يؤدى إلى دروس العلم وشىء أحكمته القدماء لا يترك مراعاته لجهل الجاهلين

BURHAN:v1p379/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p379/r5.speaker: البيهقى
BURHAN:v1p379/r5.claim: Al-Bayhaqī urges preserving the letters used in early codices, whose writers were more learned, sincere, and trustworthy, and cautions against presuming to correct them.
BURHAN:v1p379/r5.anchor: وقد قال البيهقى فى شعب الإيمان

BURHAN:v1p379/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p379/r6.speaker: زيد
BURHAN:v1p379/r6.claim: Zayd says that recitation is a sunna.
BURHAN:v1p379/r6.anchor: وروى بسنده عن زيد قال القراءة سنة

BURHAN:v1p379/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p379/r7.speaker: سليمان بن داود الهاشمى
BURHAN:v1p379/r7.claim: Sulaymān explains the report as a warning not to oppose the community through one's own opinion in matters of following precedent.
BURHAN:v1p379/r7.anchor: قال سليمان بن داود الهاشمى يعنى ألا تخالف الناس برأيك فى الاتباع

BURHAN:v1p379/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p379/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد
BURHAN:v1p379/r8.claim: A similar explanation of Zayd's statement is attributed to Abū ʿUbayd.
BURHAN:v1p379/r8.anchor: وبمعناه بلغنى عن أبى عبيد فى تفسير ذلك

BURHAN:v1p379/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p379/r9.speaker: القراء
BURHAN:v1p379/r9.claim: Readers do not follow Arabic grammar in recitation when it conflicts with the codex's written form.
BURHAN:v1p379/r9.anchor: وترى القراء لم يلتفوا إلى مذهب العربية فى القراءة إذا خالف ذلك خط المصحف

BURHAN:v1p379/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p379/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p379/r10.claim: The author treats adherence to the codex's letters as an established sunna that no one may transgress.
BURHAN:v1p379/r10.anchor: واتباع حروف المصاحف عندنا كالسنن القائمة التى لا يجوز لأحد أن يتعداها

BURHAN:v1p192/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p192/r1.speaker: أبو القاسم الحسن بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابورى
BURHAN:v1p192/r1.claim: Al-Naysābūrī calls knowledge of revelation's settings and sequence among the noblest Qur'anic sciences, including early, middle, and late Meccan and Medinan revelation.
BURHAN:v1p192/r1.anchor: قال أبو القاسم الحسن بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابورى فى كتاب التنبيه على فضل علوم القرآن من أشرف علوم القرآن علم نزوله وجهاته

BURHAN:v1p192/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p192/r2.speaker: أبو القاسم الحسن بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابورى
BURHAN:v1p192/r2.claim: He distinguishes Meccan passages with Medinan rulings and the reverse, revelations addressed to the other community, and passages resembling the opposite revelation context.
BURHAN:v1p192/r2.anchor: قال أبو القاسم الحسن بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابورى فى كتاب التنبيه

BURHAN:v1p192/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p192/r3.speaker: أبو القاسم الحسن بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابورى
BURHAN:v1p192/r3.claim: His catalogue also classifies revelations by named location, night or day, accompanied or separately, and Meccan or Medinan verses embedded in sūras of the other kind.
BURHAN:v1p192/r3.anchor: قال أبو القاسم الحسن بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابورى فى كتاب التنبيه

BURHAN:v1p192/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p192/r4.speaker: أبو القاسم الحسن بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابورى
BURHAN:v1p192/r4.claim: He includes material carried between Mecca, Medina, and Abyssinia, revelation given in summary, explanation, or coded form, and disputed classifications.
BURHAN:v1p192/r4.anchor: قال أبو القاسم الحسن بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابورى فى كتاب التنبيه

BURHAN:v1p192/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p192/r5.speaker: أبو القاسم الحسن بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابورى
BURHAN:v1p192/r5.claim: He concludes that anyone unable to know and distinguish these twenty-five facets has no right to speak about God's Book.
BURHAN:v1p192/r5.anchor: قال أبو القاسم الحسن بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابورى فى كتاب التنبيه

ITQAN:v3p65/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p65/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p65/r2.claim: The end of Surat al-Muzzammil abrogated its opening night-prayer obligation, and the latter ruling was itself superseded by the obligation of the five prayers.
ITQAN:v3p65/r2.anchor: نعم يمثل له بأخر سورة المزمل فإنه ناسخ لأولها منسوخ بفرض الصلوات

ITQAN:v3p65/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p65/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p65/r8.claim: Al-Suyuti prefers the agreed Meccan example: the night prayer commanded at the start of al-Muzzammil was abrogated by its end or by the five daily prayers.
ITQAN:v3p65/r8.anchor: قلت أحسن من هذه نسخ قيام الليل في أول سورة المزمل بآخرها أو بإيجاب الصلوات الخمس وذلك بمكة اتفاقا

ITQAN:v1p122/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p122/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p122/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses received seven emerald tablets containing all things, then shattered them when he saw the Israelites worshipping the calf; God raised six-sevenths and one-seventh remained.
ITQAN:v1p122/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال أعطي موسى التوراة في سبعة ألواح من زبرجد فيها تبيان لكل شيء

ITQAN:v1p122/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p122/r2.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
ITQAN:v1p122/r2.claim: A report traced through Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, his father, and grandfather says Moses' tablets were made of lote trees from Paradise and measured twelve cubits long.
ITQAN:v1p122/r2.anchor: من طريق جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عن جده رفعه قال الألواح التي أنزلت على موسى كانت من سدر

ITQAN:v1p122/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p122/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p122/r3.claim: In the report of al-Futūn, Ibn ʿAbbās says Israel first resisted the obligations Moses brought, then accepted when the mountain loomed above them like a canopy.
ITQAN:v1p122/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في حديث الفتون قال أخذ موسى الألواح بعدما سكت عنه الغضب

ITQAN:v1p122/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p122/r4.speaker: ثابت بن الحجاج
ITQAN:v1p122/r4.claim: Thābit b. al-Ḥajjāj says the Torah came all at once; Israel initially refused it as burdensome and accepted only after God shaded them with the mountain.
ITQAN:v1p122/r4.anchor: عن ثابت بن الحجاج قال جاءتهم التوراة جملة واحدة فكبر عليهم

ITQAN:v1p122/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p122/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p122/r5.claim: The author calls reports about the Torah's one-time revelation sound and explicit; he infers that gradual Qur'anic revelation made acceptance easier than a single delivery of many duties and prohibitions.
ITQAN:v1p122/r5.anchor: فهذه آثار صحيحة صريحة في إنزال التوراة جملة ويؤخذ من الأثر الأخير منها حكمة أخرى لإنزال القرآن مفرقا

ITQAN:v1p122/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p122/r6.speaker: عائشة
ITQAN:v1p122/r6.claim: ʿĀʾisha says early revelation described Paradise and Hell; legal commands came after people embraced Islam, since early prohibitions of wine or adultery would have been rejected.
ITQAN:v1p122/r6.anchor: عن عائشة قالت إنما نزل أول ما نزل منه سورة من المفصل فيها ذكر الجنة والنار

ITQAN:v4p533#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p533#2/r1.speaker: النبي
ITQAN:v4p533#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet interpreted “recite what is easy of it” as one hundred verses; Ibn Kathīr calls the report very strange.
ITQAN:v4p533#2/r1.anchor: أخرج الطبراني عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم / فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه / قال ( مائة آية ) قال ابن كثير غريب جدا

ITQAN:v2p452#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p452#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p452#2/r1.claim: The form أن in “He knew that there would be” can be the lightened form of the emphatic particle, occurring after a verb of certainty or its equivalent.
ITQAN:v2p452#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ وحسبوا ألا تكون ﴾ في قراءة الرفع

ITQAN:v4p443/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p443/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p443/r1.claim: Ordinary Arabic spelling follows letter rules and pronunciation at starts and pauses, while the early Qur'anic codex sometimes departs from those rules.
ITQAN:v4p443/r1.anchor: القاعدة العربية أن اللفظ يكتب بحروف هجائية مع مراعاة الابتداء والوقوف عليه

ITQAN:v4p443/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p443/r2.speaker: مالك
ITQAN:v4p443/r2.claim: Malik rejects writing the Qur'an in newer orthography and requires retaining the original script; al-Dānī says no scholar opposed this view.
ITQAN:v4p443/r2.anchor: سئل مالك هل يكتب المصحف على ما أحدثه الناس من الهجاء فقال لا إلا على الكتبة الأولى

ITQAN:v4p443/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p443/r3.speaker: مالك
ITQAN:v4p443/r3.claim: Malik also rejects changing letters such as written alif and wāw in the Qur'anic codex.
ITQAN:v4p443/r3.anchor: سئل مالك عن الحروف في القرآن الواو والألف أترى أن يغير من المصحف إذا وجد فيه كذلك قال لا

ITQAN:v4p443/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p443/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
ITQAN:v4p443/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr explains that the extra written wāw and alif are absent in speech, as the wāw in أولوا.
ITQAN:v4p443/r4.anchor: أبو عمرو يعني الواو والألف والمزيدتين في الرسم

ITQAN:v4p443/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p443/r5.speaker: أحمد
ITQAN:v4p443/r5.claim: Aḥmad prohibits departing from the codex in any wāw, yāʾ, alif, or other letter.
ITQAN:v4p443/r5.anchor: وقال الإمام أحمد يحرم مخالفة مصحف الإمام في واو أو ياء أو ألف أو غير ذلك

ITQAN:v4p443/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p443/r6.speaker: البيهقي
ITQAN:v4p443/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqī says copyists must preserve the original orthography because its writers surpassed later people in knowledge, sincerity, and trustworthiness; one should not presume to correct them.
ITQAN:v4p443/r6.anchor: فإنهم كانوا أكثر علما وأصدق قلبا ولسانا وأعظم أمانة منا فلا ينبغي أن يظن بأنفسنا استدراكا عليهم

ITQAN:v4p443/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p443/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p443/r7.claim: The author organizes orthographic variants under deletion, addition, hamza, substitution, separation, and places where one of two readings was written.
ITQAN:v4p443/r7.anchor: وسنحصر أمر الرسم في الحذف والزيادة والهمز والبدل والفصل وما فيه قراءتان فكتب إحداهما

ITQAN:v1p34/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p34/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p34/r1.claim: Knowing whether a revelation is earlier or later helps identify abrogation or specification, according to scholars who allow later specification.
ITQAN:v1p34/r1.anchor: ومن فوائد معرفة ذلك العلم بالمتأخر فيكون ناسخا أو مخصصا على رأي من يرى تأخير المخصص

ITQAN:v1p34/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p34/r2.speaker: النيسابوري
ITQAN:v1p34/r2.claim: Al-Naysābūrī lists twenty-five dimensions of revelation history and classification, including place, time, audience, travel, and disputed Makkan or Medinan status; he says one who cannot distinguish them may not speak about God's Book.
ITQAN:v1p34/r2.anchor: فهذه خمسة وعشرون وجها من لم يعرفها ويميز بينها لم يحل له أن يتكلم في كتاب الله تعالى

ITQAN:v1p34/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p34/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v1p34/r3.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī classifies revelation as Makkan, Medinan, travel-related, settled, night, day, heavenly, earthly, between heaven and earth, or beneath the earth in a cave.
ITQAN:v1p34/r3.anchor: وقال ابن العربي في كتابه الناسخ والمنسوخ الذي علمناه على الجملة من القرآن أن منه مكيا ومدنيا وسفريا وحضريا وليليا ونهاريا

ITQAN:v1p34/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p34/r4.speaker: ابن النقيب
ITQAN:v1p34/r4.claim: Ibn al-Naqīb divides the Qur'an into Makkan, Medinan, mixed Makkan and Medinan, and neither Makkan nor Medinan passages.
ITQAN:v1p34/r4.anchor: وقال ابن النقيب في مقدمة تفسيره المنزل من القرآن على أربعة أقسام مكي ومدني وما بعضه مكي وبعضه مدني وما ليس بمكي ولا مدني

ITQAN:v1p34/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p34/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p34/r5.claim: The best-known convention defines Makkan as revealed before the Hijra and Medinan as revealed afterward, regardless of location; Yaḥyā b. Sallām likewise classifies revelation before reaching Medina during the Hijra as Makkan, and later travel revelations as Medinan.
ITQAN:v1p34/r5.anchor: أشهرها أن المكي ما نزل قبل الهجرة والمدني ما نزل بعدها سواء نزل بمكة أم بالمدينة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r1.claim: A simile or representation following an abstract meaning adorns it, raises its standing, strengthens it, and moves hearts toward it with affection.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r1.anchor: أن التمثيل إذا جاء في أعقاب المعانى أو برزت هي بإختصار في معرضه ونقلت عن صورها الأصلية إلى صورته

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r2.claim: Its force varies by genre: praise grows grander and more beloved, blame stings more, argument gains power, boasting gains reach, apology wins acceptance, and admonition moves its hearer.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r2.anchor: وان كان حجاجا كان برهانه أنور وسلطانه أقهر وبيانه أبهر وان كان افتخارا كان شأوه أبعد وشرفه أجد ولسانه ألد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r3.claim: Al-Buḥturī first describes a generous man as near to petitioners yet beyond rivals, then likens him to a lofty moon whose light is close to night travelers.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r3.anchor: كالبدر افرط في العلو وضوءه للعصبة السارين جد قريب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r4.claim: The reader should compare the meaning's effect after the first line with its transformed force after the simile in the second.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p92/r4.anchor: وفكر في حالك وحال المعنى معك وأنت في البيت الأول لم تنته إلى الثاني ولم تتدبر نصرته إياه وتمثيله له

BURHAN:v4p308/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p308/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p308/r7.claim: He explains أن سيكون منكم مرضى by treating the illness as continuing in sense, just as ما علم الله زيد يخرج can mean that Zayd will not leave as far as God knows.
BURHAN:v4p308/r7.anchor: فهو متأول للمرضى في المعنى كما إن النفي

BURHAN:v3p94/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p94/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p94/r5.claim: An inna-clause may provide the reason for the preceding command or statement, as in seeking forgiveness, praying for people, and disclaiming a blameless self.
BURHAN:v3p94/r5.anchor: وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم

ITQAN:v1p36/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p36/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p36/r9.claim: Al-Mulk, al-Qalam, al-Haqqa, al-Ma'arij, Nuh, and al-Jinn are Meccan; al-Muzzammil is excepted for two Medinan verses, while al-Muddaththir through its end is Meccan.
ITQAN:v1p36/r9.anchor: والملك ون والحاقة وسأل وسورة نوح والجن والمزمل إلا آيتين ﴿ إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم

DAMGHANI:v1p372/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p372/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p372/r2.claim: Yaqduru can mean to know; God knows the hours of night and day.
DAMGHANI:v1p372/r2.anchor: السادس يقدر أي يعلم قوله سبحانه في سورة المزمل والله يقدر الليل والنهار

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p400/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p400/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p400/r8.claim: Exegetes give ḍarb the sense of traveling in these verses about setting out in God’s cause or across the land.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p400/r8.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضرب في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r2.claim: Qiyām can mean ordinary standing upright.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r2.anchor: أحدها : القيام المعروف الذي هو انتصاب القامة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p270/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p270/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p270/r2.claim: الضرب can mean traveling or journeying.

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهنلايكنفصلاإلافيالفعلولاي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهنلايكنفصلاإلافيالفعلولاي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهنلايكنفصلاإلافيالفعلولاي.claim: The same separator analysis applies to هو خيرا وأعظم أجرا in the verse about good deeds presented to God.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهنلايكنفصلاإلافيالفعلولاي.anchor: وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله هو خيرا وأعظم أجرا
